```text
1	// Package sessionindex implements sessions.db — the machine-level index of every coding-agent
2	// session SpecStory knows about, across all projects and providers. It backs the
3	// `specstory resume` selection UX and is (re)built by `specstory reindex`.
4	//
5	// sessions.db is a DERIVED CACHE over the native session stores: it can be deleted and
6	// fully rebuilt at any time. See docs/SESSIONS-DB.md for the design and schema.
7	package sessionindex
8	
9	import (
10		"context"
11		"database/sql"
12		"errors"
13		"fmt"
14		"log/slog"
15		"os"
16		"path/filepath"
17		"sort"
18		"strings"
19	
20		_ "modernc.org/sqlite" // SQLite driver (pure Go), same as pkg/provenance
21	)
22	
23	// Connection-pool sizing. Writes (reindex) must serialize on a single connection to
24	// avoid SQLITE_BUSY/deadlocks. The interactive browse path (resume/search) only reads,
25	// so it opens several connections — WAL permits many concurrent readers, which keeps a
26	// single slow full-text query (a broad prefix can take seconds) from starving the UI.
27	const (
28		writerConns = 1
29		readerConns = 4
30	)
31	
32	// connectionPragmas are applied to EVERY pooled connection via the DSN rather than run once
33	// with db.Exec. synchronous/cache_size/temp_store/mmap_size are per-connection settings, and
34	// OpenReader uses several connections — a one-shot Exec would configure only whichever single
35	// connection happened to serve it and leave the rest on SQLite defaults, defeating the
36	// multi-reader design. page_size only takes effect before the database file is created, so it
37	// must be set at open time (on the writer that first creates sessions.db), not after the schema
38	// exists. Values avoid spaces so they need no URL escaping in the DSN query string.
39	var connectionPragmas = []string{
40		"busy_timeout=15000",
41		"journal_mode(WAL)",
42		"synchronous=NORMAL",
43		"cache_size=-64000",
44		"temp_store=MEMORY",
45		"mmap_size=268435456",
46		"page_size=8192",
47	}
48	
49	// Session is one row of the restore index (the `sessions` table), plus Body, which is
50	// indexed into the FTS table rather than stored on the row. See docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
51	type Session struct {
52		ProjectID    string // resolved git_id (else workspace_id)
53		ProjectName  string
54		Agent        string // provider id: claude, codex, gemini, droid, deepseek, cursor
55		SessionID    string // native session id (uuid)
56		CreatedAt    string // ISO 8601, first turn
57		UpdatedAt    string // ISO 8601, last activity (last turn, else file mtime)
58		UserTurns    int    // count of user prompts
59		TotalTurns   int    // count of all messages
60		Slug         string
61		Name         string
62		NativePath   string // absolute path the provider opens to read this session
63		OriginCwd    string // working directory the session was launched from
64		Size         int64  // native file size, bytes — part of the freshness fingerprint
65		Mtime        int64  // native file mtime, epoch ms — part of the freshness fingerprint
66		IndexVersion int    // reindex logic version that wrote this row — part of the fingerprint
67		IndexedAt    string // ISO 8601, when reindex last wrote this row
68	
69		// Body is the full conversation text, indexed into sessions_fts (not persisted on
70		// the sessions row). Left empty on rows read back out of the index.
71		Body string
72	
73		// IsNew is a write-time hint, not a persisted column: when true, the caller has
74		// determined this (agent, session_id) has no existing index row, so upsertOne can skip
75		// looking up and deleting a prior FTS row before insert. Leave false when unsure — the
76		// lookup-and-delete is then kept, which is always correct (a missing prior row is a no-op).
77		IsNew bool
78	}
79	
80	// Fingerprint identifies an indexed session's freshness: the native file's size and
81	// mtime, plus the reindex logic version that produced the row. reindex skips a session
82	// whose fingerprint is unchanged. See docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
83	type Fingerprint struct {
84		Size    int64
85		Mtime   int64
86		Version int
87	}
88	
89	// Store is a handle to sessions.db.
90	type Store struct {
91		db *sql.DB
92	}
93	
94	// DefaultPath returns ~/.specstory/sessions.db.
95	func DefaultPath() (string, error) {
96		home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
97		if err != nil {
98			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve home directory: %w", err)
99		}
100		return filepath.Join(home, ".specstory", "sessions.db"), nil
101	}
102	
103	// Open opens (or creates) sessions.db for writing — a single serialized connection,
104	// applying WAL + performance pragmas (matching pkg/provenance) and ensuring the schema
105	// exists. Use OpenReader for the read-only interactive browse path.
106	func Open(path string) (*Store, error) {
107		return openWith(path, writerConns)
108	}
109	
110	// OpenReader opens sessions.db for the interactive browse path (resume/search), which
111	// only reads. It allows several concurrent connections so one slow full-text query can't
112	// starve the UI (WAL permits many simultaneous readers). Never write through this handle.
113	func OpenReader(path string) (*Store, error) {
114		return openWith(path, readerConns)
115	}
116	
117	func openWith(path string, maxConns int) (*Store, error) {
118		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
119			return nil, fmt.Errorf("creating database directory: %w", err)
120		}
121	
122		dsn := "file:" + filepath.ToSlash(path) + "?_pragma=" + strings.Join(connectionPragmas, "&_pragma=")
123		db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", dsn)
124		if err != nil {
125			return nil, fmt.Errorf("opening sessions.db: %w", err)
126		}
127	
128		db.SetMaxOpenConns(maxConns)
129		db.SetMaxIdleConns(maxConns)
130	
131		s := &Store{db: db}
132		if err := s.ensureSchema(); err != nil {
133			_ = db.Close()
134			return nil, fmt.Errorf("ensuring schema: %w", err)
135		}
136		return s, nil
137	}
138	
139	// Close closes the database connection.
140	func (s *Store) Close() error {
141		return s.db.Close()
142	}
143	
144	// sessionColumns is the canonical sessions column list, shared by every SELECT so the
145	// scan order in scanSessions stays in lockstep with it.
146	const sessionColumns = `project_id, project_name, agent, session_id, created_at, updated_at,
147		user_turns, total_turns, slug, name, native_path, origin_cwd, size, mtime, index_version, indexed_at`
148	
149	// sessionInsertColumns is sessionColumns plus fts_rowid, the internal link to the session's
150	// FTS row. fts_rowid is write-only — set on insert, read only by SessionBody's join — so it is
151	// deliberately kept out of sessionColumns and the Session struct rather than threaded through
152	// every read path.
153	const sessionInsertColumns = sessionColumns + `, fts_rowid`
154	
155	func (s *Store) ensureSchema() error {
156		schema := `
157		CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
158			project_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
159			project_name TEXT,
160			agent        TEXT NOT NULL,
161			session_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
162			created_at   TEXT,
163			updated_at   TEXT,
164			user_turns   INTEGER,
165			total_turns  INTEGER,
166			slug         TEXT,
167			name         TEXT,
168			native_path  TEXT,
169			origin_cwd   TEXT,
170			size          INTEGER,
171			mtime         INTEGER,
172			index_version INTEGER,
173			indexed_at    TEXT,
174			fts_rowid     INTEGER,
175			PRIMARY KEY (agent, session_id)
176		);
177		-- Composite over the project filter PLUS the picker's sort order. ListByProject
178		-- (the resume picker's hot path) filters by project_id and orders by
179		-- updated_at DESC, created_at DESC; this index serves both, so SQLite walks it
180		-- backward instead of filtering then sorting in a temp b-tree. project_id is the
181		-- left prefix, so ProjectCount/UnattributedCount still use it. Replaces the old
182		-- single-column idx_sessions_project (dropped in the migration below).
183		CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_project_recent ON sessions(project_id, updated_at, created_at);
184	
185		-- Standalone FTS5 index over the conversation body + name. session_id/agent ride
186		-- along UNINDEXED as join keys back to the sessions row. See docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
187		CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions_fts USING fts5(
188			session_id UNINDEXED,
189			agent UNINDEXED,
190			name,
191			body
192		);
193		`
194		if _, err := s.db.Exec(schema); err != nil {
195			return fmt.Errorf("executing schema: %w", err)
196		}
197		// Migration for indexes created before index_version existed (the column is part of
198		// the freshness fingerprint). The error is benign when the column already exists.
199		s.runMigration(`ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN index_version INTEGER DEFAULT 0`)
200		// fts_rowid links a session row to its sessions_fts row, so the body read and the
201		// delete-before-insert are O(1) rowid lookups instead of whole-FTS scans (session_id/agent
202		// are UNINDEXED). NULL on rows written before this column existed; a reindex (reindexVersion
203		// bump) repopulates it. Benign error when the column already exists.
204		s.runMigration(`ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN fts_rowid INTEGER`)
205		// Drop the old single-column project index now superseded by the composite
206		// idx_sessions_project_recent (project_id is its left prefix). Idempotent; a no-op
207		// on fresh databases that never had it.
208		s.runMigration(`DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_sessions_project`)
209		return nil
210	}
211	
212	// runMigration applies an idempotent schema migration whose error is usually the benign
213	// "column/index already exists". We can't cleanly tell that apart from a real failure (locked
214	// DB, I/O) without matching driver-specific strings, so we log at Debug rather than fail: a
215	// genuine problem still resurfaces as a later query error, but it is no longer fully invisible.
216	func (s *Store) runMigration(stmt string) {
217		if _, err := s.db.Exec(stmt); err != nil {
218			slog.Debug("sessionindex: migration step skipped", "stmt", stmt, "error", err)
219		}
220	}
221	
222	// Fingerprints returns the freshness fingerprint of every indexed session, keyed by
223	// fingerprintKey(agent, session_id). reindex loads this once and skips any session
224	// whose native file is unchanged (same size + mtime) and was indexed by the current
225	// logic version.
226	func (s *Store) Fingerprints() (map[string]Fingerprint, error) {
227		rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT agent, session_id, size, mtime, index_version FROM sessions`)
228		if err != nil {
229			return nil, err
230		}
231		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
232	
233		out := make(map[string]Fingerprint)
234		for rows.Next() {
235			var agent, sessionID string
236			var fp Fingerprint
237			if err := rows.Scan(&agent, &sessionID, &fp.Size, &fp.Mtime, &fp.Version); err != nil {
238				return nil, err
239			}
240			out[FingerprintKey(agent, sessionID)] = fp
241		}
242		return out, rows.Err()
243	}
244	
245	// FingerprintKey is the map key for a session's fingerprint: agent + NUL + session_id.
246	func FingerprintKey(agent, sessionID string) string {
247		return agent + "\x00" + sessionID
248	}
249	
250	// sessionUpsertStmts are the per-row statements UpsertBatch prepares once and reuses across
251	// every row in a transaction, so the SQL is parsed once per batch instead of once per row.
252	type sessionUpsertStmts struct {
253		insSession    *sql.Stmt
254		selOldRowid   *sql.Stmt
255		delFTSByRowid *sql.Stmt
256		delFTSByKey   *sql.Stmt
257		insFTS        *sql.Stmt
258	}
259	
260	// upsertOne writes one session's row and full-text row using the batch's prepared statements.
261	// FTS5 standalone tables are not auto-synced, so the FTS row is maintained by hand. The new FTS
262	// row is inserted first so its rowid can be stored on the sessions row (fts_rowid) — that link
263	// is what makes later body reads and replace-deletes O(1) rowid lookups instead of whole-FTS
264	// scans (session_id/agent are UNINDEXED). For an existing session the prior FTS row is removed
265	// first; brand-new sessions (sess.IsNew) skip that lookup-and-delete entirely.
266	func upsertOne(st sessionUpsertStmts, sess Session) error {
267		if !sess.IsNew {
268			if err := deleteOldFTSRow(st, sess); err != nil {
269				return err
270			}
271		}
272		res, err := st.insFTS.Exec(sess.SessionID, sess.Agent, sess.Name, sess.Body)
273		if err != nil {
274			return fmt.Errorf("insert fts row: %w", err)
275		}
276		ftsRowid, err := res.LastInsertId()
277		if err != nil {
278			return fmt.Errorf("read fts rowid: %w", err)
279		}
280		if _, err := st.insSession.Exec(
281			sess.ProjectID, sess.ProjectName, sess.Agent, sess.SessionID, sess.CreatedAt, sess.UpdatedAt,
282			sess.UserTurns, sess.TotalTurns, sess.Slug, sess.Name, sess.NativePath, sess.OriginCwd,
283			sess.Size, sess.Mtime, sess.IndexVersion, sess.IndexedAt, ftsRowid); err != nil {
284			return fmt.Errorf("upsert session row: %w", err)
285		}
286		return nil
287	}
288	
289	// deleteOldFTSRow removes an existing session's current FTS row before the sessions row is
290	// replaced (INSERT OR REPLACE would otherwise drop the fts_rowid link and orphan the FTS row).
291	// It resolves the row by its stored fts_rowid (O(1)); for rows written before fts_rowid existed
292	// (NULL) it falls back to the by-key delete — a whole-FTS scan that a reindex retires by
293	// repopulating fts_rowid.
294	func deleteOldFTSRow(st sessionUpsertStmts, sess Session) error {
295		var oldRowid sql.NullInt64
296		switch err := st.selOldRowid.QueryRow(sess.Agent, sess.SessionID).Scan(&oldRowid); {
297		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
298			return nil // no prior row to remove
299		case err != nil:
300			return fmt.Errorf("look up old fts rowid: %w", err)
301		}
302		if oldRowid.Valid {
303			if _, err := st.delFTSByRowid.Exec(oldRowid.Int64); err != nil {
304				return fmt.Errorf("clear fts row by rowid: %w", err)
305			}
306			return nil
307		}
308		if _, err := st.delFTSByKey.Exec(sess.Agent, sess.SessionID); err != nil {
309			return fmt.Errorf("clear legacy fts row: %w", err)
310		}
311		return nil
312	}
313	
314	// prepareUpsert prepares the per-row statements on tx and returns them with a closer.
315	func prepareUpsert(tx *sql.Tx) (sessionUpsertStmts, func(), error) {
316		var prepared []*sql.Stmt
317		closer := func() {
318			for _, s := range prepared {
319				_ = s.Close()
320			}
321		}
322		prep := func(what, query string) (*sql.Stmt, error) {
323			s, err := tx.Prepare(query)
324			if err != nil {
325				closer()
326				return nil, fmt.Errorf("prepare %s: %w", what, err)
327			}
328			prepared = append(prepared, s)
329			return s, nil
330		}
331	
332		insSession, err := prep("session upsert", `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO sessions (`+sessionInsertColumns+`)
333			VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)`)
334		if err != nil {
335			return sessionUpsertStmts{}, func() {}, err
336		}
337		selOldRowid, err := prep("fts rowid lookup", `SELECT fts_rowid FROM sessions WHERE agent = ? AND session_id = ?`)
338		if err != nil {
339			return sessionUpsertStmts{}, func() {}, err
340		}
341		delFTSByRowid, err := prep("fts delete by rowid", `DELETE FROM sessions_fts WHERE rowid = ?`)
342		if err != nil {
343			return sessionUpsertStmts{}, func() {}, err
344		}
345		delFTSByKey, err := prep("fts delete by key", `DELETE FROM sessions_fts WHERE agent = ? AND session_id = ?`)
346		if err != nil {
347			return sessionUpsertStmts{}, func() {}, err
348		}
349		insFTS, err := prep("fts insert", `INSERT INTO sessions_fts (session_id, agent, name, body) VALUES (?,?,?,?)`)
350		if err != nil {
351			return sessionUpsertStmts{}, func() {}, err
352		}
353		return sessionUpsertStmts{
354			insSession:    insSession,
355			selOldRowid:   selOldRowid,
356			delFTSByRowid: delFTSByRowid,
357			delFTSByKey:   delFTSByKey,
358			insFTS:        insFTS,
359		}, closer, nil
360	}
361	
362	// Upsert inserts or replaces a single session row and its full-text row, atomically. A
363	// re-index of the same session (same agent + session_id) replaces both in lockstep.
364	func (s *Store) Upsert(sess Session) error {
365		return s.UpsertBatch([]Session{sess})
366	}
367	
368	// UpsertBatch writes many sessions in one transaction — the write path for `reindex`,
369	// which batches to avoid thousands of tiny WAL commits.
370	func (s *Store) UpsertBatch(sessions []Session) error {
371		if len(sessions) == 0 {
372			return nil
373		}
374		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
375		if err != nil {
376			return fmt.Errorf("begin upsert: %w", err)
377		}
378		committed := false
379		defer func() {
380			if !committed {
381				_ = tx.Rollback()
382			}
383		}()
384	
385		st, closeStmts, err := prepareUpsert(tx)
386		if err != nil {
387			return err
388		}
389		defer closeStmts()
390	
391		for _, sess := range sessions {
392			if err := upsertOne(st, sess); err != nil {
393				return err
394			}
395		}
396	
397		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
398			return fmt.Errorf("commit upsert: %w", err)
399		}
400		committed = true
401		return nil
402	}
403	
404	// Exists reports whether a session row is already indexed, looked up by the primary key
405	// (agent, session_id) so it stays O(log n) instead of scanning. Because a session's sessions
406	// row and its sessions_fts row are always written together (upsertOne, one transaction), a
407	// missing sessions row guarantees a missing FTS row — which lets the live writer set
408	// Session.IsNew and skip the whole-table FTS delete for genuinely new sessions.
409	func (s *Store) Exists(agent, sessionID string) (bool, error) {
410		var one int
411		err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT 1 FROM sessions WHERE agent = ? AND session_id = ?`, agent, sessionID).Scan(&one)
412		if errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
413			return false, nil
414		}
415		if err != nil {
416			return false, err
417		}
418		return true, nil
419	}
420	
421	// Count returns the number of indexed sessions.
422	func (s *Store) Count() (int, error) {
423		var n int
424		if err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions`).Scan(&n); err != nil {
425			return 0, err
426		}
427		return n, nil
428	}
429	
430	// ProjectCount returns the number of distinct attributed projects in the index
431	// (excluding the unknownID bucket).
432	func (s *Store) ProjectCount(unknownID string) (int, error) {
433		var n int
434		err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT project_id) FROM sessions WHERE project_id != ?`, unknownID).Scan(&n)
435		return n, err
436	}
437	
438	// UnattributedCount returns the number of sessions in the unknownID bucket.
439	func (s *Store) UnattributedCount(unknownID string) (int, error) {
440		var n int
441		err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions WHERE project_id = ?`, unknownID).Scan(&n)
442		return n, err
443	}
444	
445	// ListByProject returns a project's sessions, newest activity first. Body is not
446	// populated (it lives only in the FTS index). Used by the `specstory resume` picker.
447	func (s *Store) ListByProject(projectID string) ([]Session, error) {
448		rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT `+sessionColumns+`
449			FROM sessions WHERE project_id = ? ORDER BY updated_at DESC, created_at DESC`, projectID)
450		if err != nil {
451			return nil, err
452		}
453		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
454		return scanSessions(rows)
455	}
456	
457	// ProjectSummary is a rolled-up view of one project for the all-projects picker.
458	type ProjectSummary struct {
459		ProjectID    string
460		ProjectName  string
461		Sessions     int            // total sessions in the project
462		LastActivity string         // most recent updated_at across the project
463		AgentCounts  map[string]int // sessions per agent (claude, codex, …)
464	}
465	
466	// ListProjects returns one rolled-up summary per project, most recently active first.
467	// Used by the all-projects view (date-bucketed). The unknown-project bucket is included;
468	// the caller decides how to present it.
469	func (s *Store) ListProjects() ([]ProjectSummary, error) {
470		rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT project_id, project_name, agent, COUNT(*), MAX(updated_at)
471			FROM sessions GROUP BY project_id, agent`)
472		if err != nil {
473			return nil, err
474		}
475		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
476	
477		byID := map[string]*ProjectSummary{}
478		for rows.Next() {
479			var pid, pname, agent, last string
480			var n int
481			if err := rows.Scan(&pid, &pname, &agent, &n, &last); err != nil {
482				return nil, err
483			}
484			ps, ok := byID[pid]
485			if !ok {
486				ps = &ProjectSummary{ProjectID: pid, ProjectName: pname, AgentCounts: map[string]int{}}
487				byID[pid] = ps
488			}
489			ps.Sessions += n
490			ps.AgentCounts[agent] += n
491			if ps.ProjectName == "" {
492				ps.ProjectName = pname
493			}
494			if last > ps.LastActivity {
495				ps.LastActivity = last
496			}
497		}
498		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
499			return nil, err
500		}
501	
502		out := make([]ProjectSummary, 0, len(byID))
503		for _, ps := range byID {
504			out = append(out, *ps)
505		}
506		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].LastActivity > out[j].LastActivity })
507		return out, nil
508	}
509	
510	// SessionBody returns the full-text conversation body for a session (for the preview
511	// pane), or "" if the session has no indexed body (e.g. Cursor, metadata-only).
512	func (s *Store) SessionBody(agent, sessionID string) (string, error) {
513		var body string
514		// Fast path: resolve the FTS row by the rowid stored on the sessions row (O(1)), instead of
515		// scanning the whole FTS (session_id/agent are UNINDEXED).
516		err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT f.body FROM sessions s
517			JOIN sessions_fts f ON f.rowid = s.fts_rowid
518			WHERE s.agent = ? AND s.session_id = ?`, agent, sessionID).Scan(&body)
519		if err == nil {
520			return body, nil
521		}
522		if !errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
523			return "", err
524		}
525		// No fts_rowid link (a row written before the column existed). Fall back to the by-key scan;
526		// a reindex repopulates fts_rowid and retires this path.
527		err = s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT body FROM sessions_fts WHERE agent = ? AND session_id = ?`,
528			agent, sessionID).Scan(&body)
529		if errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows) {
530			return "", nil
531		}
532		return body, err
533	}
534	
535	// Search runs a full-text query and returns matching sessions, most recent first.
536	// projectID scopes the search to one project; "" searches across all projects.
537	func (s *Store) Search(query, projectID string) ([]Session, error) {
538		return s.SearchContext(context.Background(), query, projectID)
539	}
540	
541	// SearchContext is Search bound to a context. The interactive search cancels the context
542	// when a newer keystroke arrives, which aborts a slow in-flight query and frees its
543	// connection. Snippets are deliberately fetched separately for only the visible rows:
544	// FTS5 snippet generation over hundreds of full transcripts dominates broad searches.
545	func (s *Store) SearchContext(ctx context.Context, query, projectID string) ([]Session, error) {
546		q := `SELECT ` + prefixed("s", sessionColumns) + `
547			FROM sessions_fts
548			JOIN sessions s ON s.agent = sessions_fts.agent AND s.session_id = sessions_fts.session_id
549			WHERE sessions_fts MATCH ?`
550		args := []any{query}
551		if projectID != "" {
552			q += ` AND s.project_id = ?`
553			args = append(args, projectID)
554		}
555		// Order by recency, not FTS5's BM25 rank. For full-conversation transcripts BM25 is
556		// noisy (length-normalization dominates) and a single-term query gets no IDF signal,
557		// so relevance order looks arbitrary; newest-first is what's useful when browsing your
558		// own history. It also makes LIMIT keep the 500 most RECENT matches (vs the 500 densest)
559		// and skips BM25 scoring entirely. updated_at is ISO 8601, so TEXT sort = chronological.
560		q += ` ORDER BY s.updated_at DESC LIMIT 500`
561	
562		rows, err := s.db.QueryContext(ctx, q, args...)
563		if err != nil {
564			return nil, err
565		}
566		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
567	
568		return scanSessions(rows)
569	}
570	
571	// Snippets returns highlighted match snippets for the provided sessions. The result is
572	// keyed by FingerprintKey(agent, session_id). Matched terms are wrapped in \x02 and \x03
573	// (STX/ETX) so callers can highlight without colliding with conversation text.
574	func (s *Store) Snippets(query string, sessions []Session) (map[string]string, error) {
575		return s.SnippetsContext(context.Background(), query, sessions)
576	}
577	
578	// SnippetsContext is Snippets bound to a context. Callers should pass only the currently
579	// visible rows; snippet() is intentionally lazy because it is the expensive part of FTS
580	// search on long transcripts.
581	func (s *Store) SnippetsContext(ctx context.Context, query string, sessions []Session) (map[string]string, error) {
582		out := map[string]string{}
583		if query == "" || len(sessions) == 0 {
584			return out, nil
585		}
586	
587		clauses := make([]string, 0, len(sessions))
588		args := []any{query}
589		seen := map[string]bool{}
590		for _, sess := range sessions {
591			key := FingerprintKey(sess.Agent, sess.SessionID)
592			if seen[key] {
593				continue
594			}
595			seen[key] = true
596			clauses = append(clauses, `(agent = ? AND session_id = ?)`)
597			args = append(args, sess.Agent, sess.SessionID)
598		}
599		if len(clauses) == 0 {
600			return out, nil
601		}
602	
603		q := `SELECT agent, session_id, snippet(sessions_fts, 3, char(2), char(3), '…', 12)
604			FROM sessions_fts
605			WHERE sessions_fts MATCH ? AND (` + strings.Join(clauses, ` OR `) + `)`
606		rows, err := s.db.QueryContext(ctx, q, args...)
607		if err != nil {
608			return nil, err
609		}
610		defer func() { _ = rows.Close() }()
611	
612		for rows.Next() {
613			var agent, sessionID, snippet string
614			if err := rows.Scan(&agent, &sessionID, &snippet); err != nil {
615				return nil, err
616			}
617			out[FingerprintKey(agent, sessionID)] = snippet
618		}
619		return out, rows.Err()
620	}
621	
622	// prefixed qualifies each comma-separated column in cols with the given table alias,
623	// e.g. prefixed("s", "a, b") -> "s.a, s.b". Used to disambiguate the sessions columns
624	// in the FTS join (where session_id/agent also exist on the FTS table).
625	func prefixed(alias, cols string) string {
626		parts := strings.Split(cols, ",")
627		for i, p := range parts {
628			parts[i] = alias + "." + strings.TrimSpace(p)
629		}
630		return strings.Join(parts, ", ")
631	}
632	
633	// scanSessions scans rows selected with sessionColumns (in order) into Sessions.
634	func scanSessions(rows *sql.Rows) ([]Session, error) {
635		var out []Session
636		for rows.Next() {
637			var s Session
638			if err := rows.Scan(
639				&s.ProjectID, &s.ProjectName, &s.Agent, &s.SessionID, &s.CreatedAt, &s.UpdatedAt,
640				&s.UserTurns, &s.TotalTurns, &s.Slug, &s.Name, &s.NativePath, &s.OriginCwd,
641				&s.Size, &s.Mtime, &s.IndexVersion, &s.IndexedAt,
642			); err != nil {
643				return nil, err
644			}
645			out = append(out, s)
646		}
647		return out, rows.Err()
648	}

284	// prepareResumeTarget produces the native session ID to hand to ExecAgentAndWatch.
285	// Same-agent resume reuses the existing session; cross-agent reconstructs the
286	// source SessionData into the target's native store and returns the fresh ID.
287	func prepareResumeTarget(plan *resumePlan, cwd string, out io.Writer) (string, error) {
288		// Same agent: native resume on the existing session, no transform.
289		if plan.fromID == plan.toID {
290			fprintf(out, "\nResuming %s session %s in place...\n", plan.from.Name(), shortID(plan.sessionID))
291			return plan.sessionID, nil
292		}
293	
294		// One event records every cross-agent reconstruction outcome so portability usage and
295		// failure rates are visible. Fired at each terminal branch below.
296		track := func(outcome string) {
297			analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventResumeReconstructed, analytics.Properties{
298				"from_agent": plan.fromID,
299				"to_agent":   plan.toID,
300				"outcome":    outcome,
301			})
302		}
303		slog.Info("resume: reconstructing cross-agent session",
304			"from", plan.fromID, "to", plan.toID, "sessionID", plan.sessionID)
305	
306		// Cross-agent: load source SessionData, reconstruct, write into target store.
307		// The source must be read from the directory it was originally launched in, not the
308		// user's current cwd — a session picked from another project (all-projects browser)
309		// lives elsewhere, and providers like Codex locate it by its recorded cwd. The
310		// reconstructed session is still written and launched under the current cwd below.
311		fromCwd := plan.fromCwd
312		if fromCwd == "" {
313			fromCwd = cwd
314		}
315		fromSession, err := plan.from.GetAgentChatSession(fromCwd, plan.sessionID, false)
316		if err != nil {
317			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to load source session: %w", err)
318		}
319		if fromSession == nil || fromSession.SessionData == nil {
320			return "", fmt.Errorf("source session %s has no data to reconstruct", plan.sessionID)
321		}
322	
323		note := fmt.Sprintf("Resumed from a %s session via SpecStory.", plan.from.Name())
324		rec, err := plan.to.ReconstructSession(fromSession.SessionData, spi.ReconstructOptions{
325			WorkspaceRoot: cwd,
326			MigrationNote: note,
327		})
328		if err != nil {
329			if errors.Is(err, spi.ErrReconstructionUnsupported) {
330				track("unsupported")
331				return "", utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
332					"%s can't yet be a cross-agent resume target. Choose Claude Code or Codex CLI (or resume in %s itself).",
333					plan.to.Name(), plan.from.Name())}
334			}
335			slog.Warn("resume: reconstruction failed", "from", plan.fromID, "to", plan.toID, "error", err)
336			track("error")
337			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to reconstruct session for %s: %w", plan.to.Name(), err)
338		}
339	
340		path, err := plan.to.NativeSessionPath(cwd, rec.Filename)
341		if err != nil {
342			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve target session path: %w", err)
343		}
344		if err := writeReconstructedSession(path, rec.Content); err != nil {
345			return "", err
346		}
347		// The agent runs in a separate process and resolves the session by reading this file the
348		// instant it starts. On a filesystem without strong close-to-open coherence the freshly
349		// written file can lag, so confirm it is actually readable before handing the agent a
350		// --resume it would otherwise reject as "session not found".
351		if err := waitForSessionFileVisible(path, sessionFileVisibleTimeout); err != nil {
352			return "", fmt.Errorf("reconstructed %s session is not ready to resume: %w", plan.to.Name(), err)
353		}
354	
355		slog.Info("resume: wrote reconstructed session", "path", path, "newID", rec.SessionID)
356		track("success")
357		fprintf(out, "\nReconstructed %s session into %s as %s.\n", plan.from.Name(), plan.to.Name(), shortID(rec.SessionID))
358		return rec.SessionID, nil
359	}
360	
361	// shortID abbreviates a session ID for display.
362	func shortID(id string) string {
363		if len(id) <= 13 {
364			return id
365		}
366		return id[:5] + "..." + id[len(id)-5:]
367	}
368	
369	// sessionFileVisibleTimeout bounds how long resume waits for a just-written reconstructed
370	// session file to become readable to other processes before launching the agent. It is
371	// generous enough to absorb the propagation lag of a weak-coherence filesystem (network or
372	// roaming home, cloud-synced folder, VM/container shared mount) yet short enough not to hang
373	// an interactive command — on a local disk the very first check passes, so it never waits.
374	const sessionFileVisibleTimeout = 10 * time.Second
375	
376	// writeReconstructedSession durably and atomically writes a reconstructed session file. A
377	// plain os.WriteFile leaves the data in the page cache and the new directory entry possibly
378	// non-durable; on a filesystem without strong close-to-open coherence the separately-spawned
379	// agent process can then fail to see a (large) file and report the session as missing. To
380	// avoid that, the content is written to a temp file in the SAME directory (so the rename is
381	// atomic rather than cross-device), fsync'd, renamed into place, and the parent directory is
382	// fsync'd so the entry itself is durable.
383	func writeReconstructedSession(path string, content []byte) (err error) {
384		dir := filepath.Dir(path)
385		if mkErr := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); mkErr != nil {
386			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create target session directory: %w", mkErr)
387		}
388	
389		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp(dir, ".resume-*.tmp")
390		if err != nil {
391			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create temp session file: %w", err)
392		}
393		tmpPath := tmp.Name()
394		// Best-effort cleanup of the temp file on any early return; a no-op once it is renamed away.
395		defer func() { _ = os.Remove(tmpPath) }()
396	
397		// Preserve the world-readable mode the previous os.WriteFile(…, 0o644) produced
398		// (CreateTemp makes the file 0o600).
399		if chErr := tmp.Chmod(0o644); chErr != nil {
400			_ = tmp.Close()
401			return fmt.Errorf("failed to set session file mode: %w", chErr)
402		}
403		if _, wErr := tmp.Write(content); wErr != nil {
404			_ = tmp.Close()
405			return fmt.Errorf("failed to write temp session file: %w", wErr)
406		}
407		// Flush the bytes to the backing store before the rename so a reader cannot observe a
408		// renamed-but-empty file.
409		if syncErr := tmp.Sync(); syncErr != nil {
410			_ = tmp.Close()
411			return fmt.Errorf("failed to flush temp session file: %w", syncErr)
412		}
413		if closeErr := tmp.Close(); closeErr != nil {
414			return fmt.Errorf("failed to close temp session file: %w", closeErr)
415		}
416	
417		if rnErr := os.Rename(tmpPath, path); rnErr != nil {
418			return fmt.Errorf("failed to move session file into place: %w", rnErr)
419		}
420	
421		// Fsync the directory so the new entry is durable and propagates. Best-effort: not all
422		// platforms permit fsync on a directory handle, and it is a negligible cost on local disks.
423		if d, openErr := os.Open(dir); openErr == nil {
424			_ = d.Sync()
425			_ = d.Close()
426		}
427		return nil
428	}
429	
430	// waitForSessionFileVisible polls until path is readable — present AND with at least one
431	// byte available, since on a weak-coherence filesystem a stat can succeed before the
432	// content propagates — or the timeout elapses, in which case it returns a diagnostic error
433	// so the caller can fail clearly rather than launch a --resume the agent would reject.
434	func waitForSessionFileVisible(path string, timeout time.Duration) error {
435		deadline := time.Now().Add(timeout)
436		for {
437			readable, checkErr := sessionFileReadable(path)
438			if readable {
439				return nil
440			}
441			if time.Now().After(deadline) {
442				return fmt.Errorf("session file %q did not become readable within %s "+
443					"(the target filesystem may lack close-to-open coherence): %w", path, timeout, checkErr)
444			}
445			time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
446		}
447	}
448	
449	// sessionFileReadable reports whether path exists and at least one byte can be read.
450	// A reconstructed session always has content, so an empty read means it has not propagated
451	// yet even though the directory entry exists. This is a readiness probe, not a parse: a
452	// single-byte read keeps it O(1) and format-agnostic, so it stays cheap for a binary native
453	// format (e.g. Cursor's store.db, which has no newline to scan to) as well as JSONL.
454	func sessionFileReadable(path string) (bool, error) {
455		f, err := os.Open(path)
456		if err != nil {
457			return false, err
458		}
459		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
460	
461		var b [1]byte
462		n, err := f.Read(b[:])
463		if n > 0 {
464			return true, nil
465		}
466		if err == io.EOF || err == nil {
467			return false, fmt.Errorf("session file is empty")
468		}
469		return false, err
470	}
471

1	package cmd
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"strings"
6		"time"
7		"unicode"
8	
9		tea "charm.land/bubbletea/v2"
10	
11		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/sessionindex"
12	)
13	
14	// ftsQuery turns free-form input into a safe FTS5 prefix query (alnum tokens only).
15	// minQueryLen is the shortest query we run a full-text search for. A single-character
16	// prefix (e.g. "t*") matches almost the entire corpus, and ranking + snippet generation
17	// over that set is pathologically slow (~80s on a ~800-session index), so we never fire
18	// it. Shared by resume and search so both behave the same.
19	const minQueryLen = 2
20	
21	// queryReady reports whether input has enough searchable characters (letters/digits, the
22	// same runes ftsQuery keeps) to run an FTS query. Below minQueryLen we don't search.
23	func queryReady(input string) bool {
24		n := 0
25		for _, r := range input {
26			if unicode.IsLetter(r) || unicode.IsDigit(r) {
27				n++
28				if n >= minQueryLen {
29					return true
30				}
31			}
32		}
33		return false
34	}
35	
36	// ftsQuery turns free-form input into an FTS5 query string. Three shapes:
37	//
38	//   - Bare words become independent prefix terms, AND-ed (matched anywhere, any order) —
39	//     a loose search:  thank you      -> thank* you*
40	//   - A double-quoted span becomes a phrase: tokens adjacent and in order —
41	//     an exact phrase:  "thank you"    -> "thank you"
42	//   - A still-open quote (the user is mid-typing the phrase) keeps the final token a prefix,
43	//     so results keep updating live:  "thank yo    -> thank + yo*
44	//
45	// A single typed word that contains punctuation (e.g. a filename, "poem.txt") is itself an
46	// adjacency phrase. The index's unicode61 tokenizer splits on every non-alphanumeric run, so
47	// "poem.txt" is stored as the two adjacent tokens poem, txt — never the fused "poemtxt". We
48	// must tokenize the query the same way, or the term can't match what was indexed. So a bare
49	// "poem.txt" becomes the phrase poem + txt* (adjacent, prefix the last token for type-ahead);
50	// quoted, it is the committed phrase "poem txt" (adjacent, no prefix).
51	//
52	// Only letters and digits survive tokenization, so no FTS5 syntax character from the raw
53	// input can reach MATCH — every query this builds is safe to execute.
54	func ftsQuery(input string) string {
55		// Splitting on '"' yields alternating runs: even indexes are outside quotes, odd indexes
56		// are inside. An odd-indexed run that is also the LAST run means the closing quote hasn't
57		// been typed yet (an open phrase), so its final token stays a prefix for live type-ahead.
58		segs := strings.Split(input, `"`)
59		var parts []string
60		for i, seg := range segs {
61			switch {
62			case i%2 == 0: // outside quotes: each word is its own loose, prefix-terminated term
63				for _, f := range strings.Fields(seg) {
64					if toks := fieldTokens(f); len(toks) > 0 {
65						parts = append(parts, strings.Join(toks, " + ")+"*")
66					}
67				}
68			case i == len(segs)-1: // open phrase (still typing): adjacency across all tokens + prefix last
69				if toks := segmentTokens(seg); len(toks) > 0 {
70					parts = append(parts, strings.Join(toks, " + ")+"*")
71				}
72			default: // closed phrase: exact adjacency, no prefix (a committed phrase)
73				if toks := segmentTokens(seg); len(toks) > 0 {
74					parts = append(parts, `"`+strings.Join(toks, " ")+`"`)
75				}
76			}
77		}
78		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
79	}
80	
81	// fieldTokens splits one whitespace-delimited field into its FTS5 tokens the way the index's
82	// default unicode61 tokenizer does: every run of non-alphanumeric characters is a token
83	// boundary. So "poem.txt" -> [poem, txt] and "max-cpu!" -> [max, cpu]. Mirroring the index
84	// tokenizer here is the whole point — previously punctuation was stripped and the pieces
85	// fused into one token ("poemtxt") that the index, holding poem and txt separately, never had.
86	func fieldTokens(field string) []string {
87		var tokens []string
88		var b strings.Builder
89		flush := func() {
90			if b.Len() > 0 {
91				tokens = append(tokens, b.String())
92				b.Reset()
93			}
94		}
95		for _, r := range field {
96			if unicode.IsLetter(r) || unicode.IsDigit(r) {
97				b.WriteRune(r)
98			} else {
99				flush()
100			}
101		}
102		flush()
103		return tokens
104	}
105	
106	// segmentTokens tokenizes a whole quoted segment into one flat, ordered token list — both the
107	// whitespace between words and any punctuation within them are token boundaries (unicode61),
108	// so the phrase matches the adjacency the index actually stored.
109	func segmentTokens(seg string) []string {
110		var tokens []string
111		for _, f := range strings.Fields(seg) {
112			tokens = append(tokens, fieldTokens(f)...)
113		}
114		return tokens
115	}
116	
117	// ---- async, debounced full-text search ----
118	
119	// searchDebounceMsg fires after a brief typing pause; the query runs only if its seq is
120	// still current. searchResultMsg carries the async FTS results back to the model. Both
121	// keep typing instant: the input updates synchronously while the query runs off-thread.
122	type searchDebounceMsg struct {
123		seq  int
124		kind tuiMode // modeList (project-scoped) or modeProjects (global)
125	}
126	
127	type searchResultMsg struct {
128		seq      int
129		kind     tuiMode
130		sessions []sessionindex.Session
131	}
132	
133	type snippetResultMsg struct {
134		seq      int
135		kind     tuiMode
136		snippets map[string]string
137	}
138	
139	const searchDebounceDelay = 50 * time.Millisecond
140	
141	// searchDebounce schedules a debounce tick. On fire, the model checks the seq and decides
142	// whether to actually run the query (so only the last keystroke in a burst queries).
143	func searchDebounce(seq int, kind tuiMode) tea.Cmd {
144		return tea.Tick(searchDebounceDelay, func(time.Time) tea.Msg {
145			return searchDebounceMsg{seq: seq, kind: kind}
146		})
147	}
148	
149	// runSearch returns a command that performs the FTS query off the UI thread.
150	func (m sessionTUI) runSearch(seq int, kind tuiMode, ctx context.Context) tea.Cmd {
151		store := m.store
152		query, projectID := m.searchQuery, m.projectID
153		if kind == modeProjects {
154			query, projectID = m.globalQuery, m.globalScopeID // "" = all projects, else scoped
155		}
156		fq := ftsQuery(query)
157		return func() tea.Msg {
158			if !queryReady(query) {
159				return searchResultMsg{seq: seq, kind: kind}
160			}
161			sessions, _ := store.SearchContext(ctx, fq, projectID)
162			return searchResultMsg{seq: seq, kind: kind, sessions: sessions}
163		}
164	}
165	
166	// applySearchResults installs async FTS results into the matching list (scoped or global).
167	func (m *sessionTUI) applySearchResults(kind tuiMode, sessions []sessionindex.Session) {
168		if kind == modeProjects {
169			m.globalSnippets = map[string]string{}
170			var out []sessionindex.Session
171			for _, s := range sessions {
172				if m.agentFilter == "" || s.Agent == m.agentFilter {
173					out = append(out, s)
174				}
175			}
176			m.globalResults = out
177			if m.globalCursor > len(m.globalResults)-1 {
178				m.globalCursor = len(m.globalResults) - 1
179			}
180			if m.globalCursor < 0 {
181				m.globalCursor = 0
182			}
183			m.globalTop = 0
184			return
185		}
186	
187		// Cache the raw results so a subsequent agent cycle re-filters them in memory (no re-query).
188		m.searchRaw = sessions
189		var out []sessionindex.Session
190		for _, s := range sessions {
191			if m.agentFilter == "" || s.Agent == m.agentFilter {
192				out = append(out, s)
193			}
194		}
195		m.filtered = out
196		m.filteredSnippets = map[string]string{}
197		if m.cursor > len(m.filtered)-1 {
198			m.cursor = len(m.filtered) - 1
199		}
200		if m.cursor < 0 {
201			m.cursor = 0
202		}
203		m.top = 0
204		m.clampScroll()
205	}
206	
207	func (m *sessionTUI) requestVisibleSnippets(kind tuiMode) tea.Cmd {
208		var query string
209		var rows []sessionindex.Session
210		if kind == modeProjects {
211			if !queryReady(m.globalQuery) || len(m.globalResults) == 0 {
212				return nil
213			}
214			h := m.globalHeight()
215			end := min(m.globalTop+h, len(m.globalResults))
216			if m.globalTop >= end {
217				return nil
218			}
219			query = m.globalQuery
220			rows = append([]sessionindex.Session(nil), m.globalResults[m.globalTop:end]...)
221		} else {
222			if !queryReady(m.searchQuery) || len(m.filtered) == 0 {
223				return nil
224			}
225			h := m.listHeight()
226			end := min(m.top+h, len(m.filtered))
227			if m.top >= end {
228				return nil
229			}
230			query = m.searchQuery
231			rows = append([]sessionindex.Session(nil), m.filtered[m.top:end]...)
232		}
233	
234		store := m.store
235		fq := ftsQuery(query)
236		m.snippetSeq++
237		seq := m.snippetSeq
238		return func() tea.Msg {
239			snips, _ := store.SnippetsContext(context.Background(), fq, rows)
240			return snippetResultMsg{seq: seq, kind: kind, snippets: snips}
241		}
242	}

84	// validateFlags checks for mutually exclusive flag combinations
85	func validateFlags() error {
86		if console && silent {
87			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "cannot use `console` and `silent` together. These are mutually exclusive"}
88		}
89		if debug && !console && !logFile {
90			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "`debug` requires either `console` or `log` to be specified"}
91		}
92		if onlyCloudSync && noCloudSync {
93			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "cannot use `only-cloud-sync` and `no-cloud-sync` together. These are mutually exclusive"}
94		}
95		if onlyStats && onlyCloudSync {
96			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "cannot use --only-stats and --only-cloud-sync together. These flags are mutually exclusive"}
97		}
98		if onlyStats && noCloudSync {

100		}
101		if onlyStats && printToStdout {
102			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "cannot use --only-stats and --print together. These flags are mutually exclusive"}
103		}
104		if printToStdout && onlyCloudSync {
105			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "cannot use --print and `only-cloud-sync` together. These are mutually exclusive"}
106		}
107		if printToStdout && console {
108			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "cannot use --print and `console` together. Console debug output would interleave with markdown on stdout"}
109		}
110		return nil
111	}

113	// createRootCommand dynamically creates the root command with provider information

148

155		}

204	
205				// Set silent mode for user messages
206				log.SetSilent(silent)
207	
208				// Initialize cloud sync manager
209				cloud.InitSyncManager(!noCloudSync)
210				cloud.SetSilent(silent)
211				cloud.SetClientVersion(version)
212				// Set custom cloud URL if provided (otherwise cloud package uses its default)
213				if cloudURL != "" {
214					cloud.SetAPIBaseURL(cloudURL)
215				}
216	
217				// If --cloud-token flag was provided, verify the refresh token works
218				// This bypasses normal authentication and uses the token for this session only
219				if cloudToken != "" {
220					slog.Info("Using session-only refresh token from --cloud-token flag")
221					if err := cloud.SetSessionRefreshToken(cloudToken); err != nil {
222						fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr) // Visual separation
223						fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "❌ Failed to authenticate with the provided token:")
224						fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "   %v\n", err)
225						fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr)
226						fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "💡 The token may be invalid, expired, or revoked.")
227						fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "   Please check your token and try again, or use 'specstory login' for interactive authentication.")
228						fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr)
229						return fmt.Errorf("authentication failed with provided token")
230					}
231					if !silent {
232						fmt.Println()
233						fmt.Println("🔑 Authenticated using provided refresh token (session-only)")
234						fmt.Println()
235					}
236				}
237	
238				// Validate that --only-cloud-sync requires authentication
239				if onlyCloudSync && !cloud.IsAuthenticated() {
240					return utils.ValidationError{Message: "--only-cloud-sync requires authentication. Please run 'specstory login' first"}
241				}
242	
243				return nil
244			},
245			Run: func(c *cobra.Command, args []string) {
246				// Track help command usage (when no command is specified)
247				analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventHelpCommand, analytics.Properties{
248					"help_topic":  "general",
249					"help_reason": "requested",
250				})
251				// If no command is specified, show logo then help
252				cmdpkg.DisplayLogoAndHelp(c)
253			},
254		}
255	}

259	// createRunCommand dynamically creates the run command with provider information
260	func createRunCommand() *cobra.Command {
261		registry := factory.GetRegistry()
262		ids := registry.ListIDs()
263		providerList := registry.GetProviderList()
264	
265		// Build dynamic examples
266		examples := `
267	# Run default agent with auto-saving
268	specstory run`
269	
270		if len(ids) > 0 {
271			examples += "\n\n# Run specific agent"
272			for _, id := range ids {
273				examples += fmt.Sprintf("\nspecstory run %s", id)
274			}
275	
276			// Use first provider for custom command example
277			examples += fmt.Sprintf("\n\n# Run with custom command\nspecstory run %s -c \"/custom/path/to/agent\"", ids[0])
278		}
279	
280		examples += `
281	
282	# Resume a specific session
283	specstory run --resume 5c5c2876-febd-4c87-b80c-d0655f1cd3fd
284	
285	# Run with custom output directory
286	specstory run --output-dir ~/my-sessions`
287	
288		// Determine default agent name
289		defaultAgent := "the default agent"
290		if len(ids) > 0 {
291			if provider, err := registry.Get(ids[0]); err == nil {
292				defaultAgent = provider.Name()
293			}
294		}
295	
296		longDesc := fmt.Sprintf(`Launch terminal coding agents in interactive mode with auto-save markdown file generation.
297	
298	By default, launches %s. Specify a specific agent ID to use a different agent.`, defaultAgent)
299		if providerList != "No providers registered" {
300			longDesc += "\n\nAvailable provider IDs: " + providerList + "."
301		}
302	
303		return &cobra.Command{
304			Use:     "run [provider-id]",
305			Aliases: []string{"r"},
306			Short:   "Launch terminal coding agents in interactive mode with auto-save",
307			Long:    longDesc,
308			Example: examples,
309			Args:    cobra.MaximumNArgs(1), // Accept 0 or 1 argument (provider ID)
310			PreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
311				// Get custom command if provided via flag
312				customCmd, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("command")
313	
314				// Validate that -c flag requires a provider
315				if customCmd != "" && len(args) == 0 {
316					registry := factory.GetRegistry()
317					ids := registry.ListIDs()
318					example := "specstory run <provider> -c \"/custom/path/to/agent\""
319					if len(ids) > 0 {
320						example = fmt.Sprintf("specstory run %s -c \"/custom/path/to/agent\"", ids[0])
321					}
322					return utils.ValidationError{
323						Message: "The -c/--command flag requires a provider to be specified.\n" +
324							"Example: " + example,
325					}
326				}
327				return nil
328			},
329			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
330				config.EnsureDefaultProjectConfig()
331				slog.Info("Running in interactive mode")
332	
333				// Get custom command if provided via flag
334				customCmd, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("command")
335	
336				// Get the provider
337				registry := factory.GetRegistry()
338				var providerID string
339				if len(args) == 0 {
340					// Default to first registered provider
341					ids := registry.ListIDs()
342					if len(ids) > 0 {
343						providerID = ids[0]
344					} else {
345						return fmt.Errorf("no providers registered")
346					}
347				} else {
348					providerID = args[0]
349				}
350	
351				provider, err := registry.Get(providerID)
352				if err != nil {
353					// Provider not found - show helpful error
354					fmt.Printf("❌ Provider '%s' is not a valid provider implementation\n\n", providerID)
355	
356					ids := registry.ListIDs()
357					if len(ids) > 0 {
358						fmt.Println("The registered providers are:")
359						for _, id := range ids {
360							if p, _ := registry.Get(id); p != nil {
361								fmt.Printf("  • %s - %s\n", id, p.Name())
362							}
363						}
364						fmt.Println("\nExample: specstory run " + ids[0])
365					}
366					return err
367				}
368	
369				// Fall back to config file provider command if -c flag wasn't provided
370				if customCmd == "" && loadedConfig != nil {
371					customCmd = loadedConfig.GetProviderCmd(providerID)
372				}
373	
374				slog.Info("Launching agent", "provider", provider.Name())
375	
376				// Set the agent provider for analytics
377				analytics.SetAgentProviders([]string{provider.Name()})
378	
379				// Setup output configuration
380				config, err := utils.SetupOutputConfig(outputDir, debugDir)
381				if err != nil {
382					return err
383				}
384				// Ensure history directory exists for interactive mode
385				if err := utils.EnsureHistoryDirectoryExists(config); err != nil {
386					return err
387				}
388	
389				// Initialize project identity
390				cwd, err := os.Getwd()
391				if err != nil {
392					slog.Error("Failed to get current working directory", "error", err)
393					return err
394				}
395				identityManager := utils.NewProjectIdentityManager(cwd)
396				if _, err := identityManager.EnsureProjectIdentity(); err != nil {
397					// Log error but don't fail the command
398					slog.Error("Failed to ensure project identity", "error", err)
399				}
400	
401				// Create context for graceful cancellation (Ctrl+C handling)
402				ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
403				defer cancel()
404	
405				// Start provenance infrastructure before the agent so all file changes are captured
406				provenanceEngine, provenanceCleanup, err := provenance.StartEngine(provenanceEnabled)
407				if err != nil {
408					return err
409				}
410				defer provenanceCleanup()
411	
412				fsCleanup, err := provenance.StartFSWatcher(ctx, provenanceEngine, cwd)
413				if err != nil {
414					return err
415				}
416				defer fsCleanup()
417	
418				// Check authentication for cloud sync
419				cmdpkg.CheckAndWarnAuthentication(noCloudSync)
420				// Track extension activation
421				analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventExtensionActivated, nil)
422	
423				// Get resume session ID if provided
424				resumeSessionID, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("resume")
425				if resumeSessionID != "" {
426					resumeSessionID = strings.TrimSpace(resumeSessionID)
427					// Note: Different providers may have different session ID formats
428					// Let the provider validate its own format
429					slog.Info("Resuming session", "sessionId", resumeSessionID)
430				}
431	
432				// Get debug-raw flag value (must be before callback to capture in closure)
433				debugRaw, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("debug-raw")
434				useUTC := !localTimeZone
435	
436				// Keep sessions.db current in real time alongside the markdown writes (nil/no-op
437				// if the index can't be opened — never block the running agent on it).
438				liveIndex := cmdpkg.NewLiveIndexer(cwd)
439				defer liveIndex.Close()
440	
441				// This callback pattern enables real-time processing of agent sessions
442				// without blocking the agent's execution. As the agent writes updates to its
443				// data files, the provider's watcher detects changes and invokes this callback,
444				// allowing immediate markdown generation and cloud sync. Errors are logged but
445				// don't stop execution because transient failures (e.g., network issues) shouldn't
446				// interrupt the user's coding session.
447				sessionCallback := func(session *spi.AgentChatSession) {
448					if session == nil {
449						return
450					}
451	
452					// Track the session ID for deep linking on exit
453					lastRunSessionID = session.SessionID
454	
455					// Process the session (write markdown and sync to cloud)
456					// Don't show output during interactive run mode
457					// This is autosave mode (true)
458					_, err := sessionpkg.ProcessSingleSession(context.Background(), session, config, sessionpkg.ProcessingOptions{
459						OnlyCloudSync:      onlyCloudSync,
460						IsAutosave:         true,
461						DebugRaw:           debugRaw,
462						UseUTC:             useUTC,
463						NoTelemetryPrompts: noTelemetryPrompts,
464					})
465					if err != nil {
466						// Log error but continue - don't fail the whole run
467						// In interactive mode, we prioritize keeping the agent running.
468						// Failed markdown writes or cloud syncs can be retried later via
469						// the sync command, so we just log and continue.
470						slog.Error("Failed to process session update",
471							"sessionId", session.SessionID,
472							"error", err)
473					}
474	
475					// Mirror the markdown write into the restore index in real time.
476					liveIndex.Record(providerID, session)
477	
478					// Push agent events to provenance engine for correlation
479					provenance.ProcessEvents(ctx, provenanceEngine, session)
480				}
481	
482				// Execute the agent and watch for updates
483				slog.Info("Starting agent execution and monitoring", "provider", provider.Name())
484				err = provider.ExecAgentAndWatch(cwd, customCmd, resumeSessionID, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
485	
486				if err != nil {
487					slog.Error("Agent execution failed", "provider", provider.Name(), "error", err)
488				}
489	
490				return err
491			},
492		}
493	}
494	
495	var runCmd *cobra.Command

544			Use:     "sync [provider-id]",
545			Aliases: []string{"s"},
546			Short:   "Sync markdown files for terminal coding agent sessions",
547			Long:    longDesc,

555				}

557					return utils.ValidationError{Message: "cannot use --only-stats with -s/--session. Use --only-stats without -s to collect statistics for all sessions"}
558				}
559				return nil

566

587	// syncSpecificSessions syncs one or more sessions by their IDs
588	// When printToStdout is set, outputs markdown to stdout instead of saving to files.
589	// args[0] is the optional provider ID
590	func syncSpecificSessions(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, sessionIDs []string) error {
591		if len(sessionIDs) == 1 {
592			slog.Info("Running single session sync", "sessionId", sessionIDs[0])
593		} else {
594			slog.Info("Running multiple session sync", "sessionCount", len(sessionIDs))
595		}
596	
597		// Get debug-raw flag value
598		debugRaw, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("debug-raw")
599		useUTC := !localTimeZone
600	
601		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
602		if err != nil {
603			slog.Error("Failed to get current working directory", "error", err)
604			return err
605		}
606	
607		// Setup file output and cloud sync (not needed for --print mode)
608		var config utils.OutputConfig
609		// liveIndex keeps sessions.db current for the sessions we save. Skipped for --print, which
610		// outputs to stdout without saving (so there's nothing to "sync"). Best-effort no-op on nil.
611		var liveIndex *cmdpkg.LiveIndexer
612		if !printToStdout {
613			config, err = utils.SetupOutputConfig(outputDir, debugDir)
614			if err != nil {
615				return err
616			}
617	
618			identityManager := utils.NewProjectIdentityManager(cwd)
619			if _, err := identityManager.EnsureProjectIdentity(); err != nil {
620				slog.Error("Failed to ensure project identity", "error", err)
621			}
622	
623			cmdpkg.CheckAndWarnAuthentication(noCloudSync || onlyStats)
624	
625			if err := utils.EnsureHistoryDirectoryExists(config); err != nil {
626				return err
627			}
628	
629			liveIndex = cmdpkg.NewLiveIndexer(cwd)
630			defer liveIndex.Close()
631		}
632	
633		registry := factory.GetRegistry()
634	
635		// Track statistics for summary output
636		var successCount, notFoundCount, errorCount int
637		var lastError error
638	
639		// Resolve provider once if specified (fail fast if provider not found)
640		var specifiedProvider spi.Provider
641		if len(args) > 0 {
642			providerID := args[0]
643			provider, err := registry.Get(providerID)
644			if err != nil {
645				if !printToStdout {
646					fmt.Printf("❌ Provider '%s' not found\n", providerID)
647				}
648				return fmt.Errorf("provider '%s' not found: %w", providerID, err)
649			}
650			specifiedProvider = provider
651		}
652	
653		// Process each session ID
654		var printedSessions int // tracks sessions printed to stdout for separator logic
655		for _, sessionID := range sessionIDs {
656			sessionID = strings.TrimSpace(sessionID)
657			if sessionID == "" {
658				continue // Skip empty session IDs
659			}
660	
661			// Find session across providers
662			var session *spi.AgentChatSession
663			var foundAgentID string // registry id of the provider that has this session (for indexing)
664	
665			// Case A: Provider was specified - use it directly
666			if specifiedProvider != nil {
667				session, err = specifiedProvider.GetAgentChatSession(cwd, sessionID, debugRaw)
668				if err != nil {
669					if !printToStdout {
670						fmt.Printf("❌ Error getting session '%s' from %s: %v\n", sessionID, specifiedProvider.Name(), err)
671					}
672					slog.Error("Error getting session from provider", "sessionId", sessionID, "provider", specifiedProvider.Name(), "error", err)
673					errorCount++
674					lastError = err
675					continue
676				}
677				if session == nil {
678					if !printToStdout {
679						fmt.Printf("❌ Session '%s' not found in %s\n", sessionID, specifiedProvider.Name())
680					}
681					slog.Warn("Session not found in provider", "sessionId", sessionID, "provider", specifiedProvider.Name())
682					notFoundCount++
683					continue
684				}
685				foundAgentID = args[0]
686			} else {
687				// Case B: No provider specified - try all providers
688				providerIDs := registry.ListIDs()
689				for _, id := range providerIDs {
690					provider, err := registry.Get(id)
691					if err != nil {
692						continue
693					}
694	
695					session, err = provider.GetAgentChatSession(cwd, sessionID, debugRaw)
696					if err != nil {
697						slog.Debug("Error checking provider for session", "provider", id, "sessionId", sessionID, "error", err)
698						continue
699					}
700					if session != nil {
701						foundAgentID = id
702						if !silent && !printToStdout {
703							fmt.Printf("✅ Found session '%s' for %s\n", sessionID, provider.Name())
704						}
705						break // Found it, don't check other providers
706					}
707				}
708	
709				if session == nil {
710					if !printToStdout {
711						fmt.Printf("❌ Session '%s' not found in any provider\n", sessionID)
712					}
713					slog.Warn("Session not found in any provider", "sessionId", sessionID)
714					notFoundCount++
715					continue
716				}
717			}
718	
719			// Process the found session
720			if printToStdout {
721				sessionpkg.ValidateSessionData(session, debugRaw)
722				sessionpkg.WriteDebugSessionData(session, debugRaw)
723	
724				markdownContent, err := sessionpkg.GenerateMarkdownFromAgentSession(session.SessionData, false, useUTC)
725				if err != nil {
726					slog.Error("Failed to generate markdown", "sessionId", session.SessionID, "error", err)
727					analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventSyncMarkdownError, analytics.Properties{
728						"session_id": session.SessionID,
729						"error":      err.Error(),
730						"mode":       "print",
731					})
732					errorCount++
733					lastError = err
734					continue
735				}
736	
737				// Separate multiple sessions with a horizontal rule
738				if printedSessions > 0 {
739					fmt.Print("\n---\n\n")
740				}
741				fmt.Print(markdownContent)
742				printedSessions++
743				successCount++
744				analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventSyncMarkdownSuccess, analytics.Properties{
745					"session_id": session.SessionID,
746					"mode":       "print",
747				})
748			} else {
749				// Normal sync: write to file and optionally cloud sync
750				if _, err := sessionpkg.ProcessSingleSession(context.Background(), session, config, sessionpkg.ProcessingOptions{
751					OnlyCloudSync:      onlyCloudSync,
752					ShowOutput:         true,
753					DebugRaw:           debugRaw,
754					UseUTC:             useUTC,
755					NoTelemetryPrompts: noTelemetryPrompts,
756				}); err != nil {
757					errorCount++
758					lastError = err
759				} else {
760					successCount++
761					// Mirror the synced session into the restore index.
762					liveIndex.Record(foundAgentID, session)
763				}
764			}
765		}
766	
767		// Print summary if multiple sessions were processed (not for --print mode)
768		if !printToStdout && len(sessionIDs) > 1 && !silent {
769			fmt.Println()
770			fmt.Println("📊 Session sync summary:")
771			fmt.Printf("  ✅ %d %s successfully synced\n", successCount, pluralSession(successCount))
772			if notFoundCount > 0 {
773				fmt.Printf("  ❌ %d %s not found\n", notFoundCount, pluralSession(notFoundCount))
774			}
775			if errorCount > 0 {
776				fmt.Printf("  ❌ %d %s failed with errors\n", errorCount, pluralSession(errorCount))
777			}
778			fmt.Println()
779		}
780	
781		// Return error if any sessions failed
782		if errorCount > 0 || (notFoundCount > 0 && successCount == 0) {
783			if lastError != nil {
784				return lastError
785			}
786			return fmt.Errorf("%d %s not found", notFoundCount, pluralSession(notFoundCount))
787		}
788	
789		return nil
790	}
791	
792	// preloadBulkSessionSizesIfNeeded optimizes bulk syncs by fetching all session sizes upfront.
793	// This avoids making individual HEAD requests for each session during sync operations.
794	//
795	// The function only performs the preload if:
796	//   - Cloud sync is enabled (noCloudSync flag is false)
797	//   - User is authenticated with SpecStory Cloud
798	//   - A valid projectID can be determined from the identity manager
799	//
800	// Parameters:
801	//   - identityManager: Provides project identity (git_id or workspace_id) for the current project
802	//
803	// The preloaded sizes are cached in the SyncManager and shared across all providers since they
804	// use the same projectID. If the bulk fetch fails or if projectID cannot be determined, individual
805	// sessions will gracefully fall back to HEAD requests during sync.
806	//
807	// This function is safe to call multiple times but should typically be called once before processing
808	// multiple sessions in batch sync operations.
809	func preloadBulkSessionSizesIfNeeded(identityManager *utils.ProjectIdentityManager) {
810		// Skip if cloud sync is disabled or user is not authenticated
811		if noCloudSync || !cloud.IsAuthenticated() {
812			return
813		}
814	
815		// Get projectID from identity manager - required for cloud sync
816		projectID, err := identityManager.GetProjectID()
817		if err != nil {
818			slog.Warn("Cannot preload session sizes: failed to get project ID", "error", err)
819			return
820		}
821	
822		// Preload bulk sizes once - shared across all providers since they use same projectID
823		if syncMgr := cloud.GetSyncManager(); syncMgr != nil {
824			syncMgr.PreloadSessionSizes(projectID)
825		} else {
826			slog.Warn("Cannot preload session sizes: sync manager is nil despite authentication")
827		}
828	}
829	
830	// syncProvider performs the actual sync for a single provider.
831	// The caller-provided statsCollector accumulates statistics across providers so
832	// they can be flushed to disk in a single I/O operation after all providers are done.
833	// Returns (sessionCount, error) for analytics tracking.
834	func syncProvider(provider spi.Provider, providerID string, config utils.OutputConfig, debugRaw bool, useUTC bool, statsCollector *sessionpkg.StatisticsCollector) (int, error) {

842		// SessionData below, so indexing it is essentially free. Best-effort: a nil indexer (open

844		liveIndex := cmdpkg.NewLiveIndexer(cwd)

852			parseProgress = func(current, total int) {
853				fmt.Printf("\rParsing %s sessions [%d/%d]", providerName, current, total)
854				_ = os.Stdout.Sync()

856		}

858		// Get all sessions from the provider

862		}

864		sessionCount := len(sessions)

866		if sessionCount == 0 && !silent {

869			fmt.Println()
870			return 0, nil
871		}
872	
873		if !silent && !onlyStats {

875		}

877		// Initialize statistics

888			session := &sessions[i]
889	
890			// Process session in a closure so defers scope to each iteration,
891			// ensuring spans are ended and metrics recorded even on early returns.
892			func() {
893				processingStart := time.Now()
894	
895				// Create a context with a deterministic trace ID from the session ID
896				sessionCtx := telemetry.ContextWithSessionTrace(ctx, session.SessionID)
897	
898				// Start an OTel span for this session processing
899				sessionCtx, span := telemetry.Tracer("specstory").Start(sessionCtx, "process_session")
900				defer span.End()
901	
902				// Compute session statistics
903				sessionStats := telemetry.ComputeSessionStats(agentName, session)
904				defer func() {
905					telemetry.RecordSessionMetrics(sessionCtx, sessionStats, time.Since(processingStart))
906				}()
907	
908				// Set session span attributes
909				telemetry.SetSessionSpanAttributes(span, sessionStats)
910	
911				// Create child spans for each exchange
912				if session.SessionData != nil && len(session.SessionData.Exchanges) > 0 {
913					telemetry.ProcessExchangeSpans(sessionCtx, sessionStats, session.SessionData.Exchanges, noTelemetryPrompts)
914				}
915	
916				sessionpkg.ValidateSessionData(session, debugRaw)
917				sessionpkg.WriteDebugSessionData(session, debugRaw)
918	
919				// Mirror this session into the restore index as we sync it (covers normal and
920				// only-stats modes — we have the SessionData either way).
921				liveIndex.Record(providerID, session)
922	
923				// Generate markdown from SessionData
924				markdownContent, err := sessionpkg.GenerateMarkdownFromAgentSession(session.SessionData, false, useUTC)
925				if err != nil {

937				// Compute statistics from the SessionData

940

950	
951				// Check if file already exists with same content
952				identicalContent := false
953				fileExists := false

955					fileExists = true
956					if string(existingContent) == markdownContent {
957						identicalContent = true

962				}
963	
964				// Write file if needed (skip if only-cloud-sync is enabled)
965				if !onlyCloudSync {

967						// Ensure history directory exists (handles deletion during long-running sync)

969							slog.Error("Failed to ensure history directory", "error", err)
970							return
971						}
972						err := os.WriteFile(fileFullPath, []byte(markdownContent), 0644)
973						if err != nil {
974							slog.Error("Error writing markdown file",
975								"sessionId", session.SessionID,
976								"error", err)

978							analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventSyncMarkdownError, analytics.Properties{
979								"session_id":      session.SessionID,
980								"error":           err.Error(),
981								"only_cloud_sync": onlyCloudSync,
982							})
983							return
984						}
985						slog.Info("Successfully wrote file",

987							"path", fileFullPath)
988	
989						// Track successful sync

991							analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventSyncMarkdownNew, analytics.Properties{
992								"session_id":      session.SessionID,
993								"only_cloud_sync": onlyCloudSync,
994							})
995						} else {

997								"session_id":      session.SessionID,

999							})
1000						}
1001					}
1002	
1003					// Update statistics for normal mode

1006					} else if fileExists {

1008					} else {
1009						stats.SessionsCreated++
1010					}
1011				} else {

1015						"sessionId", session.SessionID)

1022			}()
1023	
1024			// Print progress with [n/m] format
1025			if !silent && !onlyStats {

1027				_ = os.Stdout.Sync()

1029		}
1030	
1031		// Print newline after progress
1032		if !silent && sessionCount > 0 && !onlyCloudSync && !onlyStats {
1033			fmt.Println()
1034

1037	
1038			// Print summary message with proper pluralization

1040				log.ColorBoldGreen, provider.Name(), log.ColorReset,

1042			fmt.Println()

42		//   5: parse Codex bodies from the enumerated NativePath (was a by-id tree search), so a
43		//      session's body and its freshness fingerprint now derive from the same file
44		//   6: populate sessions.fts_rowid (the O(1) link to each session's FTS row) — existing
45		//      rows have it NULL until re-parsed, so bump to repopulate the whole index once
46		reindexVersion = 6
47	)
48	
49	// CreateReindexCommand builds the `specstory reindex` command: a full, from-scratch
50	// rebuild of the restore index (~/.specstory/sessions.db) of every coding-agent session
51	// SpecStory can find, across all projects and providers. See docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
52	func CreateReindexCommand() *cobra.Command {
53		cmd := &cobra.Command{
54			Use:   "reindex",
55			Short: "Rebuild the restore index of all known agent sessions",
56			Long: `Rebuild the restore index used by 'specstory resume'.
57	
58	'reindex' enumerates every session across all installed agents and projects and writes a
59	searchable index to ~/.specstory/sessions.db. It is incremental: a session whose native
60	file is unchanged since it was last indexed is skipped, so re-runs are fast. Use --force to
61	re-index everything regardless. The index is a derived cache: it is safe to delete.`,
62			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
63			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
64				force, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("force")
65				return runReindex(force)
66			},
67		}
68		cmd.Flags().Bool("force", false, "re-index every session even if unchanged")
69		return cmd
70	}
71	
72	// reindexItem is one unit of work: a session to parse and index. size/mtime are the
73	// native file's stat, captured during the freshness check and reused (no re-stat).
74	type reindexItem struct {
75		agent string
76		prov  spi.Provider
77		ref   spi.GlobalSessionRef
78		size  int64
79		mtime int64
80		isNew bool // no existing index row → writer can skip the standalone-FTS delete
81	}
82	
83	func runReindex(force bool) error {
84		start := time.Now()
85	
86		// Graceful Ctrl+C: stop feeding work, flush what's written, exit cleanly.
87		ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
88		defer cancel()
89	
90		dbPath, err := sessionindex.DefaultPath()
91		if err != nil {
92			return err
93		}
94		store, err := sessionindex.Open(dbPath)
95		if err != nil {
96			return fmt.Errorf("opening restore index: %w", err)
97		}
98		defer func() { _ = store.Close() }()
99	
100		registry := factory.GetRegistry()
101	
102		// ---- Phase 1: enumerate every provider concurrently, then dedup ----
103		ids, provs, perProvider := enumerateAll(registry, true)
104	
105		// Existing fingerprints, so unchanged sessions can be skipped (the incremental path).
106		fingerprints := map[string]sessionindex.Fingerprint{}
107		if !force {
108			if fps, err := store.Fingerprints(); err != nil {
109				slog.Warn("reindex: could not load fingerprints, re-indexing all", "error", err)
110			} else {
111				fingerprints = fps
112			}
113		}
114	
115		best, order, foundPerAgent := dedupRefs(ids, provs, perProvider)
116		found := len(order)
117		cache := &projectIDCache{m: map[string]projectIDName{}}
118		work, totals, unchanged := selectWork(order, best, fingerprints, "", force, cache)
119	
120		if found == 0 {
121			fprintln(os.Stderr, "No agent sessions found to index.")
122			return nil
123		}
124		fprintf(os.Stderr, "✓   Found %d sessions  ·  %s\n", found, summarizeCounts(ids, foundPerAgent))
125		if len(work) == 0 {
126			fprintf(os.Stderr, "✓   All %d sessions already up to date.  (%.1fs)\n", found, time.Since(start).Seconds())
127			return nil
128		}
129		if unchanged > 0 {
130			fprintf(os.Stderr, "    %d unchanged · indexing %d…\n\n", unchanged, len(work))
131		} else {
132			fprintln(os.Stderr, "")
133		}
134	
135		// ---- Phase 2+3: parse (worker pool) → write (single goroutine), with live progress ----
136		prog := newReindexProgress(ids, totals)
137		prog.begin()
138		indexedAt := start.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)
139		writeErr := processWork(ctx, store, work, cache, indexedAt, min(runtime.NumCPU(), 12), prog)
140		prog.end()
141	
142		if writeErr != nil {
143			return fmt.Errorf("writing restore index: %w", writeErr)
144		}
145	
146		// ---- Summary (counts reflect the WHOLE index, not just this run's work) ----
147		elapsed := time.Since(start)
148		projects, _ := store.ProjectCount(unknownProjectID)
149		unattributed, _ := store.UnattributedCount(unknownProjectID)
150		printReindexSummary(ids, foundPerAgent, dbPath, elapsed, prog.totalDone(), unchanged, projects, unattributed)
151		analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventReindexCompleted, analytics.Properties{
152			"sessions":     len(work),
153			"unchanged":    unchanged,
154			"projects":     projects,
155			"unattributed": unattributed,
156			"duration_ms":  elapsed.Milliseconds(),
157		})
158		return nil
159	}
160	
161	// ---- reindex engine (shared by the foreground command and the background warm) ----
162	
163	// enumerateAll concurrently lists every installed provider's sessions. The returned slices
164	// are index-aligned: provs[i]/perProvider[i] correspond to ids[i] (a nil provs[i] marks a
165	// provider that failed to load). When visible, it renders a live "Scanning agents…" line
166	// (foreground reindex); the background warm passes visible=false and stays silent.
167	func enumerateAll(registry *factory.Registry, visible bool) (ids []string, provs []spi.Provider, perProvider [][]spi.GlobalSessionRef) {
168		ids = registry.ListIDs()
169		perProvider = make([][]spi.GlobalSessionRef, len(ids))
170		provs = make([]spi.Provider, len(ids))
171	
172		var scan *scanProgress
173		if visible {
174			scan = newScanProgress(ids)
175			scan.begin()
176			defer scan.end()
177		}
178	
179		var ewg sync.WaitGroup
180		for i, id := range ids {
181			prov, err := registry.Get(id)
182			if err != nil {
183				continue
184			}
185			provs[i] = prov
186			reporter := scan.reporterFor(id)
187			ewg.Add(1)
188			go func(i int, id string, prov spi.Provider, reporter *spi.ScanReporter) {
189				defer ewg.Done()
190				refs := enumerateOne(id, prov, reporter)
191				perProvider[i] = refs
192				scan.markDone(id, len(refs))
193			}(i, id, prov, reporter)
194		}
195		ewg.Wait()
196		return ids, provs, perProvider
197	}
198	
199	// enumerateOne enumerates a single provider's sessions, preferring the progress-reporting path
200	// (Codex, the long pole, ticks the live line; the rest snap to their final count via markDone).
```
