200	// (Codex, the long pole, ticks the live line; the rest snap to their final count via markDone).
201	// A panic in a provider's enumeration (e.g. a malformed session tree) is recovered and logged so
202	// one bad provider degrades to "no sessions" rather than crashing the entire reindex/warm sweep.
203	func enumerateOne(id string, prov spi.Provider, reporter *spi.ScanReporter) (refs []spi.GlobalSessionRef) {
204		defer func() {
205			if r := recover(); r != nil {
206				slog.Error("reindex: provider enumeration panicked", "provider", id, "panic", r)
207				refs = nil
208			}
209		}()
210		var err error
211		if pe, ok := prov.(spi.ProgressEnumerator); ok {
212			refs, err = pe.ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(reporter)
213		} else {
214			refs, err = prov.ListAllAgentChatSessions()
215		}
216		if err != nil {
217			slog.Warn("reindex: enumeration failed", "provider", id, "error", err)
218		}
219		return refs
220	}
221	
222	// dedupRefs collapses enumerated refs by (agent, session_id), keeping the freshest file. A
223	// resumed session can span MULTIPLE native files sharing one id; they all map to one
224	// (agent, session_id) row, so without dedup the duplicates ping-pong — each run, one file's
225	// stat never matches the fingerprint the other file just stored, re-indexing both forever.
226	// Keeping the freshest by mtime makes the fingerprint stable. Sessions with no native id are
227	// dropped (unresumable, and would collide on the PK). order is first-seen order (deterministic
228	// processing); foundPerAgent is the distinct-session count per agent (for the "Found" line).
229	func dedupRefs(ids []string, provs []spi.Provider, perProvider [][]spi.GlobalSessionRef) (best map[string]reindexItem, order []string, foundPerAgent map[string]int) {
230		best = map[string]reindexItem{}
231		foundPerAgent = map[string]int{}
232		for i, id := range ids {
233			if provs[i] == nil {
234				continue
235			}
236			for _, ref := range perProvider[i] {
237				if strings.TrimSpace(ref.SessionID) == "" {
238					slog.Debug("reindex: skipping session with no id", "agent", id, "path", ref.NativePath)
239					continue
240				}
241				size, mtime := statNative(ref.NativePath)
242				item := reindexItem{agent: id, prov: provs[i], ref: ref, size: size, mtime: mtime}
243				key := sessionindex.FingerprintKey(id, ref.SessionID)
244				if cur, ok := best[key]; ok {
245					if mtime > cur.mtime {
246						best[key] = item
247					}
248					continue
249				}
250				best[key] = item
251				order = append(order, key)
252			}
253		}
254		for _, key := range order {
255			foundPerAgent[best[key].agent]++
256		}
257		return best, order, foundPerAgent
258	}
259	
260	// selectWork applies the incremental fingerprint skip (and an optional project filter) to the
261	// deduped set. projectFilter "" means all projects; otherwise only sessions whose originating
262	// cwd resolves to that project id are kept (used by the background warm's current-project
263	// pass). totals is the per-agent to-do count (drives the foreground progress bars).
264	func selectWork(order []string, best map[string]reindexItem, fingerprints map[string]sessionindex.Fingerprint, projectFilter string, force bool, cache *projectIDCache) (work []reindexItem, totals map[string]int, unchanged int) {
265		totals = map[string]int{}
266		for _, key := range order {
267			item := best[key]
268			if projectFilter != "" {
269				if pid, _ := cache.resolve(item.ref.OriginCwd); pid != projectFilter {
270					continue
271				}
272			}
273			fp, ok := fingerprints[key]
274			if ok && fp.Size == item.size && fp.Mtime == item.mtime && fp.Version == reindexVersion {
275				unchanged++
276				continue // already indexed and unchanged
277			}
278			// A session absent from the fingerprint set has no sessions row, hence no sessions_fts
279			// row either (the pair is written atomically) — so the writer can skip the O(rows)
280			// standalone-FTS delete. Under --force the fingerprint map is deliberately empty, so
281			// absence proves nothing; keep the delete to avoid duplicate FTS rows.
282			item.isNew = !force && !ok
283			work = append(work, item)
284			totals[item.agent]++
285		}
286		return work, totals, unchanged
287	}
288	
289	// reindexReporter receives per-session progress from processWork. The foreground command
290	// passes *reindexProgress (live bars); the background warm passes nopReporter (silent).
291	type reindexReporter interface {
292		observe(projectID string)
293		inc(agent string)
294	}
295	
296	// nopReporter is the silent reporter used by the background warm.
297	type nopReporter struct{}
298	
299	func (nopReporter) observe(string) {}
300	func (nopReporter) inc(string)     {}
301	
302	// processWork parses each work item (worker pool) and writes the results to the store via a
303	// single writer goroutine, reporting progress through rep. It stops feeding work when ctx is
304	// cancelled; the writer flushes what it already received. If the writer fails (a store write
305	// error), it closes writerDone and stops draining, so the workers and the feed loop both
306	// select on writerDone to tear the pipeline down — otherwise a full sessionsCh buffer would
307	// block every worker forever and wwg.Wait would deadlock. Returns the writer's error, if any.
308	func processWork(ctx context.Context, store *sessionindex.Store, work []reindexItem, cache *projectIDCache, indexedAt string, workers int, rep reindexReporter) error {
309		if len(work) == 0 {
310			return nil
311		}
312		if workers < 1 {
313			workers = 1
314		}
315	
316		// Schedule the largest sessions first. A few huge Codex files (hundreds of MB) would
317		// otherwise be end-of-run stragglers that leave most worker cores idle; starting them
318		// first overlaps them with the long tail of small sessions. Order does not affect the
319		// resulting index.
320		sort.SliceStable(work, func(i, j int) bool { return work[i].size > work[j].size })
321	
322		sessionsCh := make(chan sessionindex.Session, 256)
323		var writeErr error
324		writerDone := make(chan struct{})
325		go func() {
326			defer close(writerDone)
327			writeErr = drainToStore(store, sessionsCh)
328		}()
329	
330		workCh := make(chan reindexItem)
331		var wwg sync.WaitGroup
332		for w := 0; w < workers; w++ {
333			wwg.Add(1)
334			go func() {
335				defer wwg.Done()
336				for item := range workCh {
337					sess := buildSession(item, cache, indexedAt)
338					rep.observe(sess.ProjectID)
339					// Abandon the push if the writer has already exited on a write error; without
340					// this, a full sessionsCh would block here forever (nothing drains it).
341					select {
342					case sessionsCh <- sess:
343						rep.inc(item.agent)
344					case <-writerDone:
345						return
346					}
347				}
348			}()
349		}

368	// warmIndexInBackground keeps ~/.specstory/sessions.db warm as a side effect of resume/search.
369	// It runs two SILENT incremental passes over its own writer handle: the current project first
370	// (so its rows refresh quickly, and the open TUI re-queries via onProjectWarmed), then the full
371	// corpus. It enumerates once and reuses the result for both passes. It stops promptly when ctx
372	// is cancelled (the TUI exited); an abandoned write batch is safe under WAL. Errors are logged
373	// at debug and never surfaced — warmth is best-effort.
374	func warmIndexInBackground(ctx context.Context, dbPath, currentProjectID string, onProjectWarmed func()) {
375		store, err := sessionindex.Open(dbPath)
376		if err != nil {
377			slog.Debug("warm: could not open index", "error", err)
378			return
379		}
380		defer func() { _ = store.Close() }()
381	
382		registry := factory.GetRegistry()
383		ids, provs, perProvider := enumerateAll(registry, false)
384		if ctx.Err() != nil {
385			return
386		}
387		best, order, _ := dedupRefs(ids, provs, perProvider)
388		cache := &projectIDCache{m: map[string]projectIDName{}}
389		indexedAt := time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)
390	
391		// Gentle: fewer workers than a foreground reindex, since the user is interacting.
392		workers := min(runtime.NumCPU(), 4)
393	
394		// Pass 1 — the current project, so its rows are fresh almost immediately.
395		fps, _ := store.Fingerprints()
396		work, _, _ := selectWork(order, best, fps, currentProjectID, false, cache)
397		if err := processWork(ctx, store, work, cache, indexedAt, workers, nopReporter{}); err != nil {
398			slog.Debug("warm: current-project pass failed", "error", err)
399		}
400		if ctx.Err() != nil {
401			return
402		}
403		if onProjectWarmed != nil {
404			onProjectWarmed() // let the open TUI re-query the (now fresh) current project
405		}
406	
407		// Pass 2 — everything else. Reload fingerprints so pass-1's writes now register as
408		// unchanged and are skipped, leaving only the rest of the corpus to parse.
409		fps, _ = store.Fingerprints()
410		work, _, _ = selectWork(order, best, fps, "", false, cache)
411		if err := processWork(ctx, store, work, cache, indexedAt, workers, nopReporter{}); err != nil {
412			slog.Debug("warm: full pass failed", "error", err)
413		}
414	}
415	
416	// ---- real-time indexing (watch / run / resume launch) ----
417	
418	// LiveIndexer keeps ~/.specstory/sessions.db current in real time, alongside the markdown
419	// files that watch/run/resume already write as a session changes. It holds one writer handle
420	// for the command's lifetime and upserts a single row per detected update, reusing the same
421	// content derivation as reindex. The project is resolved once (a watch/run has a fixed cwd).
422	//
423	// Everything is best-effort: real-time indexing must never disrupt the agent or the markdown
424	// write, so construction failures yield a nil *LiveIndexer (whose methods are no-ops) and
425	// per-update errors are logged at debug. A live row carries no native-file fingerprint
426	// (Size/Mtime/NativePath are unknown without enumerating), so the next reindex re-verifies and
427	// rewrites it with a stable fingerprint — the live row is correct and queryable in the interim.
428	type LiveIndexer struct {
429		store       *sessionindex.Store
430		cwd         string
431		projectID   string
432		projectName string
433		indexedAt   string
434	
435		mu       sync.Mutex
436		lastSeen map[string]string // session id -> last indexed UpdatedAt, to skip no-op upserts
437	}
438	
439	// NewLiveIndexer opens the index for writing and resolves the project for cwd. It returns nil
440	// (not an error) when the index can't be opened, so the caller keeps running with real-time
441	// indexing simply disabled. The caller owns Close.
442	func NewLiveIndexer(cwd string) *LiveIndexer {
443		dbPath, err := sessionindex.DefaultPath()
444		if err != nil {
445			slog.Debug("live index: no db path; real-time indexing disabled", "error", err)
446			return nil
447		}
448		store, err := sessionindex.Open(dbPath)
449		if err != nil {
450			slog.Debug("live index: cannot open index; real-time indexing disabled", "error", err)
451			return nil
452		}
453		projectID, projectName, err := utils.ComputeProjectID(cwd)
454		if err != nil || projectID == "" {
455			projectID, projectName = unknownProjectID, ""
456		}
457		return &LiveIndexer{
458			store:       store,
459			cwd:         cwd,
460			projectID:   projectID,
461			projectName: projectName,
462			indexedAt:   time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
463			lastSeen:    map[string]string{},
464		}
465	}
466	
467	// Record upserts the live session into the index. agentID is the provider's registry id (e.g.
468	// "claude"). It skips the write when the session's last activity hasn't advanced since the
469	// previous record (the watcher can fire repeatedly without new content). Safe on a nil
470	// receiver, and serialized so concurrent provider watchers don't contend on the single writer.
471	func (li *LiveIndexer) Record(agentID string, sess *spi.AgentChatSession) {
472		if li == nil || sess == nil || sess.SessionData == nil {
473			return
474		}
475		data := sess.SessionData
476	
477		updatedAt := sess.CreatedAt
478		if ts := lastTimestamp(data); ts != "" {
479			updatedAt = ts
480		}
481	
482		li.mu.Lock()
483		defer li.mu.Unlock()
484	
485		// Nothing advanced since the last write → skip the (FTS-heavy) upsert.
486		if updatedAt != "" && li.lastSeen[sess.SessionID] == updatedAt {
487			return
488		}
489	
490		// Skip the whole-table FTS delete (session_id/agent are UNINDEXED, so it scans the entire
491		// FTS) when this session has no existing row to replace. Only the first write of a session
492		// in this process can be new, and even then only if it isn't already in the index from a
493		// prior run — so we check by primary key just once, before lastSeen records the write.
494		isNew := false
495		if _, written := li.lastSeen[sess.SessionID]; !written {
496			if exists, err := li.store.Exists(agentID, sess.SessionID); err == nil {
497				isNew = !exists
498			}
499		}

525	// Close releases the writer handle. Safe on a nil receiver.
526	func (li *LiveIndexer) Close() {
527		if li == nil {
528			return
529		}
530		if err := li.store.Close(); err != nil {
531			slog.Debug("live index: close failed", "error", err)

535	// buildSession turns one enumeration ref into a fully-built index row. Every session
536	// yields a row from its metadata; the body + turn counts + last-activity time are
537	// ENRICHED via a full parse only when the originating cwd lets us re-locate the
538	// session (so Cursor, whose cwd is unknown for now, lands metadata-only). Nothing is
539	// dropped.
540	func buildSession(item reindexItem, cache *projectIDCache, indexedAt string) sessionindex.Session {
541		ref := item.ref
542		projectID, projectName := cache.resolve(ref.OriginCwd)
543	
544		sess := sessionindex.Session{
545			ProjectID:    projectID,
546			ProjectName:  projectName,
547			Agent:        item.agent,
548			SessionID:    ref.SessionID,
549			CreatedAt:    ref.CreatedAt,
550			UpdatedAt:    ref.CreatedAt, // default; overwritten by last-turn timestamp below
551			Slug:         ref.Slug,
552			Name:         ref.Name,
553			NativePath:   ref.NativePath,
554			OriginCwd:    ref.OriginCwd,
555			Size:         item.size, // captured during the freshness check (no re-stat)
556			Mtime:        item.mtime,
557			IndexVersion: reindexVersion,
558			IndexedAt:    indexedAt,
559			IsNew:        item.isNew,
560		}
561	
562		if ref.OriginCwd == "" {
563			return sess // cannot re-locate without a cwd → metadata-only
564		}
565		full, err := parseFullSession(item.prov, ref)
566		if err != nil || full == nil || full.SessionData == nil {
567			slog.Debug("reindex: full parse unavailable, indexing metadata only",
568				"agent", item.agent, "session", ref.SessionID, "error", err)
569			return sess
570		}
571	
572		data := full.SessionData
573		sess.Body = flattenBody(data)
574		sess.UserTurns, sess.TotalTurns = countTurns(data)
575		if ts := lastTimestamp(data); ts != "" {
576			sess.UpdatedAt = ts
577		}
578		return sess
579	}
580	
581	// parseFullSession reads a session's full data for indexing. It prefers a provider's
582	// path-keyed parse (spi.PathSessionReader) using the ref's already-known NativePath, which
583	// avoids the provider's by-id discovery search — for Codex that search walks the entire
584	// ~/.codex/sessions tree, so this is the difference between an O(N) and an O(N²) reindex.
585	// Providers without the capability (or refs lacking a NativePath) fall back to the by-id
586	// lookup. Parsing the known NativePath is also more consistent: the row's freshness
587	// fingerprint is stat'd from NativePath, so the body now comes from that same file.
588	func parseFullSession(prov spi.Provider, ref spi.GlobalSessionRef) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
589		if pr, ok := prov.(spi.PathSessionReader); ok && ref.NativePath != "" {
590			return pr.GetAgentChatSessionByPath(ref.NativePath, ref.OriginCwd, false)
591		}
592		return prov.GetAgentChatSession(ref.OriginCwd, ref.SessionID, false)
593	}
594	
595	// drainToStore writes parsed sessions to the index in batched transactions.
596	func drainToStore(store *sessionindex.Store, ch <-chan sessionindex.Session) error {
597		batch := make([]sessionindex.Session, 0, reindexWriteBatch)
598		flush := func() error {
599			if err := store.UpsertBatch(batch); err != nil {
600				return err
601			}
602			batch = batch[:0]
603			return nil
604		}
605		for sess := range ch {
606			batch = append(batch, sess)
607			if len(batch) >= reindexWriteBatch {
608				if err := flush(); err != nil {
609					return err
610				}
611			}
612		}
613		return flush()
614	}
615	
616	// ---- session field derivation ----
617	
618	// flattenBody renders SessionData to plain user/agent text for full-text indexing,
619	// reusing the reconstruction flattener (synthetic noise already stripped). No
620	// migration note is prepended — this is index content, not a resumed transcript.
621	func flattenBody(data *schema.SessionData) string {
622		turns := spi.FlattenSessionData(data, "")
623		var b strings.Builder
624		for _, t := range turns {
625			if t.Text == "" {
626				continue
627			}
628			if b.Len() > 0 {
629				b.WriteString("\n\n")
630			}
631			b.WriteString(t.Text)
632		}
633		return b.String()
634	}
635	
636	// countTurns returns (user prompts, all messages) across the session's exchanges.
637	func countTurns(data *schema.SessionData) (userTurns, totalTurns int) {
638		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
639			for _, m := range ex.Messages {
640				totalTurns++
641				if m.Role == schema.RoleUser {
642					userTurns++
643				}
644			}
645		}
646		return userTurns, totalTurns
647	}
648	
649	// lastTimestamp returns the last non-empty message timestamp in the session, or "".
650	func lastTimestamp(data *schema.SessionData) string {
651		last := ""
652		for _, ex := range data.Exchanges {
653			for _, m := range ex.Messages {
654				if m.Timestamp != "" {
655					last = m.Timestamp
656				}
657			}
658		}
659		return last
660	}
661	
662	// statNative returns the native file's size (bytes) and mtime (epoch ms), or zeros.
663	func statNative(path string) (size, mtimeMs int64) {
664		info, err := os.Stat(path)
665		if err != nil {
666			return 0, 0
667		}
668		return info.Size(), info.ModTime().UnixMilli()
669	}

673	type projectIDName struct{ id, name string }
674	
675	// projectIDCache memoizes ComputeProjectID by cwd, since many sessions share a cwd and
676	// each resolution walks the filesystem to the git root.
677	type projectIDCache struct {
678		mu sync.Mutex
679		m  map[string]projectIDName
680	}
681	
682	func (c *projectIDCache) resolve(cwd string) (string, string) {
683		if strings.TrimSpace(cwd) == "" {
684			return unknownProjectID, ""
685		}
686		c.mu.Lock()
687		defer c.mu.Unlock()
688		if v, ok := c.m[cwd]; ok {
689			return v.id, v.name
690		}
691		id, name, err := utils.ComputeProjectID(cwd)
692		if err != nil || id == "" {
693			id, name = unknownProjectID, ""
694		}
695		c.m[cwd] = projectIDName{id, name}
696		return id, name
697	}

1	-- Migration: Create Agent Sessions for Serverless-Safe Agent Registry
2	-- Date: 2026-02-03
3	-- Description: Persists agent session info in Supabase so any Vercel serverless
4	--              instance can communicate with running E2B sandboxes.
5	--              Agent sessions are scoped to collab_sessions (not arenas) to match
6	--              the LiveKit agent pattern - each collab session gets its own agent.
7	
8	-- ============================================================================
9	-- 1. Create agent_sessions table
10	-- ============================================================================
11	
12	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS agent_sessions (
13	  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
14	
15	  -- Primary relationship: collab session (one active agent per session)
16	  -- CASCADE delete ensures agent is cleaned up when session ends
17	  collab_session_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES collab_sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
18	
19	  -- Denormalized reference for RLS and arena-level lookups
20	  arena_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES arenas(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
21	
22	  -- E2B sandbox info (needed for communication)
23	  sandbox_id TEXT NOT NULL,
24	  sandbox_template TEXT,  -- e.g., 'intent-agent-v1'
25	
26	  -- Status tracking
27	  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running'
28	    CHECK (status IN ('running', 'paused', 'stopped', 'expired', 'error')),
29	
30	  -- Configuration (needed to reconstruct agent connection)
31	  intent_server_url TEXT NOT NULL,  -- The intent:// URL for CRDT sync
32	
33	  -- Who started it
34	  started_by_user_id UUID REFERENCES accounts(id),
35	  started_by_identity TEXT NOT NULL,  -- email/identity for display
36	
37	  -- Lifecycle timestamps
38	  started_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
39	  stopped_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
40	  expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ,  -- E2B sandbox expiration time
41	
42	  -- Error tracking
43	  error_message TEXT,  -- populated when status = 'error'
44	
45	  -- Standard timestamps
46	  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
47	  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
48	);

54	WHERE status IN ('running', 'paused');

24	// openOrBuildResumeIndex opens sessions.db, building it first (with the normal reindex
25	// UI) when it is missing or empty, then proceeding straight into the picker. builtFresh
26	// reports whether a full foreground build just ran — when it did, the index is already
27	// fully current, so callers skip the background warm (it would be redundant).
28	func openOrBuildResumeIndex() (store *sessionindex.Store, builtFresh bool, err error) {
29		dbPath, err := sessionindex.DefaultPath()
30		if err != nil {
31			return nil, false, err
32		}
33		if _, statErr := os.Stat(dbPath); statErr == nil {
34			s, err := sessionindex.OpenReader(dbPath)
35			if err != nil {
36				return nil, false, err
37			}
38			if n, _ := s.Count(); n > 0 {
39				return s, false, nil
40			}
41			_ = s.Close() // empty → rebuild below
42		}
43		if err := runReindex(false); err != nil {
44			return nil, false, err
45		}
46		s, err := sessionindex.OpenReader(dbPath)
47		return s, true, err
48	}

50	// indexWarmedMsg is sent to the running TUI when the background warm finishes refreshing the
51	// CURRENT project (the first warm pass). The model re-queries so new/changed sessions for this
52	// project appear without a restart. The subsequent full pass is silent (no refresh).
53	type indexWarmedMsg struct{}
54	
55	// startIndexWarm launches the background two-pass index warm for projectID, refreshing the
56	// running TUI (via p.Send) when the current-project pass completes. The returned cancel func
57	// should be invoked when the TUI exits: the warm is best-effort and must never block process
58	// exit. When builtFresh is true the index was just rebuilt in the foreground, so there is
59	// nothing to warm and this only returns a cancel func.
60	func startIndexWarm(p *tea.Program, projectID string, builtFresh bool) context.CancelFunc {
61		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
62		if builtFresh {
63			return cancel
64		}
65		dbPath, err := sessionindex.DefaultPath()
66		if err != nil {
67			slog.Debug("warm: no db path; skipping", "error", err)
68			return cancel
69		}
70		go warmIndexInBackground(ctx, dbPath, projectID, func() { p.Send(indexWarmedMsg{}) })
71		return cancel
72	}

75	// resume plan (or nil if the user cancelled). On a successful selection it persists the

77	func selectResumeViaTUI(registry *factory.Registry, store *sessionindex.Store, projectID, projectName, presetTo string, builtFresh bool) (*resumePlan, error) {
78		sessions, err := store.ListByProject(projectID)

81		}

83		// Only bail when the whole index is empty (nothing to resume anywhere).
84		if total, _ := store.Count(); total == 0 {
85			fprintln(os.Stderr, "\nNo agent sessions indexed yet. Run an agent here, then try again (or `specstory reindex`).")
86			return nil, nil

89		agents := map[string]agentMeta{}

19	// ValidateSessionData runs schema validation on SessionData when in debug mode.
20	// Validation is only performed when debugRaw is true to avoid overhead in normal operation.
21	// Returns true if validation passed or was skipped, false if validation failed.
22	func ValidateSessionData(session *spi.AgentChatSession, debugRaw bool) bool {
23		if !debugRaw || session.SessionData == nil {
24			return true
25		}
26		if !session.SessionData.Validate() {
27			slog.Warn("SessionData failed schema validation, proceeding anyway",
28				"sessionId", session.SessionID)
29			return false
30		}
31		return true
32	}

34	// WriteDebugSessionData writes debug session data when debugRaw is enabled.
35	// Logs warnings on failure but does not fail the operation.
36	func WriteDebugSessionData(session *spi.AgentChatSession, debugRaw bool) {
37		if !debugRaw || session.SessionData == nil {
38			return
39		}
40		if err := spi.WriteDebugSessionData(session.SessionID, session.SessionData); err != nil {
41			slog.Warn("Failed to write debug session data", "sessionId", session.SessionID, "error", err)
42		}
43	}

45	// FormatFilenameTimestamp formats a timestamp for use in filenames.
46	// The format is filesystem-safe and matches the markdown title format.
47	func FormatFilenameTimestamp(t time.Time, useUTC bool) string {
48		if useUTC {
49			// Use UTC with Z suffix: "2006-01-02_15-04-05Z"
50			return t.UTC().Format("2006-01-02_15-04-05") + "Z"
51		}
52		// Use local timezone with offset: "2006-01-02_15-04-05-0700"
53		return t.Local().Format("2006-01-02_15-04-05-0700")
54	}
55	
56	// BuildSessionFilePath constructs the full markdown file path for a session.
57	// All callers need consistent filename generation from session metadata.
58	func BuildSessionFilePath(session *spi.AgentChatSession, historyDir string, useUTC bool) string {
59		timestamp, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, session.CreatedAt)
60		timestampStr := FormatFilenameTimestamp(timestamp, useUTC)
61	
62		filename := timestampStr
63		if session.Slug != "" {
64			filename = fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s", timestampStr, session.Slug)
65		}
66		return filepath.Join(historyDir, filename+".md")
67	}

69	// ProcessingOptions holds flags that control session processing behavior.
70	type ProcessingOptions struct {
71		OnlyCloudSync      bool // Skip local markdown writes and only sync to cloud
72		ShowOutput         bool // Print progress to stdout
73		IsAutosave         bool // Called from run/watch (true) vs sync command (false)
74		DebugRaw           bool // Enable schema validation (only in debug mode to avoid overhead)
75		UseUTC             bool // Timestamp format: true=UTC, false=local
76		NoTelemetryPrompts bool // Exclude user prompt text from telemetry spans for privacy
77	}

79	// ProcessSingleSession writes markdown and triggers cloud sync for a single session.
80	// ctx is used for OTel trace/span propagation (no-op when telemetry is disabled).
81	// Returns the size of the markdown content in bytes.
82	func ProcessSingleSession(ctx context.Context, session *spi.AgentChatSession, config utils.OutputConfig, opts ProcessingOptions) (int, error) {
83		if session == nil || session.SessionData == nil {
84			return 0, fmt.Errorf("session or session data is nil")
85		}
86	
87		// Track processing start time for metrics
88		processingStart := time.Now()
89	
90		// Create a context with a deterministic trace ID from the session ID.
91		// This groups all spans for the same session into a single trace, even
92		// across multiple invocations in autosave mode.
93		ctx = telemetry.ContextWithSessionTrace(ctx, session.SessionID)
94	
95		// Start an OTel span for this session processing (no-op when telemetry is disabled)
96		ctx, span := telemetry.Tracer("specstory").Start(ctx, "process_session")
97		defer span.End()
98	
99		// Compute session statistics
100		agentName := session.SessionData.Provider.Name
101		stats := telemetry.ComputeSessionStats(agentName, session)
102	
103		// Record metrics (no-op when telemetry is disabled)
104		defer func() {
105			telemetry.RecordSessionMetrics(ctx, stats, time.Since(processingStart))
106		}()
107	
108		// Set session span attributes
109		telemetry.SetSessionSpanAttributes(span, stats)
110	
111		// Create child spans for each exchange
112		if len(session.SessionData.Exchanges) > 0 {
113			telemetry.ProcessExchangeSpans(ctx, stats, session.SessionData.Exchanges, opts.NoTelemetryPrompts)
114		}
115	
116		ValidateSessionData(session, opts.DebugRaw)
117		WriteDebugSessionData(session, opts.DebugRaw)
118	
119		// Generate markdown from SessionData
120		markdownContent, err := GenerateMarkdownFromAgentSession(session.SessionData, false, opts.UseUTC)
121		if err != nil {
122			slog.Error("Failed to generate markdown from SessionData", "sessionId", session.SessionID, "error", err)
123			return 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to generate markdown: %w", err)
124		}
125	
126		// Calculate markdown size in bytes
127		markdownSize := len(markdownContent)
128	
129		// Generate filename from timestamp and slug
130		fileFullPath := BuildSessionFilePath(session, config.GetHistoryDir(), opts.UseUTC)
131	
132		if opts.ShowOutput && !log.IsSilent() {
133			fmt.Printf("Processing session %s...", session.SessionID)
134		}
135	
136		// Check if file already exists with same content
137		var outcome string
138		identicalContent := false
139		fileExists := false
140		if existingContent, err := os.ReadFile(fileFullPath); err == nil {
141			fileExists = true
142			if string(existingContent) == markdownContent {
143				identicalContent = true
144				slog.Info("Markdown file already exists with same content, skipping write",
145					"sessionId", session.SessionID,
146					"path", fileFullPath)
147			}
148		}
149	
150		// Write file if needed (skip if only-cloud-sync is enabled)
151		if !opts.OnlyCloudSync {
152			if !identicalContent {
153				// Ensure history directory exists (handles deletion during long-running watch/run)
154				if err := utils.EnsureHistoryDirectoryExists(config); err != nil {
155					return 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to ensure history directory: %w", err)
156				}
157				err := os.WriteFile(fileFullPath, []byte(markdownContent), 0644)
158				if err != nil {
159					// Track write error
160					if opts.IsAutosave {
161						analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventAutosaveError, analytics.Properties{
162							"session_id":      session.SessionID,
163							"error":           err.Error(),
164							"only_cloud_sync": opts.OnlyCloudSync,
165						})
166					} else {
167						analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventSyncMarkdownError, analytics.Properties{
168							"session_id":      session.SessionID,
169							"error":           err.Error(),
170							"only_cloud_sync": opts.OnlyCloudSync,
171						})
172					}
173					return 0, fmt.Errorf("error writing markdown file: %w", err)
174				}
175	
176				// Track successful write
177				if opts.IsAutosave {
178					if !fileExists {
179						// New file created during autosave
180						analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventAutosaveNew, analytics.Properties{
181							"session_id":      session.SessionID,
182							"only_cloud_sync": opts.OnlyCloudSync,
183						})
184					} else {
185						// File updated during autosave
186						analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventAutosaveSuccess, analytics.Properties{
187							"session_id":      session.SessionID,
188							"only_cloud_sync": opts.OnlyCloudSync,
189						})
190					}
191				} else {
192					if !fileExists {
193						// New file created during manual sync
194						analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventSyncMarkdownNew, analytics.Properties{
195							"session_id":      session.SessionID,
196							"only_cloud_sync": opts.OnlyCloudSync,
197						})
198					} else {
199						// File updated during manual sync
200						analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventSyncMarkdownSuccess, analytics.Properties{
201							"session_id":      session.SessionID,
202							"only_cloud_sync": opts.OnlyCloudSync,
203						})
204					}
205				}
206	
207				slog.Info("Successfully wrote file",
208					"sessionId", session.SessionID,
209					"path", fileFullPath)
210			}
211	
212			// Determine outcome for user feedback
213			if identicalContent {
214				outcome = "up to date (skipped)"
215			} else if fileExists {
216				outcome = "updated"
217			} else {
218				outcome = "created"
219			}
220		} else {
221			// Only cloud sync mode - no local file operations
222			outcome = "synced to cloud only"
223			slog.Info("Skipping local file write (only-cloud-sync mode)",
224				"sessionId", session.SessionID)
225		}
226	
227		// Trigger cloud sync with provider-specific data
228		// In only-cloud-sync mode: always sync (no file to check for identical content)
229		// In normal mode: skip sync only if identical content AND in autosave mode
230		if opts.OnlyCloudSync || !identicalContent || !opts.IsAutosave {
231			cloud.SyncSessionToCloud(session.SessionID, fileFullPath, markdownContent, []byte(session.RawData), session.SessionData.Provider.Name, opts.IsAutosave)
232		}
233	
234		if opts.ShowOutput && !log.IsSilent() {
235			fmt.Printf(" %s\n", outcome)
236			fmt.Println() // Visual separation
237		}
238	
239		return markdownSize, nil
240	}

1	# Sessions Index (`sessions.db`)
2	
3	> **STATUS: FIRST CUT RATIFIED; LATER STAGES STRAWMAN.** The first build chunk — the
4	> `sessions.db` schema, the global-enumeration SPI method, and the `specstory reindex` command
5	> — is **agreed** and specified in
6	> [Build Plan — First Cut](#build-plan--first-cut). Everything
7	> about *keeping the index warm* (steady-state hooks, staleness, eviction) and the cloud
8	> stages remains strawman; sections still marked **OPEN** are unresolved. The reconstruction
9	> design this serves lives in [SESSION-PORTABILITY.md](SESSION-PORTABILITY.md).
10	
11	## Purpose
12	
13	`specstory resume` (cross-provider and, next, cross-project resume — see
14	[SESSION-PORTABILITY.md](SESSION-PORTABILITY.md)) needs a good selection UX: *"show me the
15	session I want to continue, wherever it came from."* For cross-project resume in
16	particular, that means surfacing sessions that originated in **other** projects, from one
17	place, with full-text search to help find them.
18	
19	Today the SPI answers only a narrower question — *"for this project dir, what sessions
20	exist?"* — by mapping a `projectPath` forward to a native store location. The resume
21	experience needs a broader, searchable view across everything we know about. `sessions.db`
22	is the proposed index that backs it.
23	
24	This doc is about **where that index lives, and WHEN entries get into it** — not the
25	column-level schema (that is deliberately deferred; see [Non-Goals](#non-goals)).
26	
27	## Decisions taken so far
28	
29	Settled in conversation:
30	
31	- **One global index, not per-project.** A single machine-level `sessions.db`
32	  (`~/.specstory/sessions.db`, no leading dot — matches its sibling `lore.db`) indexes
33	  sessions from every project, each row tagged with `project_id`. Cross-project resume's
34	  defining need is to see across projects from one place; a per-project index would force a
35	  full-disk discovery + N-database union at every pick, and a per-project index file inside
36	  `.specstory/` is either a privacy leak (if committed) or doesn't travel (if gitignored) —
37	  so it earns nothing.
38	- **Separate from `lore.db`.** Lore keeps its own corpus (`~/.specstory/lore.db`), with its
39	  own `PARSER_VERSION` cadence, fed by parsing rendered markdown. `sessions.db` is a new,
40	  independent database fed by the Go providers from raw native session data. Different
41	  inputs, different lifecycles — coupling them would couple two unrelated version cadences.
42	  They can still share discovery and the project-identity code.
43	- **Command surface: `specstory reindex` (top-level).** The full cold sweep is its own
44	  top-level command, *not* a subcommand of `resume`. The existing interactive picker stays
45	  `specstory resume`. `sessions.db` is an internal implementation-detail name — neither command
46	  is renamed to `restore`.
47	- **No new dependency.** SQLite is already vendored: `modernc.org/sqlite` (pure Go), used by
48	  the Cursor reader and `pkg/provenance/store.go`. `sessions.db` mirrors the provenance house
49	  style (`database/sql` + a `file:…?_pragma=busy_timeout=…&_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)` DSN +
50	  perf pragmas) — **not** lore's `node:sqlite` (lore is a separate Node skill; nothing shared
51	  at the code level).
52	- **First cut indexes full-body full-text, for all six providers.** `reindex` parses each
53	  session's full `SessionData` and indexes the entire conversation body into FTS5 (not a
54	  metadata-only sweep), and every provider implements the global enumerator from day one. See
55	  [Build Plan — First Cut](#build-plan--first-cut).
56	
57	## Guiding principle: `sessions.db` is a derived cache
58	
59	The authoritative source of truth is, and stays, the **native session stores**. `sessions.db`
60	is a **cache** over them. Two consequences drive the rest of this design:
61	
62	1. **It must be fully rebuildable from scratch at any time.** Deleting it is always safe.
63	2. **Incremental population is an optimization, never the only path.** If the only way data
64	   got in were live SpecStory events, any session we failed to witness would be missing
65	   *forever*. Because catchup can always rebuild, gaps are transient, not permanent.
66	
67	## Project identity: reuse the algorithm, NOT the stored files
68	
69	`pkg/utils/project_identity.go` already defines the identity *algorithm* this index needs:
70	
71	- `git_id` = `sha256(normalized origin remote URL)` → `xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx`. Derived from the
72	  remote, so it is **stable across directory, machine, and user** — the cross-project /
73	  cross-machine join key.
74	- `workspace_id` = `sha256(absolute path)` — machine-local fallback for repos with no remote.
75	
76	What is **already solved** is identity across *clones / machines*: two checkouts of the same
77	remote both compute the same `git_id` (verified — two clones of one repo, differing
78	`workspace_id`s, identical `git_id`).
79	
80	What is **NOT solved by the stored files** is the monorepo case, and this is the trap to avoid.
81	`EnsureProjectIdentity` / `generateGitID` look for `.git/config` at *exactly* the project root
82	they were given and **never walk up**. So when an agent runs from a subdirectory of a repo, the
83	written `.specstory/.project.json` there has **no `git_id`** and a fresh, path-based
84	`workspace_id` — three launch directories in one repo (`/`, `/a`, `/b`) produce three different
85	identities. **Reading the nearest stored `.project.json` would therefore *fragment* one
86	monorepo into many projects.**
87	
88	**Resolution strategy for `sessions.db` (the new part — Build Plan step 1).** Identity is
89	computed fresh per session by `ComputeProjectID(cwd)`, which **walks up from the session's cwd
90	to the git root**, computes `git_id` from *that* root's remote, and **ignores any per-directory
91	`.project.json`**. From `/a` it walks up, finds the repo's `.git`, and yields the same `git_id`
92	as `/`. Root, `/a`, `/b` all collapse to one project — which is the monorepo behavior we want.
93	It also computes `workspace_id` from the **walked-up root**, not the launch subdir, so even a
94	remote-less monorepo's subdirectories share one identity on a given machine.
95	
96	**Caveats to keep honest:**
97	
98	- **Remote-less repos** still don't cross machines: walk-up finds `.git` but no origin, so
99	  there is no `git_id`, only the path-based `workspace_id`. Subdirectories collapse (shared
100	  root), but the project is machine-local. A real constraint for the later cross-machine /
101	  cross-user stages.
102	- **No `.git` anywhere up the tree** has no natural root and genuinely fragments; that is the
103	  irreducible case.
104	
105	`project_id` (the resolved `git_id`, else `workspace_id`) is the same vocabulary the cloud sync
106	and Lore speak, so the index, the cloud, and Lore share one identity space.
107	
108	**The writer is fixed too, not just sessions.db.** To avoid maintaining two divergent identity
109	strategies, the existing `EnsureProjectIdentity` writer is switched onto the same walk-up core
110	(Build Plan step 1), so the stored `.specstory/.project.json` files stop fragmenting. The cloud
111	groups sessions by `project_id`, so monorepo-subdir sessions consequently regroup under the
112	repo's project. That is **intended and desirable**; the rare case of a previously-synced subdir
113	session "moving" cloud project is an accepted edge case, not a concern.
114	
115	## When do entries get into `sessions.db`?
116	
117	Two modes: **steady state** (warm, incremental) and **catchup** (cold, full rebuild).
118	
119	### Steady state — incremental upsert at every sighting
120	
121	The commands that already parse sessions upsert into `sessions.db` as a side effect. They
122	already hold a parsed `SessionData`, so they can populate the metadata row **and** the
123	full-text content in one shot, for free:
124	
125	- `specstory sync` — every session it processes.
126	- `specstory run` / `specstory watch` — every session update the watcher sees.
127	- `specstory resume` — a **double write**: re-index the source session, and index the
128	  freshly reconstructed target session so it is itself resumable next time.
129	
130	### The witness gap — and why more hooks don't close it
131	
132	Event-driven population only sees sessions specstory was attached to. An agent session run
133	without specstory will be absent. **This gap cannot be closed by adding more event points** —
134	there is always a session we didn't witness. The gap-closer is the catchup scan (below), run
135	opportunistically (e.g. when `reindex` finds the index stale or empty), not an ever-growing
136	list of hooks. The reframe: the gap is something the periodic scan *sweeps up*, not a hole we
137	must plug live.
138	
139	### Catchup — cold rebuild / explicit reindex
140	
141	Triggered explicitly by the user via `specstory reindex` (and, in a later chunk, automatically
142	when `sessions.db` is missing or detected stale). This is the path that enumerates *everything*
143	and is the reason for the new SPI capability below — and it is the **entirety of the first
144	cut** ([Build Plan](#build-plan--first-cut)): the only population path that exists initially.
145	
146	## The missing SPI capability: project-*discovering* enumeration
147	
148	Today's listing is project-**scoped**: `projectPath → store location → sessions`. Catchup
149	needs the inverse — enumerate **every** native session, then **discover** which project each
150	belongs to. The project becomes an *output*, not an input.
151	
152	That changes the return shape. A global enumeration must surface each session's **originating
153	cwd**, because the cwd is the only thing that lets the CLI attribute the session to a
154	`project_id`. Identity resolution stays in the CLI (one source of truth) via the new
155	read-only `ComputeProjectID(cwd)` helper (see [Build Plan](#build-plan--first-cut)) — providers
156	surface the cwd, they do not compute `project_id`.
157	
158	Signature (ratified for the first cut):
159	
160	```go
161	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every session in this provider's native store,
162	// regardless of project. Unlike ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath), the project is not an
163	// input — each returned ref carries the originating cwd so the caller can resolve project
164	// identity. Lightweight: metadata + cwd only, no full SessionData parse (reindex re-fetches
165	// full data per ref via the existing GetAgentChatSession(originCwd, sessionID)).
166	ListAllAgentChatSessions() ([]GlobalSessionRef, error)
167	
168	type GlobalSessionRef struct {
169	    SessionID  string // native session id (uuid)
170	    CreatedAt  string // ISO 8601
171	    Slug       string // human-readable, filename-safe
172	    Name       string // human-readable description (may be empty)
173	    NativePath string // absolute path to the native session file
174	    OriginCwd  string // working dir the session was launched from (→ project_id)
175	}
176	```
177	
178	**cwd is always read from *inside* the session file — uniformly, for every provider.** Claude
179	Code writes `cwd` on every JSONL record; Codex writes it in the `session_meta` record. The
180	store's *directory* is at best a hint and at worst misleading:
181	
182	- **Claude Code** — store dir is `~/.claude/projects/<cwd-encoded>/`, but the encoding
183	  (`encodeProjectDirName`) replaces *every* non-alphanumeric character with a dash and is
184	  therefore **lossy and not reversible** — do **not** try to decode cwd from the directory
185	  name; read the record `cwd`. Enumerate all project dirs, read each session's `cwd`.
186	- **Codex CLI** — sessions live under `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/`, **not** project-keyed
187	  at all; cwd is inside the rollout `session_meta`. Proof that "the project is a property
188	  discovered from the session," not from its location. The existing project-scoped listing is
189	  already a global walk filtered by cwd (`findCodexSessions`) — the enumerator is that walk
190	  with the filter removed.
191	- **Gemini, Droid, DeepSeek, Cursor** — each has its own layout; same contract: return
192	  sessions + the cwd recorded inside each.
193	
194	## Monorepos: `git_id` dissolves most of it
195	
196	Because `git_id` hashes the *remote*, any cwd inside a repo boundary — child, peer, or parent
197	directory — resolves to the **same** `git_id` once we walk up to `.git` and read origin. So
198	sessions launched from different directories of one monorepo attribute to one project
199	automatically, *provided we resolve each session's cwd to its git root*.
200	
201	Sharp consequence: the cwd-scoped store lookup is **too narrow even for the current project**
202	— a session launched from a sibling directory of the same repo lives under a *different*
203	encoded store dir and a project-scoped list misses it. So "all sessions for THIS project" in a
204	monorepo is best answered by **enumerate-all-then-filter-by-`git_id`** — the same global
205	primitive — not by the forward store lookup. The new capability is therefore not only a
206	catchup tool; it is also the correct primitive for the monorepo current-project view.
207	
208	Still fragments: remote-less directories (only `workspace_id`, which is path-based). Flagged,
209	not solved.
210	
211	## Two fill-levels (a future optimization, not the first cut)
212	
213	The index has two natural fill-levels:
214	
215	1. **Existence + metadata** — `project_id`, `uuid`, `agent`, `date`, `slug`, native path.
216	   Obtainable cheaply from the global enumeration (no `SessionData` parse). Enough to *browse
217	   and pick*.
218	2. **Content / full-text** — requires parsing `SessionData`.
219	
220	**First-cut decision: `reindex` does both at once — it parses full `SessionData` and indexes
221	the whole conversation body into FTS5.** A *first* index of a session is therefore a full
222	parse, not a cheap metadata sweep; full-body search is the UX we want from day one.
223	
224	**`reindex` is incremental, though.** It loads every indexed session's freshness fingerprint
225	(`size + mtime + index_version`) up front and **skips any session whose native file is
226	unchanged and was indexed by the current logic version** — exactly Lore's idempotency contract.
227	So the *first* run is a full parse, but re-runs only touch new/changed sessions (verified:
228	~20s → ~2s with most sessions unchanged). `--force` re-indexes everything; bumping
229	`index_version` (when parse/derivation logic changes) auto-invalidates every row. The cheap
230	metadata-only enumeration still runs every time (it's how sessions are discovered), but the
231	expensive full parse is gated by the fingerprint.
232	
233	The two-level split also keeps the index warm *without* an explicit `reindex`, two ways:
234	
235	- **`resume`/`search` background warm.** While the picker is open, a background goroutine
236	  (`warmIndexInBackground`) runs the same incremental engine over its own writer handle in two
237	  silent passes — the **current project first** (so its rows refresh almost immediately, and the
238	  open TUI re-queries via `indexWarmedMsg`), then the **full corpus**. It reuses the exact
239	  `enumerateAll` → `dedupRefs` → `selectWork` → `processWork` engine the foreground `reindex`
240	  uses (only the progress reporter differs: live bars vs. a silent `nopReporter`). It is
241	  cancelled the instant the TUI exits and never blocks process exit — an abandoned write batch
242	  is safe under WAL. It is skipped when the index was just built fresh in the foreground (see
243	  `openOrBuildResumeIndex` → `builtFresh`).
244	
245	- **Real-time upserts from `watch`/`run`/`resume`-launch.** These already write a markdown file
246	  on every detected session change; a `LiveIndexer` (held for the command's lifetime) mirrors
247	  each change into the index with a single-row `Upsert`, reusing the same content derivation
248	  (`flattenBody`/`countTurns`/`lastTimestamp`). The project is resolved once (a watch/run has a
249	  fixed cwd); repeat callbacks with no new activity are skipped. A live row carries **no
250	  native-file fingerprint** (Size/Mtime/NativePath are unknown without enumerating), so the next
251	  `reindex`/warm re-verifies and rewrites it with a stable fingerprint — the live row is correct
252	  and queryable in the interim. All of it is best-effort: indexing never disrupts the agent or
253	  the markdown write (a nil `LiveIndexer` is a safe no-op; per-update errors log at debug).
254	
255	- **`sync` indexes as it goes.** `sync`/`sync <provider>`/`sync -s` already load every session's
256	  full `SessionData` for the current project, so each is `Record`ed into the index via the same
257	  `LiveIndexer` — indexing is essentially free there. `--print` (stdout, no save) is excluded.
258

311	### Reindex Concurrency Model
312	
313	The hot path is the per-session full parse (`GetAgentChatSession` → `SessionData` → flatten
314	body, count turns, derive timestamps). Each session is an independent, read-only parse of its
315	own native file — embarrassingly parallel. `reindex` runs a **3-stage streaming pipeline**:
316	
317	```
318	enumerate (6 providers, parallel)  →  parse+build (bounded worker pool)  →  write (1 goroutine)
319	      cheap, independent                  the hot CPU+IO fan-out             SQLite single-writer
320	```
321	
322	- **Enumerate** — the six `ListAllAgentChatSessions()` run concurrently; each walks its own
323	  store. Cheap, and lets parsing start streaming before enumeration finishes.
324	- **Parse + build** — a bounded worker pool (`min(NumCPU, ~8–12)`) over all refs. Workers are
325	  pure `ref → sessionindex.Session`. A per-session parse failure is logged and skipped, never aborts
326	  the sweep.
327	- **Write** — a *single* writer goroutine drains a channel and upserts in **batched
328	  transactions** (commit every ~200 rows). SQLite is single-writer (`MaxOpenConns=1`), so this
329	  serializes anyway; batching avoids thousands of tiny WAL commits — the main perf lever after
330	  parse concurrency.
331	
332	**Streaming, not collect-then-write:** session bodies are large (1–5 MB each), so parsed
333	sessions stream parse → FTS-index → discard; we never retain a body after its upsert, keeping
334	memory bounded.
335	
336	**`cwd → project_id` cache.** Many sessions share a cwd (same project), and `ComputeProjectID`
337	walks the filesystem to the git root each call. A mutex-guarded `map[cwd]projectID` (or a
338	pre-pass over the unique cwd set) eliminates the redundant walks.
339	
340	**Provider concurrency-safety** is a precondition: `GetAgentChatSession` is called from N
341	goroutines, so the providers' parse paths must hold no shared mutable state. Audited before
342	implementation (providers are effectively stateless; per-call caches like Cursor's
343	`MessageTimestampCache` are local).
344	
345	**No cross-provider barrier in this cut.** The deferred Cursor cwd recovery (above) *will*
346	introduce one (collect all other cwds before md5-matching Cursor); until then the pipeline is
347	fully streaming.
348	
349	### Reindex Progress UX
350	
351	`reindex` aims for a world-class, engaging readout. All progress goes to **stderr** (stdout
352	reserved for a future `--emit json`); the renderer is **TTY-aware**. Three moments:
353	
354	1. **Discover** (instant — enumeration is fast and runs first):
355	
356	   ```
357	   🔍  Scanning 6 agents…
358	   ✓   Found 822 sessions  ·  claude 683 · codex 70 · cursor 49 · droid 16 · deepseek 3 · gemini 1
359	   ```
360	
361	2. **Index** (the long parse phase) — a **multi-line, in-place per-agent progress block**, one
362	   bar per agent ticking independently, plus an aggregate header:
363	
364	   ```
365	   Indexing  512/822 · 23 projects · 130/s
366	
367	     claude   ▕███████████░░░▏ 470/683
368	     codex    ▕██████████████▏  70/70 ✓
369	     cursor   ▕████░░░░░░░░░░▏  12/49
370	     droid    ▕██████████████▏  16/16 ✓
371	     deepseek ▕██████████████▏   3/3  ✓
372	     gemini   ▕██████████████▏   1/1  ✓
373	   ```
374	
375	   Implementation: workers bump **atomic per-agent counters**; a single render goroutine ticks
376	   (~10 Hz) and redraws the block in place via ANSI cursor-up. The distinct-project counter is a
377	   mutex-guarded set. No worker draws directly (avoids interleaving). Fixed-width bars; no color
378	   dependency.
379	
380	3. **Summary** — a clean, scannable final block, honest about gaps:
381	
382	   ```
383	   ✓   Indexed 822 sessions into ~/.specstory/sessions.db  (6.1s)
384	
385	         claude 683   codex 70   cursor 49   droid 16   deepseek 3   gemini 1
386	
387	         31 projects  ·  49 unattributed
388	   ```
389	
390	**Non-TTY fallback** (piped / CI): no ANSI, no spinner — periodic plain `indexed N/822…` lines
391	plus the same final summary, so logs stay clean.
392	
393	## Schema
394	
395	`~/.specstory/sessions.db`. Two tables.
396	
397	### `sessions` — one row per known session
398	
399	| Column          | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                            |
400	|-----------------|---------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
401	| `project_id`    | TEXT    | Resolved identity (walk-up `git_id`, else `workspace_id`). The value the cloud groups by and Lore speaks. Indexed.                                     |
402	| `project_name`  | TEXT    | Human-readable project name (repo name from the walked-up root).                                                                                       |
403	| `agent`         | TEXT    | Provider id: `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `droid`, `deepseek`, `cursor`. Part of the primary key.                                                      |
404	| `session_id`    | TEXT    | Native session id (uuid). Part of the primary key.                                                                                                     |
405	| `created_at`    | TEXT    | ISO 8601 session creation timestamp (first turn). Powers the "Created" sort.                                                                           |
406	| `updated_at`    | TEXT    | ISO 8601 last-activity timestamp (last turn, else file mtime). Powers "X ago", the "Updated" sort, and resume-last.                                    |
407	| `user_turns`    | INTEGER | Count of user prompts — the headline "how much work is here" signal.                                                                                   |
408	| `total_turns`   | INTEGER | Count of all messages (user + agent). Computed alongside `user_turns`.                                                                                 |
409	| `slug`          | TEXT    | Filename-safe slug derived from the first user message.                                                                                                |
410	| `name`          | TEXT    | Human-readable session description (may be empty).                                                                                                     |
411	| `native_path`   | TEXT    | Absolute path the provider opens to read this session — a JSONL/JSON file for most agents, or a per-session `store.db` for Cursor. Unique per session. |
412	| `origin_cwd`    | TEXT    | Working directory the session was launched from (the input to identity resolution).                                                                    |
413	| `size`          | INTEGER | Native file size in bytes — part of the freshness fingerprint (incremental-skip on re-run).                                                            |
414	| `mtime`         | INTEGER | Native file modification time, epoch ms — part of the freshness fingerprint.                                                                           |
415	| `index_version` | INTEGER | reindex logic version that wrote the row — part of the fingerprint; bumping it forces a full re-parse.                                                 |
416	| `indexed_at`    | TEXT    | ISO 8601 time this row was last written by `reindex`.                                                                                                  |
417	| `fts_rowid`     | INTEGER | rowid of this session's `sessions_fts` row — the O(1) link used to read the body and to delete-before-insert without scanning the FTS (see below). NULL on rows written before this column existed, until a `reindex` repopulates them. |
418	
419	Primary key: `(agent, session_id)` — a session is unique within a provider, and belongs to
420	exactly one project. `project_id` is indexed for per-project filtering. `created_at` /
421	`updated_at` / `user_turns` / `total_turns` come from the full `SessionData` parse `reindex`
422	already performs; the rest come from the lightweight enumeration ref.
423	
424	**Considered and deliberately excluded (first cut):**
425	
426	- **Git branch.** Claude Code records `gitBranch` per turn (stable within a session), but Codex
427	  and the others record nothing — a half-populated, Claude-only column isn't worth it yet. If
428	  added later it belongs on the enumeration ref as native metadata, *not* in neutral
429	  `SessionData`.
430	- **User naming / rename.** No `custom_name`; sessions are not renameable in the first cut.
431	  Keeps `sessions` a purely rebuildable cache (no user-authoritative fields to preserve across
432	  `reindex`).
433	- **Lineage.** No `source_session_id`. The breadcrumb already exists natively for free —
434	  reconstruction writes `specstorySourceSessionId` (the source session id) into the rebuilt
435	  file's meta (`claudecode`/`codexcli`/`droidcli` `reconstruct.go`) — so it can be surfaced
436	  later (ideally also capturing the source *agent*, which that field does not) when fork/resume
437	  lineage UX is actually designed.
438	
439	### `sessions_fts` — FTS5 full-text index (kept in tandem with `sessions`)
440	
441	| Column       | In FTS index?    | Description                                                                                     |
442	|--------------|------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
443	| `session_id` | No (`UNINDEXED`) | Join key back to `sessions`; stored in the row but not tokenized.                               |
444	| `agent`      | No (`UNINDEXED`) | Join key back to `sessions`; stored in the row but not tokenized.                               |
445	| `name`       | Yes              | Session description / first-message-derived name; tokenized + searchable.                       |
446	| `body`       | Yes              | Full conversation text — the reconstruction-flattened user/agent turns; tokenized + searchable. |
447	
448	`UNINDEXED` is an FTS5 per-column keyword meaning the column is **stored but excluded from the
449	full-text index** — not "lacks a b-tree index" (FTS5 tables have no secondary b-tree indexes at
450	all). The two join keys ride along in the row so a `MATCH` hit maps straight back to its
451	`sessions` row without a separate lookup table. Default FTS5 tokenizer. Rows are
452	inserted/replaced alongside their `sessions` row during
453	`reindex`; deletion of a `sessions` row removes its `sessions_fts` row.
454	
455	**Reaching a *specific* FTS row is by `fts_rowid`, never by the join keys.** Because
456	`session_id`/`agent` are `UNINDEXED`, a point query like `WHERE agent=? AND session_id=?`
457	against `sessions_fts` has nothing to seek on and **scans the entire table** — fine for a
458	`MATCH` search (which uses the full-text index), O(N) for a single-row lookup. So the writer
459	stores each FTS row's rowid on its `sessions` row (`fts_rowid`) at insert time
460	(`last_insert_rowid()`), and:
461	
462	- **Body reads** (`SessionBody`, the preview pane) join `sessions_fts ON rowid = sessions.fts_rowid`,
463	  an O(1) rowid lookup, with a one-time fallback to the by-key scan for rows whose `fts_rowid`
464	  is still NULL (written before the column existed; a `reindex` retires the fallback).
465	- **Replace-before-insert** deletes the prior FTS row by `WHERE rowid = ?` rather than by the
466	  UNINDEXED keys. Brand-new sessions skip the lookup+delete entirely (`Session.IsNew`), since
467	  there is no prior row.
468	
469	This is why the body lookup and the per-row delete stay O(1) as the index grows into the tens of
470	thousands of rows, instead of each becoming a full-table scan.
471	
472	## Non-Goals (first cut)
473	
474	- **The picker rewiring.** `specstory resume`'s interactive flow still uses the project-scoped
475	  `ListAgentChatSessions` until a later chunk points it at `sessions.db`.
476	- **Storing serialized `SessionData`.** The first cut stores metadata + full-text body, not a
477	  `SessionData` blob. A blob becomes relevant for cloud Stages 3–4 (where the cloud is the
478	  source). Deferred.
479	
480	## Deferred — DO NEXT (Cursor cwd recovery)
481	
482	Cursor CLI sessions are currently enumerated with `OriginCwd=""` and therefore indexed
483	under the **`unknown` project_id**. This is a first-cut shortcut, not the end state — it is
484	the immediate follow-up after the `reindex` first cut.
485	
486	Cursor stores sessions at `~/.cursor/chats/<projectHash>/<sessionID>/store.db`, where
487	`projectHash = md5(canonical project path)` (`cursorcli/path_utils.go` `GetProjectHashDir`),
488	and records no workspace path inside the store. md5 is one-way, but the hash is embedded in
489	`GlobalSessionRef.NativePath` (two directories up from `store.db`). **Recovery plan:** the
490	`reindex` orchestrator builds `map[md5(canonicalize(cwd))]cwd` from every *other* provider's
491	cwds (optionally augmented by a filesystem scan for git/`.specstory` roots), then matches each
492	Cursor ref's `projectHash` to recover its cwd → resolve `project_id` via `ComputeProjectID`.
493	Unmatched Cursor sessions remain `unknown`. (Tracked in memory: `restore-cursor-cwd-deferred`.)
494	
495	## Open questions (later chunks)
496	
497	- **DONE — Warm-keeping triggers.** `resume`/`search` warm the index in the background on launch
498	  (current project first, then full corpus); `watch`/`run`/`resume`-launch upsert each change in
499	  real time via `LiveIndexer`; and `sync` indexes every session it loads (all via the same
500	  `LiveIndexer`). See "keeping the index warm" above and [RESUME-TUI.md](RESUME-TUI.md). Possible
501	  follow-up: throttle repeated background warms (today every `resume`/`search` invocation
502	  re-enumerates, which is cheap but unbounded in frequency).
503	- **OPEN — Eviction / prune.** When a native session is deleted, when does its row leave
504	  `sessions.db`? (Lore prunes on rescan when the file is gone.)
505	- **OPEN — Remote-less projects.** How (if at all) cross-project / cross-machine works for
506	  repos with only a `workspace_id`.
507	
508	## Related Documents
509	
510	- [SESSION-PORTABILITY.md](SESSION-PORTABILITY.md) — the reconstruction / resume design this
511	  index serves.
512	- [PROVIDER-SPI.md](PROVIDER-SPI.md) — the provider interface the new enumeration method joins.
513	- `pkg/utils/project_identity.go` — `git_id` / `workspace_id` / `GetProjectID()`.
514

1	package spi

3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"log/slog"
6		"os"
7		"path/filepath"
8		"runtime"
9		"sync"

12	
13	// GlobalSessionRef is a lightweight, project-discovering reference to a single
14	// native session, returned by Provider.ListAllAgentChatSessions.
15	//
16	// Unlike the project-scoped ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath), the project is NOT
17	// an input here: each ref carries the originating working directory (read from inside
18	// the session) so the caller — the `specstory reindex` command — can resolve project
19	// identity with utils.ComputeProjectID. The project is discovered, not supplied.
20	//
21	// It is intentionally metadata-only (no full SessionData parse); reindex re-fetches
22	// full data per ref via GetAgentChatSession(OriginCwd, SessionID) when it needs the
23	// conversation body. See docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
24	type GlobalSessionRef struct {
25		SessionID  string // native session id (uuid)
26		CreatedAt  string // ISO 8601 creation timestamp (first turn), may be empty
27		Slug       string // filename-safe slug derived from the first user message
28		Name       string // human-readable description (may be empty)
29		NativePath string // absolute path the provider opens to read this session
30		OriginCwd  string // working directory the session was launched from (-> project_id)
31	}
32	
33	// PathSessionReader is an OPTIONAL capability a Provider may implement: parse a single
34	// session directly from its already-known native file path, skipping the by-id discovery
35	// search that GetAgentChatSession performs.
36	//
37	// Why: some providers locate a session by scanning their native store. Codex's by-id
38	// lookup walks the entire ~/.codex/sessions tree on every call, so resolving N sessions
39	// that way is O(N²). reindex already holds each session's exact file path
40	// (GlobalSessionRef.NativePath) from enumeration, so a path-keyed parse turns that back
41	// into O(N). reindex prefers this when a provider implements it and the ref carries a
42	// NativePath, and falls back to GetAgentChatSession otherwise.
43	//
44	// originCwd is the session's originating working directory (GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd),
45	// passed through as the workspace root for path normalization — matching what
46	// GetAgentChatSession receives as projectPath.
47	type PathSessionReader interface {
48		GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath string, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*AgentChatSession, error)
49	}
50	
51	// ScanReporter accumulates a provider's enumeration progress (sessions found) so the CLI can
52	// render a live "scanning" display. It is safe for concurrent use and safe to call on a nil
53	// receiver (a no-op), so providers can report unconditionally.
54	type ScanReporter struct {
55		found atomic.Int64
56	}
57	
58	// Add records that n more sessions have been found. Files that yield no session (warmup-only or
59	// sidechain-only transcripts) are deliberately not counted, so the running total reflects real
60	// sessions rather than raw files.
61	func (r *ScanReporter) Add(n int) {
62		if r != nil {
63			r.found.Add(int64(n))
64		}
65	}
66	
67	// Found returns the number of sessions found so far.
68	func (r *ScanReporter) Found() int64 {
69		if r == nil {
70			return 0
71		}
72		return r.found.Load()
73	}
74	
75	// ProgressEnumerator is an OPTIONAL Provider capability: enumerate all sessions while reporting
76	// scan progress into r (which may be nil — ScanReporter is nil-safe, so report unconditionally).
77	// Providers that don't implement it are enumerated via ListAllAgentChatSessions with no live
78	// feedback. reindex uses this to render a per-agent "Scanning agents…" display.
79	type ProgressEnumerator interface {
80		ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *ScanReporter) ([]GlobalSessionRef, error)
81	}
82	
83	// ScanSessionsInParallel walks root for *.jsonl session files and scans each one concurrently
84	// with scan, returning the collected refs. It is the shared engine behind each provider's
85	// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress: providers differ only in where their sessions live (root)
86	// and how a single file's header maps to a GlobalSessionRef (scan).
87	//
88	// scan returns (ref, nil) to include a session, (nil, nil) to skip a non-session file
89	// (warmup-only / empty / sidechain-only), or (nil, err) to log-and-skip a malformed file.
90	// Files are independent and the per-file read+parse is CPU-bound, so scanning fans out across
91	// CPUs; output order is unspecified (reindex dedups and sorts later). r counts sessions found
92	// (not files scanned) and is nil-safe. label names the provider in scan-failure logs.
93	func ScanSessionsInParallel(root, label string, r *ScanReporter, scan func(path string) (*GlobalSessionRef, error)) ([]GlobalSessionRef, error) {
94		// Phase 1: collect file paths (dirents only — no opens).
95		var paths []string
96		walkErr := filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, d os.DirEntry, err error) error {
97			if err != nil {
98				return nil // skip unreadable entries rather than abort the whole sweep
99			}
100			if d.IsDir() || filepath.Ext(path) != ".jsonl" {
101				return nil
102			}
103			paths = append(paths, path)
104			return nil
105		})
106		if walkErr != nil {
107			return nil, fmt.Errorf("walking %s sessions: %w", label, walkErr)
108		}
109	
110		// Phase 2: scan headers in parallel. min(NumCPU, 12) is always ≥ 1, so no lower-bound guard.
111		workers := min(runtime.NumCPU(), 12)
112		pathCh := make(chan string, workers)
113		refs := make([]GlobalSessionRef, 0, len(paths))
114		var mu sync.Mutex
115		var wg sync.WaitGroup
116		for i := 0; i < workers; i++ {
117			wg.Add(1)
118			go func() {
119				defer wg.Done()
120				for path := range pathCh {
121					ref, scanErr := safeScan(scan, path)
122					if scanErr != nil {
123						slog.Warn("reindex: failed to scan session", "agent", label, "path", path, "error", scanErr)
124						continue
125					}
126					if ref == nil {
127						continue // not a session (warmup / empty / sidechain)
128					}
129					mu.Lock()
130					refs = append(refs, *ref)
131					mu.Unlock()
132					r.Add(1) // count sessions found, not files scanned
133				}
134			}()
135		}
136		for _, path := range paths {
137			pathCh <- path
138		}
139		close(pathCh)
140		wg.Wait()
141		return refs, nil
142	}
143	
144	// safeScan runs scan(path), converting a panic into an error so one malformed session file is
145	// logged and skipped (via the caller's normal error path) rather than crashing the whole sweep.
146	func safeScan(scan func(string) (*GlobalSessionRef, error), path string) (ref *GlobalSessionRef, err error) {
147		defer func() {
148			if r := recover(); r != nil {
149				ref, err = nil, fmt.Errorf("panic scanning session: %v", r)
150			}
151		}()
152		return scan(path)
153	}
154

45	// FormatFilenameTimestamp formats a timestamp for use in filenames.
46	// The format is filesystem-safe and matches the markdown title format.
47	func FormatFilenameTimestamp(t time.Time, useUTC bool) string {
48		if useUTC {
49			// Use UTC with Z suffix: "2006-01-02_15-04-05Z"
50			return t.UTC().Format("2006-01-02_15-04-05") + "Z"
51		}
52		// Use local timezone with offset: "2006-01-02_15-04-05-0700"
53		return t.Local().Format("2006-01-02_15-04-05-0700")
54	}

56	// BuildSessionFilePath constructs the full markdown file path for a session.
57	// All callers need consistent filename generation from session metadata.
58	func BuildSessionFilePath(session *spi.AgentChatSession, historyDir string, useUTC bool) string {
59		timestamp, _ := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, session.CreatedAt)
60		timestampStr := FormatFilenameTimestamp(timestamp, useUTC)
61	
62		filename := timestampStr
63		if session.Slug != "" {
64			filename = fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s", timestampStr, session.Slug)
65		}
66		return filepath.Join(historyDir, filename+".md")
67	}

114	// calculateTimedOut computes the number of sessions that timed out during sync.
115	// This is calculated as: attempted - (skipped + updated + created + errored)
116	// Includes defensive validation to prevent negative values in case of counter bugs.
117	func (stats *CloudSyncStats) calculateTimedOut() {
118		finished := stats.SessionsSkipped + stats.SessionsUpdated + stats.SessionsCreated + stats.SessionsErrored
119	
120		// Defensive validation: finished should never exceed attempted
121		if finished > stats.SessionsAttempted {
122			slog.Error("CloudSyncStats counter inconsistency detected",
123				"attempted", stats.SessionsAttempted,
124				"finished", finished,
125				"skipped", stats.SessionsSkipped,
126				"updated", stats.SessionsUpdated,
127				"created", stats.SessionsCreated,
128				"errored", stats.SessionsErrored)
129			stats.SessionsTimedOut = 0
130			return
131		}
132	
133		stats.SessionsTimedOut = stats.SessionsAttempted - finished
134	}

166	// incrementCategory atomically increments the counter for a given category
167	func (stats *CloudSyncStats) incrementCategory(category syncCategory) {
168		switch category {
169		case categorySkipped:
170			atomic.AddInt32(&stats.SessionsSkipped, 1)
171		case categoryErrored:
172			atomic.AddInt32(&stats.SessionsErrored, 1)
173		case categoryUpdated:
174			atomic.AddInt32(&stats.SessionsUpdated, 1)
175		case categoryCreated:
176			atomic.AddInt32(&stats.SessionsCreated, 1)
177		}
178	}
179	
180	// decrementCategory atomically decrements the counter for a given category
181	func (stats *CloudSyncStats) decrementCategory(category syncCategory) {
182		switch category {
183		case categorySkipped:
184			atomic.AddInt32(&stats.SessionsSkipped, -1)
185		case categoryErrored:
186			atomic.AddInt32(&stats.SessionsErrored, -1)
187		case categoryUpdated:
188			atomic.AddInt32(&stats.SessionsUpdated, -1)
189		case categoryCreated:
190			atomic.AddInt32(&stats.SessionsCreated, -1)
191		}
192	}

194	// shouldReplaceCategory determines if newCategory should replace oldCategory based on precedence
195	// Precedence (highest to lowest): created > updated > errored > skipped
196	func shouldReplaceCategory(oldCategory, newCategory syncCategory) bool {
197		// Created never gets replaced
198		if oldCategory == categoryCreated {
199			return false
200		}
201		// Updated replaces skipped and errored
202		if newCategory == categoryUpdated {
203			return oldCategory == categorySkipped || oldCategory == categoryErrored
204		}
205		// Errored replaces only skipped
206		if newCategory == categoryErrored {
207			return oldCategory == categorySkipped
208		}
209		// Created replaces everything (but we already handled oldCategory == created above)
210		if newCategory == categoryCreated {
211			return true
212		}
213		// Skipped doesn't replace anything
214		return false
215	}

217	// trackSessionInCategory records a session in a category and updates counters atomically
218	// Handles precedence rules and automatically increments/decrements appropriate counters
219	func (stats *CloudSyncStats) trackSessionInCategory(sessionID string, newCategory syncCategory) {
220		for {
221			// Try to load existing category
222			existing, loaded := stats.countedSessions.Load(sessionID)
223	
224			if !loaded {
225				// No existing entry, try to store
226				actual, loaded := stats.countedSessions.LoadOrStore(sessionID, newCategory)
227				if !loaded {
228					// Successfully stored new category - increment counter
229					stats.incrementCategory(newCategory)
230					return
231				}
232				// Someone else stored it first, loop to check precedence
233				existing = actual
234			}
235	
236			oldCategory := existing.(syncCategory)
237	
238			// Check if we should replace the old category
239			if !shouldReplaceCategory(oldCategory, newCategory) {
240				// Don't replace - higher precedence category already exists
241				return
242			}
243	
244			// Try to replace old category with new category
245			if stats.countedSessions.CompareAndSwap(sessionID, oldCategory, newCategory) {
246				// Successfully replaced - decrement old counter and increment new counter
247				stats.decrementCategory(oldCategory)
248				stats.incrementCategory(newCategory)
249				return
250			}
251			// CompareAndSwap failed, someone else modified it, loop again
252		}
253	}

255	// acquireHTTPSemaphore acquires the HTTP semaphore (blocks until available)
256	// Returns a release function that should be called with defer
257	//
258	// No timeout - blocks indefinitely until semaphore is available. Goroutines that don't acquire
259	// before the overall sync timeout (CloudSyncTimeout) are orphaned, but this is acceptable because
260	// the process terminates after sync timeout. The overall timeout handles cleanup and stats reporting.
261	func (syncMgr *SyncManager) acquireHTTPSemaphore(sessionID, requestType string) (releaseFunc func()) {
262		// Block until semaphore slot is available
263		syncMgr.httpSemaphore <- struct{}{}
264	
265		slog.Debug("Acquired HTTP semaphore",
266			"sessionId", sessionID,
267			"requestType", requestType,
268			"currentConcurrency", len(syncMgr.httpSemaphore))
269	
270		releaseFunc = func() {
271			<-syncMgr.httpSemaphore
272			slog.Debug("Released HTTP semaphore",
273				"sessionId", sessionID,
274				"requestType", requestType,
275				"currentConcurrency", len(syncMgr.httpSemaphore))
276		}
277		return releaseFunc
278	}
