248	            : remoteBinaryUri.path;
249	
250	        // Step 5: Size check — skip upload if remote binary already matches local
251	        let skipUpload = false;
252	        try {
253	            const [localStat, remoteStat] = await Promise.all([
254	                fs.stat(localBinaryPath),
255	                vscode.workspace.fs.stat(remoteBinaryUri),
256	            ]);
257	            if (localStat.size === remoteStat.size) {
258	                this.logger.log(LogLevels.DEBUG, 'Remote binary already up to date (size match)');
259	                skipUpload = true;
260	            }
261	        } catch {
262	            // Remote binary doesn't exist yet, or local binary missing — proceed with upload
263	        }
264	
265	        if (!skipUpload) {
266	            this.logger.log(LogLevels.INFO, 'Uploading remote binary', { binaryName });
267	            try {
268	                const content = await fs.readFile(localBinaryPath);
269	                await vscode.workspace.fs.writeFile(remoteBinaryUri, content);
270	                this.logger.log(LogLevels.INFO, 'Remote binary uploaded');
271	            } catch (error) {
272	                this.logger.log(LogLevels.WARN, 'Failed to upload remote binary', {
273	                    error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
274	                });
275	                return false;
276	            }
277	
278	            // Step 6: chmod on Unix (.exe files don't need it on Windows)
279	            if (!this.isWindowsRemote) {
280	                const chmodTask = this.makeTask(
281	                    'specstory-chmod',
282	                    'SpecStory Chmod',
283	                    `chmod +x '${this.remoteBinaryPath}'`
284	                );
285	                try {
286	                    await this.runOneShot(chmodTask, true);
287	                } catch (error) {
288	                    this.logger.log(LogLevels.WARN, 'chmod task failed', {
289	                        error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
290	                    });
291	                    // Non-fatal — continue
292	                }
293	            }
294	        }
295	
296	        // Step 7: Ensure bin/ is in .specstory/.gitignore
297	        await this.ensureGitignore();
298	
299	        return true;
300	    }
301	
302	    /**
303	     * Map a platform detection string (e.g. "Linux x86_64") to the bundled binary filename.
304	     * Mirrors the mapping in getBinaryName() from binary-launcher.ts.
305	     */
306	    private platformStringToBinaryName(platform: string): string | null {
307	        const map: Record<string, string> = {
308	            'Linux x86_64': 'specstory_linux_x86_64',
309	            'Linux aarch64': 'specstory_linux_arm64',
310	            'Darwin arm64': 'specstory_darwin_arm64',
311	            'Darwin x86_64': 'specstory_darwin_x86_64',
312	            'Windows X64': 'specstory_windows_x86_64.exe',
313	            'Windows Arm64': 'specstory_windows_arm64.exe',
314	        };
315	        return map[platform] ?? null;
316	    }
317	
318	    /**
319	     * Ensure bin/ is present in .specstory/.gitignore.
320	     * Reuses the same append pattern as RulesService.ts.
321	     */
322	    private async ensureGitignore(): Promise<void> {
323	        const gitignoreUri = vscode.Uri.joinPath(
324	            this.pathsService.getSpecStoryDirUri(),
325	            '.gitignore'
326	        );
327	        try {
328	            let content: string;
329	            try {
330	                const data = await vscode.workspace.fs.readFile(gitignoreUri);
331	                content = new TextDecoder().decode(data);
332	            } catch {
333	                // File doesn't exist — create it with the pattern
334	                await vscode.workspace.fs.writeFile(
335	                    gitignoreUri,
336	                    Buffer.from(`${GITIGNORE_BIN_PATTERN}\n`)
337	                );
338	                return;
339	            }
340	
341	            if (!content.includes(GITIGNORE_BIN_PATTERN)) {
342	                this.logger.log(LogLevels.INFO, 'Appending bin/ to .specstory/.gitignore');
343	                const newContent = content.endsWith('\n')
344	                    ? content + `${GITIGNORE_BIN_PATTERN}\n`
345	                    : content + `\n${GITIGNORE_BIN_PATTERN}\n`;
346	                await vscode.workspace.fs.writeFile(gitignoreUri, Buffer.from(newContent));
347	            }
348	        } catch (error) {
349	            this.logger.log(LogLevels.WARN, 'Failed to update .specstory/.gitignore', {
350	                error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
351	            });
352	        }
353	    }
354	
355	    /**
356	     * Build the safe (non-secret) CLI args and the env object containing the token.
357	     * The token is passed via env var rather than a CLI arg to avoid exposure in process listings.
358	     */
359	    private async buildArgsAndEnv(cloudSyncMode: CloudSyncMode): Promise<{
360	        safeArgs: string[];
361	        env: Record<string, string>;
362	        hasToken: boolean;
363	    }> {
364	        const safeArgs: string[] = [];
365	        const env: Record<string, string> = {};
366	        let hasToken = false;
367	
368	        // Cloud sync mode flags
369	        if (cloudSyncMode === 'only-cloud-sync') {
370	            safeArgs.push('--only-cloud-sync');
371	        } else if (cloudSyncMode === 'no-cloud-sync') {
372	            safeArgs.push('--no-cloud-sync');
373	        }
374	
375	        // Token and URL via env vars (not in the command string)
376	        if (cloudSyncMode !== 'no-cloud-sync') {
377	            const isAuthenticated = await this.authService.isAuthenticated();
378	            if (isAuthenticated) {
379	                const cloudUrl =
380	                    process.env.SPECSTORY_SYNC_SERVICE_URL || 'https://cloud.specstory.com';
381	                const token = await this.authService.getRefreshToken();
382	                if (token) {
383	                    env['SPECSTORY_CLOUD_URL'] = cloudUrl;
384	                    env['SPECSTORY_CLOUD_TOKEN'] = token;
385	                    hasToken = true;
386	                }
387	            }
388	        }
389	
390	        // Timezone
391	        if (
392	            !vscode.workspace
393	                .getConfiguration('specstory')
394	                .get<boolean>('coordinatedUniversalTimezone')
395	        ) {
396	            safeArgs.push('--local-time-zone');
397	        }
398	
399	        const outputDir = this.pathsService.getSpecStoryOutputPath();
400	        if (outputDir) {
401	            safeArgs.push('--output-dir', outputDir);
402	        }
403	
404	        const configDir = this.pathsService.getSpecStoryConfigPath();
405	        if (configDir) {
406	            // path.join uses backslashes on Windows; normalize for non-Windows remotes
407	            const remoteConfigDir = this.isWindowsRemote
408	                ? configDir
409	                : configDir.replace(/\\/g, '/');
410	            safeArgs.push('--config-dir', remoteConfigDir);
411	        }
412	
413	        const providersArg = getEnabledProvidersArg();
414	        if (providersArg) {
415	            safeArgs.push('--providers', providersArg);
416	        }
417	
418	        // Project path (required so CLI knows which workspace we're tracking)
419	        safeArgs.push('--project-path', this.getRemoteWorkspacePath());
420	
421	        // Git origin (optional — skip if unavailable)
422	        try {
423	            const gitOrigin = await this.projectIdentityService.readGitOrigin();
424	            if (gitOrigin) {
425	                safeArgs.push('--git-origin', gitOrigin);
426	            }
427	        } catch {
428	            // Non-fatal
429	        }
430	
431	        return { safeArgs, env, hasToken };
432	    }
433	
434	    /**
435	     * Build the full shell command string for a remote CLI invocation.
436	     * Token is referenced via shell env var syntax so it doesn't appear in the command string.
437	     */
438	    private buildShellCommand(
439	        subcommand: string,
440	        safeArgs: string[],
441	        cloudSyncMode: CloudSyncMode,
442	        hasToken: boolean
443	    ): string {
444	        const binary = `"${this.remoteBinaryPath}"`;
445	        const parts: string[] = [binary, subcommand, '--no-version-check'];
446	
447	        if (subcommand === 'sync') {
448	            parts.push('--no-stats');
449	        }
450	
451	        // Reference token via env var to avoid exposing it in the shell command
452	        if (hasToken && cloudSyncMode !== 'no-cloud-sync') {
453	            if (this.isWindowsRemote) {
454	                parts.push(
455	                    '--cloud-url',
456	                    '"%SPECSTORY_CLOUD_URL%"',
457	                    '--cloud-token',
458	                    '"%SPECSTORY_CLOUD_TOKEN%"'
459	                );
460	            } else {
461	                parts.push(
462	                    '--cloud-url',
463	                    '"$SPECSTORY_CLOUD_URL"',
464	                    '--cloud-token',
465	                    '"$SPECSTORY_CLOUD_TOKEN"'
466	                );
467	            }
468	        }
469	
470	        // Append safe args; quote values (non-flag tokens) to handle spaces in paths
471	        for (const arg of safeArgs) {
472	            if (arg.startsWith('-')) {
473	                parts.push(arg);
474	            } else {
475	                parts.push(`"${arg}"`);
476	            }
477	        }
478	
479	        return parts.join(' ');
480	    }
481	
482	    /**
483	     * Run a one-shot remote sync and wait for it to complete.
484	     */
485	    private async runRemoteSync(
486	        safeArgs: string[],
487	        env: Record<string, string>,
488	        cloudSyncMode: CloudSyncMode,
489	        hasToken: boolean
490	    ): Promise<void> {
491	        const cmd = this.buildShellCommand('sync', safeArgs, cloudSyncMode, hasToken);
492	        const task = new vscode.Task(
493	            { type: 'specstory-remote-sync' },
494	            vscode.TaskScope.Workspace,
495	            'SpecStory Remote Sync',
496	            'specstory',
497	            new vscode.ShellExecution(cmd, { env, cwd: this.getRemoteWorkspacePath() })
498	        );
499	        task.presentationOptions = {
500	            reveal: vscode.TaskRevealKind.Never,
501	            panel: vscode.TaskPanelKind.Dedicated,
502	            showReuseMessage: false,
503	            focus: false,
504	        };
505	
506	        const exitCode = await this.runOneShot(task);
507	        if (exitCode === 0) {
508	            this.logger.log(LogLevels.INFO, 'Remote sync completed');
509	        } else {
510	            this.logger.log(LogLevels.WARN, 'Remote sync exited with non-zero code', { exitCode });
511	        }
512	    }
513	
514	    /**
515	     * Start the long-running remote watch task.
516	     * Automatically restarts once on unexpected exit.
517	     */
518	    private async startRemoteWatch(
519	        safeArgs: string[],
520	        env: Record<string, string>,
521	        cloudSyncMode: CloudSyncMode,
522	        hasToken: boolean
523	    ): Promise<void> {
524	        const cmd = this.buildShellCommand('watch', safeArgs, cloudSyncMode, hasToken);
525	        const watchTask = new vscode.Task(
526	            { type: 'specstory-remote-watch' },
527	            vscode.TaskScope.Workspace,
528	            'SpecStory Remote Watch',
529	            'specstory',
530	            new vscode.ShellExecution(cmd, { env, cwd: this.getRemoteWorkspacePath() })
531	        );
532	        watchTask.presentationOptions = {
533	            reveal: vscode.TaskRevealKind.Never,
534	            panel: vscode.TaskPanelKind.Dedicated,
535	            showReuseMessage: false,
536	            focus: false,
537	        };
538	
539	        // Dispose any previous listener before starting a new watch
540	        this.endTaskListener?.dispose();
541	        this.endTaskListener = undefined;
542	
543	        const execution = await vscode.tasks.executeTask(watchTask);
544	        this.watchTaskExecution = execution;
545	        this.logger.log(LogLevels.INFO, 'Remote watch started');
546	
547	        this.endTaskListener = vscode.tasks.onDidEndTaskProcess((e) => {
548	            if (e.execution !== this.watchTaskExecution) {
549	                return;
550	            }
551	            this.watchTaskExecution = undefined;
552	            this.endTaskListener?.dispose();
553	            this.endTaskListener = undefined;
554	
555	            if (this.isStopping) {
556	                this.logger.log(LogLevels.DEBUG, 'Remote watch stopped intentionally');
557	                return;
558	            }
559	
560	            this.logger.log(LogLevels.WARN, 'Remote watch exited unexpectedly', {
561	                exitCode: e.exitCode,
562	            });
563	
564	            if (!this.hasRestarted) {
565	                this.hasRestarted = true;
566	                this.logger.log(LogLevels.INFO, 'Scheduling remote watch restart in 3s');
567	                setTimeout(() => {
568	                    void this.start(this.lastCloudSyncMode, this.lastAutoSaveEnabled);
569	                }, RESTART_DELAY_MS);
570	            } else {
571	                this.logger.log(
572	                    LogLevels.WARN,
573	                    'Remote watch exited again after restart, not retrying'
574	                );
575	            }
576	        });
577	    }
578	
579	    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
580	    // Temp dir management (local CLI output for remote workspaces)
581	    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
582	
583	    /**
584	     * Generate a stable hash for the workspace URI.
585	     * Used to create a persistent temp directory name.
586	     */
587	    private getWorkspaceHash(): string {
588	        const workspaceUri = this.pathsService.getWorkspaceUri();
589	        const hash = crypto.createHash('sha256');
590	        hash.update(workspaceUri.toString());
591	        return hash.digest('hex').substring(0, 16);
592	    }
593	
594	    /**
595	     * Initialize the remote CLI service: create the persistent local temp dir and bootstrap
596	     * remote identity files into it. Safe to call multiple times — temp dir is only created once.
597	     *
598	     * MUST be called before getLocalCliOptions().
599	     */
600	    public async initialize(): Promise<void> {
601	        if (!this.tempOutputDir) {
602	            const workspaceHash = this.getWorkspaceHash();
603	            this.tempOutputDir = path.join(os.tmpdir(), `specstory-${workspaceHash}`);
604	
605	            const dirAlreadyExists = await fs
606	                .stat(this.tempOutputDir)
607	                .then(() => true)
608	                .catch(() => false);
609	            this.logger.log(LogLevels.DEBUG, 'Temp output directory already exists?', {
610	                exists: dirAlreadyExists,
611	                path: this.tempOutputDir,
612	            });
613	
614	            await fs.mkdir(this.tempOutputDir, { recursive: true });
615	            this.logger.log(
616	                LogLevels.INFO,
617	                'Created persistent temp directory for remote workspace',
618	                { tempOutputDir: this.tempOutputDir, workspaceHash }
619	            );
620	        }
621	
622	        // Cache git origin for synchronous access via getLocalCliOptions()
623	        try {
624	            this.cachedGitOrigin = await this.projectIdentityService.readGitOrigin();
625	        } catch {
626	            this.cachedGitOrigin = null;
627	        }
628	
629	        // Bootstrap from remote — MUST happen before the watcher is active
630	        await this.bootstrapRemoteIdentity();
631	    }
632	
633	    /**
634	     * Return CLI options for the local binary to run correctly in a remote workspace context.
635	     * Returns an empty object if initialize() has not been called yet.
636	     */
637	    public getLocalCliOptions(): Partial<LaunchSyncBinaryOptions> {
638	        if (!this.tempOutputDir) {
639	            return {};
640	        }
641	        return {
642	            projectPath: this.pathsService.getWorkspacePath(),
643	            gitOrigin: this.cachedGitOrigin,
644	            configDir: path.join(this.tempOutputDir, 'cli'),
645	            cwd: this.tempOutputDir,
646	        };
647	    }
648	
649	    /**
650	     * Copy the local temp dir contents to the remote workspace.
651	     * Only runs when autoSaveEnabled is true (the CLI only writes markdown in that mode).
652	     */
653	    public async syncToRemote(autoSaveEnabled: boolean): Promise<void> {
654	        if (!this.tempOutputDir || !autoSaveEnabled) {
655	            return;
656	        }
657	        await this.copyOutputDirToRemoteWorkspace();
658	    }
659	
660	    /**
661	     * Start watching the local temp dir so CLI writes are automatically pushed to the remote.
662	     * Replaces any previously active watcher.
663	     * MUST be called AFTER syncToRemote() so the initial copy doesn't trigger a redundant upload.
664	     */
665	    public startWatcher(): void {
666	        this.setupTempDirWatcher();
667	    }
668	
669	    /**
670	     * Bootstrap project identity and statistics for remote workspaces.
671	     * Copies .project.json, statistics.json, and cli/config.toml from the remote .specstory/ dir
672	     * into the local temp dir so the CLI can reuse existing identity and stats.
673	     *
674	     * MUST be called BEFORE setupTempDirWatcher() — if the watcher were already active,
675	     * bootstrap writes would immediately trigger a copy back to remote.
676	     */
677	    private async bootstrapRemoteIdentity(): Promise<void> {
678	        if (!this.tempOutputDir) {
679	            return;
680	        }
681	
682	        try {
683	            const remoteSpecstoryUri = this.pathsService.getSpecStoryDirUri();
684	
685	            // .project.json — remote is always the source of truth
686	            const remoteProjectJsonUri = vscode.Uri.joinPath(remoteSpecstoryUri, '.project.json');
687	            const localProjectJsonPath = path.join(this.tempOutputDir, '.project.json');
688	            try {
689	                const remoteContent = await vscode.workspace.fs.readFile(remoteProjectJsonUri);
690	                await fs.writeFile(localProjectJsonPath, remoteContent);
691	                this.logger.log(
692	                    LogLevels.INFO,
693	                    'Bootstrapped .project.json from remote workspace',
694	                    {
695	                        tempOutputDir: this.tempOutputDir,
696	                        toLocalPath: localProjectJsonPath,
697	                        fromRemotePath: remoteProjectJsonUri.toString(),
698	                    }
699	                );
700	            } catch {
701	                const localExists = await fs
702	                    .access(localProjectJsonPath)
703	                    .then(() => true)
704	                    .catch(() => false);
705	                this.logger.log(
706	                    LogLevels.DEBUG,
707	                    localExists
708	                        ? 'Remote has no .project.json, using existing local copy'
709	                        : 'No .project.json on remote or local, CLI will create new identity'
710	                );
711	            }
712	
713	            // statistics.json — remote is always the source of truth
714	            const remoteStatisticsUri = vscode.Uri.joinPath(remoteSpecstoryUri, 'statistics.json');
715	            const localStatisticsPath = path.join(this.tempOutputDir, 'statistics.json');
716	            try {
717	                const remoteStatsContent = await vscode.workspace.fs.readFile(remoteStatisticsUri);
718	                await fs.writeFile(localStatisticsPath, remoteStatsContent);
719	                this.logger.log(
720	                    LogLevels.DEBUG,
721	                    'Bootstrapped statistics.json from remote workspace'
722	                );
723	            } catch {
724	                const localExists = await fs
725	                    .access(localStatisticsPath)
726	                    .then(() => true)
727	                    .catch(() => false);
728	                this.logger.log(
729	                    LogLevels.DEBUG,
730	                    localExists
731	                        ? 'Remote has no statistics.json, using existing local copy'
732	                        : 'No statistics.json on remote or local, CLI will create it'
733	                );
734	            }
735	
736	            // cli/config.toml — remote is always the source of truth
737	            const remoteCliConfigUri = vscode.Uri.joinPath(
738	                remoteSpecstoryUri,
739	                'cli',
740	                'config.toml'
741	            );
742	            const localCliConfigPath = path.join(this.tempOutputDir, 'cli', 'config.toml');
743	            try {
744	                const remoteCliConfigContent =
745	                    await vscode.workspace.fs.readFile(remoteCliConfigUri);
746	                await fs.mkdir(path.dirname(localCliConfigPath), { recursive: true });
747	                await fs.writeFile(localCliConfigPath, remoteCliConfigContent);
748	                this.logger.log(
749	                    LogLevels.DEBUG,
750	                    'Bootstrapped cli/config.toml from remote workspace'
751	                );
752	            } catch {
753	                const localExists = await fs
754	                    .access(localCliConfigPath)
755	                    .then(() => true)
756	                    .catch(() => false);
757	                this.logger.log(
758	                    LogLevels.DEBUG,
759	                    localExists
760	                        ? 'Remote has no cli/config.toml, using existing local copy'
761	                        : 'No cli/config.toml on remote or local, CLI will create it'
762	                );
763	            }
764	        } catch (error) {
765	            this.logger.log(LogLevels.ERROR, 'Error bootstrapping remote identity', {
766	                error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
767	            });
768	        }
769	    }
770	
771	    /**
772	     * Setup a watcher on the local temp output dir.
773	     * When the CLI writes new files there, schedule a debounced copy to the remote workspace.
774	     *
775	     * MUST be called AFTER bootstrapRemoteIdentity() and the initial syncToRemote()
776	     * so that bootstrap writes and the initial sync copy do not trigger spurious remote uploads.
777	     */
778	    private setupTempDirWatcher(): void {
779	        if (this.tempDirWatcher) {
780	            this.tempDirWatcher.close();
781	            this.tempDirWatcher = undefined;
782	        }
783	
784	        if (!this.tempOutputDir) {
785	            return;
786	        }
787	
788	        this.tempDirWatcher = fsWatch(this.tempOutputDir, { recursive: false }, () => {
789	            this.scheduleCopyToRemote();
790	        });
791	
792	        this.logger.log(LogLevels.DEBUG, 'Setup temp dir watcher', {
793	            dir: this.tempOutputDir,
794	        });
795	    }
796	
797	    /**
798	     * Schedule a debounced copy from the temp dir to the remote workspace.
799	     * Waits 2 seconds after the last change before triggering the copy.
800	     */
801	    private scheduleCopyToRemote(): void {
802	        if (this.syncDebounceTimer) {
803	            clearTimeout(this.syncDebounceTimer);
804	        }
805	        this.syncDebounceTimer = setTimeout(() => {
806	            this.logger.log(LogLevels.INFO, 'Temp dir changed, copying output to remote workspace');
807	            void this.copyOutputDirToRemoteWorkspace();
808	        }, 2000);
809	    }
810	
811	    /**
812	     * Copy all files from the local temp output dir to the remote workspace.
813	     * Destination is split by file type:
814	     * - .project.json and statistics.json → remote .specstory/ (always fixed)
815	     * - *.md files → remote {specstory.outputPath}/ (user-configured)
816	     */
817	    private async copyOutputDirToRemoteWorkspace(): Promise<void> {
818	        if (!this.tempOutputDir) {
819	            return;
820	        }
821	
822	        try {
823	            this.logger.log(LogLevels.DEBUG, 'Copying output dir files to remote workspace', {
824	                tempOutputDir: this.tempOutputDir,
825	            });
826	
827	            const remoteSpecstoryUri = this.pathsService.getSpecStoryDirUri();
828	            const remoteHistoryUri = this.pathsService.getSpecStoryHistoryUri();
829	
830	            // Ensure both remote directories exist
831	            try {
832	                await vscode.workspace.fs.createDirectory(remoteSpecstoryUri);
833	            } catch {
834	                // Directory might already exist
835	            }
836	            try {
837	                await vscode.workspace.fs.createDirectory(remoteHistoryUri);
838	            } catch {
839	                // Directory might already exist
840	            }
841	
842	            const showDevTools = vscode.workspace
843	                .getConfiguration('specstory')
844	                .get<boolean>('showDeveloperTools', false);
845	
846	            const entries = await fs.readdir(this.tempOutputDir, { withFileTypes: true });
847	            for (const entry of entries) {
848	                if (entry.isFile()) {
849	                    const localFilePath = path.join(this.tempOutputDir, entry.name);
850	                    const content = await fs.readFile(localFilePath);
851	
852	                    // .project.json and statistics.json always go to .specstory/
853	                    // *.md files go to the user-configured outputPath
854	                    const isMetaFile =
855	                        entry.name === '.project.json' || entry.name === 'statistics.json';
856	                    const remoteFileUri = vscode.Uri.joinPath(
857	                        isMetaFile ? remoteSpecstoryUri : remoteHistoryUri,
858	                        entry.name
859	                    );
860	
861	                    await vscode.workspace.fs.writeFile(remoteFileUri, content);
862	                    this.logger.log(LogLevels.DEBUG, 'Copied file to remote', {
863	                        filename: entry.name,
864	                        destination: isMetaFile ? '.specstory/' : 'outputPath/',
865	                    });
866	                } else if (entry.isDirectory()) {
867	                    if (entry.name === 'debug' && !showDevTools) {
868	                        continue;
869	                    }
870	                    const localSubDir = path.join(this.tempOutputDir, entry.name);
871	                    const remoteSubDirUri = vscode.Uri.joinPath(remoteSpecstoryUri, entry.name);
872	                    await this.copyLocalDirToRemote(localSubDir, remoteSubDirUri);
873	                    this.logger.log(LogLevels.DEBUG, 'Copied directory to remote', {
874	                        dirname: entry.name,
875	                    });
876	                }
877	            }
878	
879	            this.logger.log(
880	                LogLevels.INFO,
881	                'Successfully copied output dir files to remote workspace'
882	            );
883	        } catch (error) {

Doc now has the local schema, the CLI push payload, and a preliminary gap list captured. Waiting on the corrected `specstory-monorepo` backend analysis to fill in the server-side storage and finalize the gap analysis.

Here's where things stand and the key takeaways so far:

**The three representations of a session** (this is the crux):
- **Native transcript** (JSONL / Cursor store.db) — what `resume` needs to reconstruct/launch an agent. Lives only on the originating machine's disk locally.
- **Flattened text body** — what `search` needs. Lives in local `sessions.db` FTS5.
- **Markdown + `rawData`** — what the CLI pushes to cloud.

**The single most important finding:** the CLI already pushes `rawData` (the raw native transcript) to the cloud, not just rendered markdown (`sync.go:79`). **If** the cloud persists that `rawData`, cloud-resume is genuinely feasible — a teammate's/other-machine's session could be pulled and reconstructed exactly like a local one. If it only keeps markdown, remote resume would be degraded (markdown is lossy). That's the #1 thing the backend pass needs to confirm.

**Two identity wrinkles already visible:**
- Local PK is `(agent, session_id)`; the cloud push URL keys on `(projectId, sessionId)` with `agent` only in metadata — need a stable cross-store identity to dedup and avoid showing a session twice.
- Both sides key projects by git_id/workspace_id, so a given checkout maps to the same `project_id` — a clean basis for "also show this project's cloud sessions."

A heads-up on the first backend agent: it analyzed the wrong repo (`intent`, the voice-collab/arena product) and reported the push endpoint as "not implemented" — that's why I re-launched against `specstory-monorepo`. I'll fold the correct results in when it returns. Let me know when your local web env is up.

1	# API Reference
2	
3	This document provides a comprehensive reference for all API endpoints available in the SpecStory AI Service.
4	
5	## Base URLs
6	
7	- **Local**: http://localhost:8787
8	- **Development**: https://specstory-ai-service-dev.jake-bd9.workers.dev
9	- **Staging**: https://specstory-ai-service-staging.jake-bd9.workers.dev
10	- **Production**: https://specstory-ai-service-prod.jake-bd9.workers.dev
11	
12	## Common Response Headers
13	
14	All responses include:
15	- `X-Request-Id`: Unique identifier for request tracing
16	- `Content-Type`: `application/json`
17	
18	## Endpoints
19	
20	### Health Check
21	
22	Check the health status of the service.
23	
24	```
25	GET /status
26	```
27	
28	#### Response
29	
30	```json
31	{
32	  "status": "healthy",
33	  "service": "specstory-ai-service",
34	  "version": "0.1.0",
35	  "timestamp": "2024-12-10T12:00:00.000Z",
36	  "requestId": "unique-request-id"
37	}
38	```
39	
40	#### Status Codes
41	
42	- `200 OK` - Service is healthy
43	- `503 Service Unavailable` - Service is unhealthy
44	
45	### Hello World
46	
47	Basic endpoint to verify the service is running.
48	
49	```
50	GET /
51	```
52	
53	#### Response
54	
55	```json
56	{
57	  "message": "Hello World from SpecStory AI Service!",
58	  "timestamp": "2024-12-10T12:00:00.000Z",
59	  "requestId": "unique-request-id"
60	}
61	```
62	
63	#### Status Codes
64	
65	- `200 OK` - Success
66	
67	## Error Responses
68	
69	All errors follow a consistent format:
70	
71	```json
72	{
73	  "error": "Error message",
74	  "requestId": "unique-request-id"
75	}
76	```
77	
78	### Common Error Codes
79	
80	- `400 Bad Request` - Invalid request parameters
81	- `401 Unauthorized` - Missing or invalid authentication
82	- `403 Forbidden` - Insufficient permissions
83	- `404 Not Found` - Resource not found
84	- `500 Internal Server Error` - Server error
85	- `503 Service Unavailable` - Service temporarily unavailable
```
</details></tool-use>

342	export async function handleHeadSession(
343	  request: ApiRequest,
344	  projectId: string,
345	  sessionId: string
346	): Promise<Response> {
347	  try {
348	    // Try to get the session detail
349	    try {
350	      const session = await getSessionDetail(
351	        projectId,
352	        sessionId,
353	        request.userId!
354	      );
355	
356	      // Build the same response that GET would return (reusing the same function)
357	      const response = buildSessionDetailResponse(session);
358	      const jsonResponse = JSON.stringify(response);
359	      const contentLength = new TextEncoder().encode(jsonResponse).length;
360	
361	      // Generate ETag using the shared helper
362	      const etag = await generateSessionETag(session);
363	      const quotedEtag = `"${etag}"`;
364	
365	      // Check for conditional request using If-None-Match header
366	      const clientEtag = request.headers.get("If-None-Match");
367	      if (clientEtag && clientEtag === quotedEtag) {
368	        // Content hasn't changed, return 304 Not Modified
369	        return new Response(null, {
370	          status: 304,
371	          headers: {
372	            ETag: quotedEtag,
373	            "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
374	            "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "HEAD, OPTIONS",
375	          },
376	        });
377	      }
378	
379	      // Return HEAD response with metadata headers only (no body)
380	      return new Response(null, {
381	        status: 200,
382	        headers: {
383	          "Content-Type": "application/json",
384	          "Content-Length": contentLength.toString(),
385	          "Last-Modified": new Date(session.updatedAt).toUTCString(),
386	          ETag: quotedEtag,
387	          "X-Markdown-Size": session.markdownSize.toString(),
388	          "X-Raw-Data-Size": session.rawDataSize.toString(),
389	          "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
390	          "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "HEAD, OPTIONS",
391	        },
392	      });
393	    } catch (error) {
394	      // If session not found, return 404
395	      const errorMessage =
396	        error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
397	      if (
398	        errorMessage === "Session not found" ||
399	        errorMessage === "Session not found or access denied"
400	      ) {
401	        return new Response(null, {
402	          status: 404,
403	          headers: {
404	            "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
405	            "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "HEAD, OPTIONS",
406	          },
407	        });
408	      }
409	      throw error;
410	    }
411	  } catch (error) {
412	    console.error("Error handling head session:", error);
413	    return handleError(error);
414	  }
415	}

475	async function queueWorkers(session: SessionDetail): Promise<void> {
476	  // Queue exchange parsing job
477	  await WorkerQueue.queue("EXCHANGE_PARSER_QUEUE", {
478	    sessionId: session.id,
479	  });
480	
481	  // Queue session duration extraction job
482	  await WorkerQueue.queue("SESSION_DURATION_QUEUE", {
483	    sessionId: session.id,
484	  });
485	
486	  // Queue session summary generation job
487	  await WorkerQueue.queue("SESSION_SUMMARY_QUEUE", {
488	    sessionId: session.id,
489	  });
490	}

492	// Helper function to build session detail response, used for both GET and HEAD requests
493	function buildSessionDetailResponse(
494	  session: SessionDetail
495	): SessionDetailResponse {
496	  return {
497	    success: true,
498	    data: {
499	      session,
500	    },
501	  };
502	}

504	const getMarkdownVersion = (markdownContent: string) => {
505	  if (!markdownContent) {
506	    return "1.0.0";
507	  }
508	  const markdownVersionMatch = markdownContent.match(MARKDOWN_CONTENT_REGEX);
509	  if (!markdownVersionMatch) {
510	    return "1.0.0";
511	  }
512	  return markdownVersionMatch[1];
513	};

14	ALTER TABLE workspaces ADD COLUMN owner_id TEXT NOT NULL;
15	CREATE INDEX idx_workspaces_project_id ON workspaces(project_id);

18	-- Let's also create a unique constraint across project_id and owner_id
19	ALTER TABLE workspaces ADD CONSTRAINT unique_project_owner UNIQUE (project_id, owner_id);

21	-- Also rename the triggers for the projects tables to workspaces tables
22	ALTER TRIGGER update_projects_updated_at ON workspaces RENAME TO update_workspaces_updated_at;

24	-- From there we need to update the sessions table project_id reference.  We want to rename the column to workspace_id and

45	async function withJwtValidation(request: ApiRequest) {
46	  const allowedTokenTypes = request.url.includes("/api/v1/api-tokens")
47	    ? ["web-access"]
48	    : [];
49	
50	  const jwtValidation = await validateJWT(request, {
51	    method: request.method,
52	    allowedTokenTypes,
53	  });
54	  if (!jwtValidation.isValid) {
55	    const statusCode = jwtValidation.errorType === "forbidden" ? 403 : 401;
56	
57	    return json(
58	      {
59	        success: false,
60	        error: jwtValidation.error || "Authentication failed",
61	      },
62	      {
63	        status: statusCode,
64	        headers: {
65	          "Content-Type": "application/json",
66	          "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
67	          "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": `${request.method}, OPTIONS`,
68	          "Access-Control-Allow-Headers": "Content-Type, Authorization",
69	        },
70	      }
71	    );
72	  }
73	
74	  request.userId = jwtValidation.userId;
75	}
76	
77	const withRateLimiter = async (request: Request) => {
78	  const { pathname } = new URL(request.url);
79	  const { success } = await env.API_RATE_LIMITER.limit({ key: pathname });
80	  if (!success) {
81	    return new Response(
82	      JSON.stringify({
83	        error: `429 Failure - rate limit exceeded for ${pathname}`,
84	      }),
85	      {
86	        status: 429,
87	      }
88	    );
89	  }
90	};
91	
92	const withSizeLimiter = async (request: Request) => {
93	  // Check the content length header and if it is greater than 50MB, return a 413 error
94	  const contentLength = request.headers.get("Content-Length");
95	  if (contentLength && parseInt(contentLength) > 50 * 1024 * 1024) {
96	    const { pathname } = new URL(request.url);
97	    return new Response(
98	      JSON.stringify({
99	        error: `413 Failure - size limit exceeded for ${pathname}`,
100	      }),
101	      {
102	        status: 413,
103	      }
104	    );
105	  }
106	};

132	export async function handleUpdateProject(
133	  request: ApiRequest,
134	  projectId: string
135	): Promise<Response> {
136	  try {
137	    // Parse request body
138	    const body = await request.json();
139	    const { icon, color, name } = body as {
140	      icon?: typeof ProjectIcon;
141	      color?: typeof ProjectColor;
142	      name?: string;
143	    };
144	
145	    if (!icon && !color) {
146	      return generateResponse(
147	        {
148	          success: false,
149	          error: "At least one of icon or color must be provided",
150	        },
151	        400,
152	        "PATCH, OPTIONS",
153	        "Content-Type, Authorization"
154	      );
155	    }
156	
157	    // Check icon is ProjectIcon type
158	    if (
159	      icon &&
160	      typeof icon !== "string" &&
161	      !AVAILABLE_PROJECT_ICONS.includes(icon as any) // eslint-disable-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
162	    ) {
163	      return generateResponse(
164	        {
165	          success: false,
166	          error:
167	            "Invalid icon type, valid values are: " +
168	            AVAILABLE_PROJECT_ICONS.join(", "),
169	        },
170	        400,
171	        "PATCH, OPTIONS",
172	        "Content-Type, Authorization"
173	      );
174	    }
175	
176	    if (
177	      color &&
178	      typeof color !== "string" &&
179	      !AVAILABLE_PROJECT_COLORS.includes(color as any) // eslint-disable-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
180	    ) {
181	      return generateResponse(
182	        {
183	          success: false,
184	          error:
185	            "Invalid color type, valid values are: " +
186	            AVAILABLE_PROJECT_COLORS.join(", "),
187	        },
188	        400,
189	        "PATCH, OPTIONS",
190	        "Content-Type, Authorization"
191	      );

193	
194	    // Get workspace to find the internal workspace ID
195	    const workspace = await getWorkspaceByProjectAndUserId(request, projectId);
196	
197	    if (!workspace) {
198	      return generateResponse(
199	        {
200	          success: false,
201	          error: "Workspace not found or access denied",
202	        },
203	        404,
204	        "PATCH, OPTIONS",
205	        "Content-Type, Authorization"
206	      );
207	    }
208	
209	    if (workspace.owner_id !== request.userId) {

220

227	      name
228	    );
229	
230	    // Return only the fields that were updated
231	    const responseData: { icon?: string; color?: string; name?: string } = {};
232	    if (icon !== undefined) responseData.icon = icon as unknown as string;
233	    if (color !== undefined) responseData.color = color as unknown as string;
234	    if (name !== undefined) responseData.name = name;
235	
236	    return generateResponse(
237	      {
238	        success: true,
239	        data: responseData,
240	      },
241	      200,
242	      "PATCH, OPTIONS",

244	    );

## 6. SESSION IDENTITY & PROJECT KEYING

**Session uniqueness**: 
- **Primary key**: `sessions.id` (internal UUID, auto-generated)
- **Client ID**: `sessions.clientId` (the sessionId from PUT URL parameter)
- **Unique constraint**: `(client_id, workspace_id)` ensures no duplicate sessions per project
- Sessions keyed by: `projectId + sessionId` from CLI perspective

**Project uniqueness**:
- **Internal key**: `workspaces.id` (UUID, auto-generated)
- **External key**: `workspaces.project_id` (string from CLI, typically git_id or workspace path hash)
- **Unique constraint**: `(project_id, owner_id)` - one project per user

**Association to user/org**:
- `workspaces.ownerId` = Clerk user_id (text, from JWT `sub` claim)
- `user_permissions` table tracks user access to workspaces
- No org/team support yet; single user ownership model

**Handler flow** (lines 34-172):
1. **Workspace upsert** (`Session.upsert()` call at line 95): Creates or verifies workspace exists for the project+userId

   - `markdownContent`: Full markdown from request body
   - `rawData`: JSONL transcript from request body
   - `markdownSize` &amp; `rawDataSize`: Byte counts (line 102-103)

   - RawData uploaded to Supabase Storage at `{workspace.id}/{session.id}/raw-data.json`

## 5. FULL-TEXT SEARCH INFRASTRUCTURE

**PostgreSQL FTS with websearch_to_tsquery** (shared/models/session.ts:234):

```sql
${schema.exchanges.fts} @@ websearch_to_tsquery('english', ${formattedQuery})
```

**Search architecture**:
1. Builds CTEs (Common Table Expressions):
   - `user_workspaces`: Filters by user permission + optional projectIds
   - `matching_exchanges`: Full-text search on `exchanges.fts` column using PostgreSQL native FTS
2. Filters exchanges by date range if `timeFilter` provided
3. Aggregates matching exchanges per session with `json_agg`
4. Returns ranked results ordered by most recent matching exchange
5. Supports filtering by: clientName, agentName, deviceId, gitBranches, llmModels, tags, startDate/endDate

**Search column**: `exchanges.fts` is a generated column:
```typescript
fts: text("fts").generatedAlwaysAs("to_tsvector('english::regconfig', content)"),
```
With GIN index for performance (schema.ts:112-115).

## 6. SESSION IDENTITY &amp; PROJECT KEYING

**Session uniqueness**: 
- **Primary key**: `sessions.id` (internal UUID, auto-generated)
- **Client ID**: `sessions.clientId` (the sessionId from PUT URL parameter)
- **Unique constraint**: `(client_id, workspace_id)` ensures no duplicate sessions per project
- Sessions keyed by: `projectId + sessionId` from CLI perspective

**Project uniqueness**:
- **Internal key**: `workspaces.id` (UUID, auto-generated)
- **External key**: `workspaces.project_id` (string from CLI, typically git_id or workspace path hash)
- **Unique constraint**: `(project_id, owner_id)` - one project per user

**Association to user/org**:
- `workspaces.ownerId` = Clerk user_id (text, from JWT `sub` claim)
- `user_permissions` table tracks user access to workspaces
- No org/team support yet; single user ownership model

## 7. AUTHENTICATION &amp; AUTHORIZATION

**Auth mechanism**: Bearer JWT token validation

Location: `/Users/sean/Source/SpecStory/specstory-sync/sync-cloud/worker/handlers/shared.ts` (validateJWT function)

**JWT validation**:
- Validates Clerk JWT signature
- Extracts `userId` from JWT `sub` claim (lines 74 of router.ts)
- Token types: 
  - `bearer` - standard API token from web UI login
  - `web-access` - special token for API management endpoints

**RLS (Row Level Security)**:
- Not enabled at DB level
- Authorization enforced in application layer via `user_permissions` checks
- Every query filters by `workspaceId` and `userId` together

**Session access control** (`sessions.ts:186`):

```

Cloud "project" = `workspaces` table keyed by `(project_id, owner_id)`; single-owner, no org/team sharing yet.

Schema comparison is done and written into `docs/CLOUD-RESUME.md §1`. Here's the synthesis for our discussion.

## The core picture

A session has **three representations**, and the two CLI commands need different ones:
- `resume` needs the **native transcript** (raw provider JSONL / Cursor store.db) to reconstruct and launch the agent.
- `search` needs **flattened/indexed text**.

## What's already in place (the encouraging part)

**The cloud already stores what we need.** When the CLI syncs, it pushes both rendered `markdown` *and* `rawData` (the native transcript). On the server (`specstory-sync`, a Cloudflare Worker — **not** the monorepo), that `rawData` is persisted to Supabase object storage at `{workspace}/{session}/raw-data.json`, and every session is parsed into an `exchanges` table with a **Postgres FTS column** (`exchanges.fts`, GIN-indexed). There's even a live `searchSessions` GraphQL query and per-project `list`/`get` REST endpoints, all behind the same Clerk Bearer token the CLI already holds.

So: **cloud-resume and cloud-search are both feasible on existing infra.** The native bytes for resume exist; the search index for search exists.

## The real gaps (what we'll need to design)

1. **rawData fetch path** — the one concrete server gap. The current `GET …/{sessionId}` returns markdown + parsed exchanges, *not* the raw blob. Resume needs the raw blob (new `?include=rawData`, a `/raw` route, or a signed storage URL).
2. **Search divergence** — local is SQLite FTS5 over a flattened body (recency-ordered, LIMIT 500); cloud is Postgres `websearch_to_tsquery` over exchanges. Different tokenization/ranking → need a merge strategy for one blended TUI list.
3. **Identity dedup** — local PK is `(agent, session_id)`; cloud keys on `(project_id+owner, session_id)` with `agent` only in metadata. A session synced from *this* machine shows in both stores → dedup on `session_id` and prefer the local copy (resumes offline/instantly).
4. **Scope reality** — cloud is single-owner today (no org/team sharing), so v1 cloud-resume = "my sessions from my *other machines*," not teammates' yet.

**Net:** little new server work (mainly the rawData fetch); most effort is CLI-side — a cloud client, merging cloud rows into the existing resume/search TUI, dedup, and pulling+reconstructing a remote session before launch.

A couple of things worth deciding before I draft §2 (UX) and §3 (technical):

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**How should cloud sessions appear in the resume/search TUI relative to local ones?**

Options:
- **Unified, dedup'd list** - Local + cloud merged into one list, deduped by session_id, with a small badge (☁/local) per row. Local copy preferred when a session exists in both. Feels seamless.
- **Separate cloud section/tab** - Local sessions first (as today), cloud sessions in a distinct section or toggle. Clearer provenance, less merging logic, but two places to look.
- **Opt-in flag** - Local-only by default; cloud included only with a flag (e.g. --cloud). Zero latency/behavior change for existing users; cloud is explicit.

**When a session lives only in the cloud (came from another machine), how far should v1 go?**

Options:
- **Full pull + reconstruct + launch** - Fetch raw-data.json, write it into the local provider's native location, reindex, and launch the agent — true cross-machine resume. Most valuable, most work (needs the rawData fetch endpoint).
- **Search/preview only in v1** - Cloud sessions are searchable and previewable (markdown), but resuming a cloud-only session is deferred. Ships faster; resume stays local-only initially.

**How tightly should this couple to the cloud being reachable?**

Options:
- **Local-first, cloud best-effort** - Local index always works instantly offline; cloud results layered in async with a timeout, failures degrade silently to local-only. Recommended.
- **Cloud-aware, blocking** - Wait for cloud results before showing the list (simpler code, but adds latency and a hard network dependency to every resume/search).

## Now, the discussion

The encouraging headline: **the cloud already persists everything cloud-resume needs.** `rawData` (the native transcript) lands in Supabase storage as `raw-data.json`, and there's already Postgres FTS (`exchanges.fts`) plus list/get endpoints behind the CLI's existing Clerk token. Before I draft §2 (UX) and §3 (technical), three decisions shape everything downstream. Per how you like to work, here are the options with my recommendation on each:

**A. How do cloud sessions appear in the resume/search TUI?**
- *Unified, dedup'd list* (my rec) — merge local + cloud into one list, dedup by `session_id`, small ☁/local badge per row, prefer the local copy when both exist. Most seamless; costs merge+dedup logic.
- *Separate cloud section/tab* — clearer provenance, less merge logic, but two places to look.
- *Opt-in `--cloud` flag* — zero change for existing users; cloud is explicit but discoverable-only-if-you-know.

**B. How far does v1 go for a cloud-only session (came from another machine)?**
- *Full pull + reconstruct + launch* (my rec, if we accept the one new endpoint) — true cross-machine resume; needs the `rawData` fetch path.
- *Search/preview only in v1* — ships faster, resume stays local-only, but it's the less compelling half of the feature.

**C. Offline posture?**
- *Local-first, cloud best-effort* (my rec) — local index always works instantly offline; cloud layered in async with a timeout, silent degrade on failure. Keeps today's UX latency.
- *Cloud-aware, blocking* — simpler code, but adds a hard network dependency + latency to every resume/search.

My overall lean: **A-unified + B-full + C-local-first** — it makes cloud sessions feel native without regressing the current instant local experience, and it leans on infra that already exists. Where do you want to land on each?

146	### Gap analysis
147	
148	**The good news — most primitives already exist server-side:**
149	
150	1. **`rawData` IS persisted** (Supabase storage `…/raw-data.json`). ⇒ **Cloud-resume is feasible**: pull the native transcript and reconstruct/launch exactly like a local session. Caveat: the current `GET …/{sessionId}` read handler returns markdown + parsed *exchanges*, **not** the raw blob. **Gap:** need a way for the CLI to fetch `raw-data.json` (new query param like `?include=rawData`, a dedicated `…/{sessionId}/raw` route, or a signed storage URL).
151	
152	2. **Server-side FTS already exists** (`searchSessions` GraphQL over `exchanges.fts`). ⇒ **Cloud-search is feasible** without new infra. But ranking/tokenization differs from local: cloud = Postgres `websearch_to_tsquery` over parsed exchanges, ranked by recency-of-match; local = SQLite FTS5 over a flattened body, LIMIT 500 by recency. **Gap:** a merge/dedup strategy when blending local + cloud hits in one TUI list.
153	
154	3. **Identity reconciliation.** Local PK `(agent, session_id)`; cloud key `(workspace=project_id+owner, client_id=session_id)`, with `agent` only in `metadata.agentName`. A session synced from *this* machine appears in both stores. **Gap:** dedup on `session_id` (+ `project_id`), recovering `agent` from `metadata.agentName`, so the same session isn't listed twice and a local hit is preferred (it can resume offline/instantly).
155	
156	4. **Project scoping aligns.** Both key project by git_id/workspace_id, so the current checkout resolves to the same `project_id` on both sides — clean basis for "show this project's cloud sessions too," and the cloud already has the per-project list endpoint.
157	
158	5. **Resume fidelity across agents.** Local cross-agent resume reconstructs from native `SessionData`. Cloud rawData is the same native bytes, so cross-agent reconstruction should work identically once the blob is fetchable. Confirm `rawData` is the *unmodified* provider transcript for every agent (esp. Cursor, whose source is a `store.db`, not JSONL — what exactly got pushed as `rawData`?).
159	
160	6. **Auth/scope.** CLI already holds a Clerk Bearer token (`~/.config/specstory/auth.json`) and uses it for push; the same token authorizes list/get/search/read. No new auth work. Org/team sharing doesn't exist yet, so cloud-resume is initially "your own sessions from your other machines," not teammates'.

Corrected everywhere. Here's the model as it now reads, so we're aligned:

**`SessionData` is the canonical cloud representation.** Cloud-resume is: `GET SessionData` (JSON) from the cloud → `ReconstructSession(SessionData) → native` → launch. The raw provider transcript (`rawData`) is *not* the transport and won't be the canonical thing in the cloud. Because `SessionData` is already provider-agnostic, a cloud session reconstructs into *any* agent, and — a nice side effect — the cloud never has to understand Cursor's `store.db` or anyone's JSONL dialect; that parsing happens once, at the source.

I captured what I think is now **the central design fork** in the doc's Open Questions, and I want your call on it:

**How does the cloud produce the `SessionData` it serves?**
- **(a) Server derives it** from the `exchanges` it already parses on ingest — no change to the sync push, but only works if that server-side parse is faithful enough to reconstruct from (tool calls, thinking, usage, `workspaceRoot`, provider info). The current exchanges parse looks markdown-oriented, so it may be lossy — would need verifying.
- **(b) CLI pushes `SessionData`** on sync; the server stores it verbatim and serves it back. Guarantees end-to-end fidelity and makes `SessionData` the genuine source of truth. It's a small CLI change since `ProcessSingleSession` already has `SessionData` in hand at push time (markdown is already rendered from `SessionData.Exchanges`).

I'm **leaning (b)** — fidelity is the whole game for resume, and (a) makes reconstruction hostage to whatever the server's parser happened to preserve. (b) also opens the door to dropping `rawData` from the payload entirely.

Two things that follow from your answer:
1. If **(b)**, does pushing `SessionData` **replace** `rawData` in the payload, or run **alongside** it during a transition (existing synced sessions predate `SessionData` push, so the cloud back-catalog would only have `rawData`/`exchanges` until re-synced)?
2. Either way, the server needs to **serve** `SessionData` — new representation on `GET …/{sessionId}` (e.g. `Accept: application/vnd.specstory.sessiondata+json` or `?include=sessionData`) vs. a dedicated route.

Which way do you want to go on the fork — (a) or (b)?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 13:03:24Z)**_

Locked in as **D2** and propagated through the gap analysis. The doc now records: CLI pushes `SessionData` on sync → server stores it verbatim → serves it back for resume.

Two follow-ons fall out of that. My take on each:

**1. Does pushing `SessionData` replace `rawData`, or run alongside it?**

My recommendation: **push `SessionData`, drop `rawData`** — but keep the field wire-compatible for one transition period.
- `rawData` had one job (be the raw resume source); `SessionData` supersedes it for that, and it was never used server-side for anything else you'd lose.
- Payload shrinks (no double-shipping the transcript).
- **Back-catalog caveat worth naming:** sessions synced *before* this change have no `SessionData` in the cloud. Options: (i) accept that only sessions synced by a new-enough CLI are cloud-resumable, and everything gets `SessionData` naturally as it re-syncs; or (ii) a one-time server backfill that derives `SessionData` from the stored `rawData`/`exchanges`. I'd start with (i) — simplest, and the corpus heals itself as people work.

**2. How does the server serve `SessionData` on read?**

My recommendation: **content negotiation on the existing `GET …/{sessionId}`** — `Accept: application/vnd.specstory.session-data+json` (or a simple `?representation=session-data`), returning the stored `SessionData`. Reuses the existing auth, ETag/304, and access-control path rather than standing up a parallel route. A dedicated `/session-data` route is the fallback if content-negotiation gets awkward with the Hono/OpenAPI setup.

Where do you want to land on **replace-vs-alongside** for `rawData`, and are you good with content-negotiation for the read?

Pinned it down. Here's the factual answer:

**`rawData` goes to object storage only — not the DB.**
- On PUT, `rawData` is uploaded to the **Supabase Storage** bucket `sessions` at `{workspace.id}/{session.id}/raw-data.json` (`sessions.ts:122`, via `uploadToStorage` → `.storage.from(bucket)` in `supabase.ts:767`). So it's the Supabase storage layer, **not R2** (Supabase Storage is S3-compatible, but it's not the R2 binding).
- In the DB `sessions` row, only the **byte count** `raw_data_size` is written — `Session.upsert` inserts `markdownContent` + `rawDataSize` but there's **no `rawData` column** (`session.ts:82-110`). `rawData` the payload never touches Postgres.

For contrast, `markdown` is stored **in both** places: the `markdownContent` text column *and* the `markdown.md` storage blob.

So today: `rawData` = one write to Supabase Storage, size-only in the DB, and (as you said) no consumer.

**This directly informs D2 — where should the pushed `SessionData` live?** Three shapes, mirroring what already exists:

1. **Object storage only** (like `rawData` today) — blob `session-data.json`, size in DB. Cheapest; resume does a storage fetch. Not queryable in SQL.
2. **DB column only** (like... well, nothing today does *only* DB for the big payload). Queryable, but bloats rows and the `sessions` table.
3. **Both** (like `markdown`) — `session_data` blob for the fetch + optionally a column/columns for fields we want to query (`provider.id`, `workspaceRoot`, `schemaVersion`).

My lean: **object storage for the `SessionData` JSON blob** (resume fetches it directly, same pattern as the raw blob it replaces), plus **promote a few small fields to DB columns** only if we need them for listing/filtering (e.g. `agent`/`provider` so the resume list can badge and dedup without fetching every blob). Given `metadata.agentName` is already in the DB `metadata` JSONB, we may not even need new columns for v1.

Want `SessionData` to live as an object-storage blob (my rec), and should we simply **repurpose the existing `raw-data.json` write to be `session-data.json`** — i.e. the push swaps `rawData`→`SessionData` and the server swaps the blob it writes?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 15:49:40Z)**_

Good question, and it's the right instinct to force it into the query rather than probe storage per-row. Short answer: **you can't cheaply query blob presence from object storage, so add a column** — and there's already an exact precedent for it.

**Why not "just check the blob":** the blob lives in Supabase Storage (object store), not Postgres. Testing existence means a storage `list`/`head` per session — a per-row round-trip you can't join into a set-based list query or into the `searchSessions` FTS query. That's the thing to avoid.

**The precedent:** the `sessions` table already tracks its storage blobs with **size columns** — `markdown_size` and `raw_data_size` (`schema.ts`). The blob content lives in storage; a column mirrors its size/presence in the DB. `SessionData` should follow the identical pattern.

**Recommendation: add `session_data_size INTEGER` (nullable).**
- Set it in `Session.upsert` whenever the push includes `sessionData` (byte count, same as its siblings).
- **NULL** = legacy row / no blob; **> 0** = resumable.
- Both read paths filter on it:
  - List/browse: `... WHERE session_data_size > 0` (add to `handleListSessions`).
  - FTS: add the same predicate to the `sessions` join in `searchSessions`.
- Doubles as presence *and* size (handy later for the fetch path), and matches convention exactly — nullable also cleanly represents the back-catalog with no migration backfill.

**Alternative considered — a flag in the existing `metadata` JSONB** (`metadata->>'hasSessionData'`): works, no schema change, but JSONB predicates don't index as cleanly, it's a weaker fit for a hot list/search filter, and it breaks from the `*_size` sibling pattern. I'd only reach for it if you're avoiding migrations at all costs.

One reconciliation note: this doesn't contradict **D3's "no DB column."** D3 meant *don't put `SessionData`'s contents in a column / don't index into it*. A size/presence column is metadata *about* the blob (exactly like `raw_data_size`), not the blob itself. Let me tighten D3 and record this as a decision.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 15:54:19Z)**_

Read the actual skip logic — one correction to the mechanism, then your idea works, with a wrinkle.

**The skip is size-based, not eTag-based.** `requiresSync` (`sync.go:460-595`) decides purely on **markdown size**: `needsSync = localMarkdownSize > serverMarkdownSize`. The eTag is only *captured* from the PUT response (`sync.go:848`) and never consulted for the skip decision — so there's no `If-None-Match` in play here. The lever you want is the **size the server reports**, which is exactly your instinct ("return 0"), just via the size headers rather than the eTag.

**Wrinkle: there are *two* skip paths, and both must report 0**, or `specstory sync` won't heal:
- **HEAD path** → `X-Markdown-Size` header (`sync.go:559`)
- **Bulk path** → `GET …/sessions/sizes`, preloaded once for batch sync (`sync.go:476-500`). `specstory sync` uses this, not HEAD.

If we only touch HEAD, `run`/`watch` heals but batch `sync` doesn't. Both need the same rule.

So your mechanism, stated precisely: **when `session_data_size IS NULL`, the server reports markdown size `0` in both `X-Markdown-Size` and the bulk sizes response** → CLI sees `localSize > 0` → re-sends the full payload (now including `sessionData`) → server stores it and sets `session_data_size` → next check reports the real size → no more re-send. One-shot heal per legacy session. That works (markdown is never empty — it's validated `min(1)` — so `local > 0` always holds).

The one thing I'd flag: this **overloads `X-Markdown-Size` to mean "0 = please resend"**, which is a semantic fib a future reader will trip on. Since we're already changing the CLI (to *send* `sessionData`), there's a cleaner variant:

- **Option A (yours):** server lies — reports markdown size `0` when `session_data_size IS NULL`. CLI unchanged. Minimal, but overloads the size field.
- **Option B (explicit):** server exposes `session_data_size` honestly — new `X-Session-Data-Size` header + include it in the bulk sizes response — and the CLI's `requiresSync` re-sends if `markdown newer OR serverSessionDataSize == 0`. Honest semantics, intent visible in code and telemetry; costs one extra clause in `requiresSync` and a slightly richer sizes response shape.

Blast radius of A is small in practice — `X-Markdown-Size` / `sessions/sizes` are sync-optimization endpoints only the CLI consumes (the web app reads `markdownContent` from the DB directly). So A won't break other consumers. But **I lean B**: we're touching both sides regardless, and "0 means resend" is the kind of magic that costs someone an afternoon in a year.

Want A or B? I'll record the self-heal decision either way — let me capture it now with the mechanism marked pending your pick.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 16:02:25Z)**_

Clear answer: **there's no existing blob-retrieval path at all — neither signed URLs nor API streaming.**

What actually exists in `supabase.ts`:
- `uploadToStorage` (write) — and it *does* call `getPublicUrl`, but **both callers discard the returned URL** (`sessions.ts:116,122` just `await` it). So that URL is effectively dead code.
- `deleteFromStorage` (remove).
- **No `downloadFromStorage`, no `createSignedUrl`, no `.download()`** anywhere.

And critically: when the API serves session content on read, it returns `markdownContent` **from the Postgres column**, not from the `markdown.md` blob. So the blobs (`markdown.md`, `raw-data.json`) are **write-only today** — never read back by the server. `rawData` retrieval, specifically, doesn't exist. (Whatever new consumer you mentioned for `rawData` must read it somewhere outside this worker, or is still to be built.)

**So serving-shape is greenfield — no pattern to inherit.** That actually simplifies the call. My recommendation:

**Stream through the API (option a) for v1.** Reasoning:
- Every other client-facing read already flows through the Worker with `Bearer` auth + `Session.validateAccess` + ETag. Streaming the blob reuses that exact path — one new helper (`downloadFromStorage` via Supabase `.download()`) and one new read route/negotiation. No new auth surface.
- Signed URLs would introduce genuinely new machinery (URL minting, expiry, and — since the bucket appears private, which is correct for user data — enabling `createSignedUrl`), plus a second round-trip, all to save Worker egress.
- Resume is low-frequency and interactive (one blob per resume click), so the Worker-egress savings signed URLs buy don't matter yet.

**Signed URLs are the right *later* optimization** if `SessionData` blobs get large or resume volume climbs — client→storage direct, single egress. Worth noting as a future path, not v1.

Want me to record **API streaming for v1 (signed URL as a documented future optimization)** as the decision and close out the Data-flow/server section?

The full data-flow/server contract, D1–D8:

- **D1** `SessionData` = canonical cloud resume representation
- **D2** CLI pushes `SessionData` on sync; server stores & serves it
- **D3** stored as object-storage blob `session-data.json` (no contents column)

- **D7** heal trigger = `session_data_size` / `X-Session-Data-Size` on both sync-skip paths
- **D8** resume fetches the blob by **streaming through the API** (reuses auth/validateAccess/ETag); signed URLs = future optimization

625	// getDeviceID generates a unique device ID based on MAC address
626	func getDeviceID() string {
627		// Return cached value if available
628		if deviceID != "" {
629			return deviceID
630		}
631	
632		// Get all network interfaces
633		interfaces, err := net.Interfaces()
634		if err != nil {
635			slog.Warn("Failed to get network interfaces", "error", err)
636			// Fallback to hostname-based ID
637			hostname, _ := os.Hostname()
638			h := sha256.Sum256([]byte("specstory-" + hostname))
639			deviceID = hex.EncodeToString(h[:])
640			return deviceID
641		}
642	
643		// Find the first non-loopback interface with a MAC address
644		for _, iface := range interfaces {
645			if iface.Flags&net.FlagLoopback == 0 && len(iface.HardwareAddr) > 0 {
646				// Hash the MAC address
647				h := sha256.Sum256(iface.HardwareAddr)
648				deviceID = hex.EncodeToString(h[:])
649				slog.Debug("Generated device ID from interface", "interface", iface.Name)
650				return deviceID
651			}
652		}
653	
654		// Fallback if no suitable interface found
655		hostname, _ := os.Hostname()
656		h := sha256.Sum256([]byte("specstory-fallback-" + hostname))
657		deviceID = hex.EncodeToString(h[:])
658		slog.Debug("Using fallback device ID based on hostname")
659		return deviceID
660	}

=== EntitlementFeatures + Entitlement + GetEntitlement ===
const skillsHTTPTimeout = 30 * time.Second

// Entitlement is the signed-in user's plan and per-feature access, from
// GET /api/v1/billing/entitlement. Skills require plan "pro" (Features.Skills == true).
type Entitlement struct {
	Plan     string              `json:"plan"`
	Features EntitlementFeatures `json:"features"`
}

// EntitlementFeatures mirrors the server's per-feature boolean flags. Only the fields the
// CLI acts on are modeled; unknown features are ignored by the JSON decoder.
type EntitlementFeatures struct {
	Resume        bool `json:"resume"`
	Skills        bool `json:"skills"`
	KnowledgeBase bool `json:"knowledge_base"`
	WorkTracking  bool `json:"work_tracking"`
	Governance    bool `json:"governance"`
}

// SkillRow is one skill across every lifecycle state, mirroring the cloud's unified
// SkillRow (shared/services/lore/skill_row.ts). Two sources union behind one identity

// GetEntitlement fetches the signed-in user's plan + feature flags. Callers use
// Features.Skills to gate the skills command and craft an upgrade message.
func GetEntitlement() (*Entitlement, error) {
	var resp struct {
		Success bool        `json:"success"`
		Data    Entitlement `json:"data"`
		Error   string      `json:"error"`
	}
	if err := skillsAPIRequest(http.MethodGet, "/api/v1/billing/entitlement", nil, &resp); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if !resp.Success {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("entitlement request failed: %s", resp.Error)
	}
	return &resp.Data, nil
}

// ListSkillLibrary returns the unified skill library (review + ready + installed rows).
// Skill content (SkillMd) is included inline on every row, so no follow-up fetch is needed
// to preview or install.
func ListSkillLibrary() ([]SkillRow, error) {
	var resp struct {
		Success bool       `json:"success"`
		Skills  []SkillRow `json:"skills"`
		Error   string     `json:"error"`
=== ensureSkillsAccess gate ===
// ensureSkillsAccess verifies the user is logged in and has the Pro "skills" entitlement.
// It is the single gate for both the TUI and the subcommands. The server also enforces the
// entitlement, so this is a fast, friendly client-side check, not the security boundary.
func ensureSkillsAccess() error {
	if !cloud.IsAuthenticated() {
		return utils.ValidationError{Message: "skills require a SpecStory Cloud login. Run 'specstory login' first."}
	}
	ent, err := cloud.GetEntitlement()
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("checking your plan: %w", err)
	}
	if !ent.Features.Skills {
		plan := ent.Plan
		if plan == "" {
			plan = "free"
		}
		return utils.ValidationError{Message: fmt.Sprintf(
			"skills require a Pro plan (your plan: %s). Upgrade at https://cloud.specstory.com to enable skills.", plan)}
	}
	return nil
}

// ---- non-interactive subcommands (the machine-readable / front-end surface) ----

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 16:32:39Z)**_

Confirmed the key fact: the cloud `searchSessions` API **already supports `deviceId` / `deviceIds` filters** (`types.ts:190-195`, `graphql.ts:73-131`), and `deviceId` is already stored in each session's metadata on push (`sessions.ts:75`). That substantially changes the machine-ID recommendation — most of the plumbing exists. Let me synthesize.

## Machine identity — findings & recommendation

**We already have a machine ID: `metadata.deviceId`.** It's `SHA256(first non-loopback MAC)` (fallback hostname-hash), computed in Go (`getDeviceID`, `sync.go:625`), pushed on every sync, stored in metadata, and **already filterable** in cloud search (singular `deviceId` + array `deviceIds`). So for your four uses, the ID itself needs **no new column** — it exists and is queryable.

What's actually missing:
1. **A human-friendly name.** `deviceId` is a hash. The natural friendly name is `os.Hostname()` — *not* currently pushed. So the real gap is: **add `machineName` (hostname) to the push metadata** (new field in `WriteSessionRequestSchema` + `cleanMetadata` + the CLI). Group/badge by stable `deviceId`, display the latest `machineName`.
2. **"Exclude my machine" for search** (your reason #1): the CLI computes its own `deviceId` and drops matching rows — simplest is client-side; alternatively a server `excludeDeviceId` param. Client-side is trivial and avoids a server change (minor: dropping rows after a `limit` fetch yields slightly fewer).
3. **List/browse machine display + filter**: search already filters by device; need to confirm the `GET …/sessions` list response carries `metadata` (for the badge) and add the same filter there.

**Recommendation: reuse `metadata.deviceId` as the machine ID (no new column); add `machineName`=hostname to the push metadata.** This matches the existing precedent — `agentName` also lives in metadata with an expression index (`idx_sessions_metadata_agent_name`), and agent filtering already works that way. A dedicated `session_data_machine_id` column is available if you want the explicitness, but it'd duplicate data that's already in metadata and already filterable, so I'd skip it.

**One caveat to flag:** the MAC-based `deviceId` isn't perfectly stable (VPNs / virtual adapters / interface-ordering can change which NIC is "first"), so a machine can occasionally flip identity and appear as two. Since `deviceId` is already shipping and changing the scheme would orphan every already-synced session's ID, I'd **keep it for v1** and treat a persisted-UUID machine ID as a future hardening step if fragmentation actually bites.

## Pro gating — findings & recommendation

The `skills-interface` pattern is clean and **the `Resume` entitlement flag already exists**:
- `cloud.GetEntitlement()` → `GET /api/v1/billing/entitlement` → `Entitlement{Plan, Features{Resume, Skills, KnowledgeBase, …}}` (`skills.go:29-41`).
- `skills` hard-gates via `ensureSkillsAccess()`: `IsAuthenticated()` then `ent.Features.Skills` (`skills.go:88`). Server also enforces — client check is "fast, friendly," not the security boundary.

For cloud-resume, reuse that but as a **soft** gate (local resume/search always works for everyone; cloud is layered in only when eligible):
- **Eligible** = `IsAuthenticated()` **and** `GetEntitlement().Features.Resume` → include cloud sessions.
- **Not logged in** → local-only + nudge: *"Log into SpecStory Cloud to search & resume sessions from your other machines."*
- **Logged in, not Pro** (`!Features.Resume`) → local-only + nudge: *"Upgrade to Pro to search & resume sessions from your other machines."*
- **Push stays unconditional** (D2) — non-Pro users still push `SessionData`, so upgrading retroactively unlocks their existing cloud history. 
- Entitlement is a network call → fetch **async/cached** so the TUI stays local-first/instant (ties to Q-UX5).
- **Dependency:** the entitlement client (`skills.go`) lives on the `skills-interface` branch; cloud-resume needs it merged or the `GetEntitlement`/`Entitlement` bits shared.

Let me record this in the doc, then I have three small forks to confirm.

55		// Splitting on '"' yields alternating runs: even indexes are outside quotes, odd indexes

64					if toks := fieldTokens(f); len(toks) > 0 {

67				}
68			case i == len(segs)-1: // open phrase (still typing): adjacency across all tokens + prefix last

70					parts = append(parts, strings.Join(toks, " + ")+"*")

72			default: // closed phrase: exact adjacency, no prefix (a committed phrase)
73				if toks := segmentTokens(seg); len(toks) > 0 {
74					parts = append(parts, `"`+strings.Join(toks, " ")+`"`)
75				}
76			}
77		}
78		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
79	}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 22:49:39Z)**_

Good thing I checked — the cloud operator handling is actually murky (the function is named `applyImplicitOr`, its comment says "implicit AND", and it inserts `|`, which then goes through `websearch_to_tsquery` that doesn't treat `|` as an operator). So I won't over-claim on AND-vs-OR. But the semantics are **far apart** on three things that *are* certain and material:

## (1) Query-semantics differences

| Dimension | Local (SQLite FTS5) | Cloud (`websearch_to_tsquery('english', …)`) |
|---|---|---|
| **Tokenizer/config** | `unicode61` — **literal**, no stemming | `english` — **Porter stemming** (`running`≈`run`, `files`≈`file`) |
| **Stopwords** | kept (you can search `you`, `the`) | **removed** — `you`/`the`/`to` match nothing |
| **Prefix / type-ahead** | last token gets `*` → live results while typing (`ftsQuery`) | `websearch_to_tsquery` emits **no prefix terms** — no type-ahead |
| **Operators** | deterministic implicit-AND of prefix terms | `websearch_to_tsquery` parsing of a `\|`-joined string — **ambiguous** (naming/comment/impl disagree) |

Stemming + stopwords + no-prefix alone make the two feel like different searches on the same query — exactly the incoherence to avoid. **Verdict: far apart → your second option (an aligned cloud search path).**

**To match local semantics on Postgres**, the aligned path needs:
- A **`simple`-config** tsvector (no stemming, no stopwords → mirrors `unicode61`): a new generated column `fts_simple = to_tsvector('simple', content)` + GIN index on `exchanges` (a migration + backfill — the one real cost).
- A server-side query builder that mirrors `ftsQuery`: implicit **AND**, phrase adjacency (`<->`), last-token **prefix** (`:*`), via `to_tsquery('simple', …)` — *not* `websearch_to_tsquery`.

This can be a **new endpoint or a `mode`/`config` param** on `searchSessions` — keeping it separate avoids regressing the web app's existing `english` search.

*Cheaper compromise if you want to weigh it:* reuse the existing `english` FTS, just fix operators to AND and add prefix — no new column/backfill — but cloud still stems and drops stopwords, so results diverge from local in those cases. I lean **faithful (`simple` column)** since consistency is the whole point, but the backfill on `exchanges` is the tradeoff.

## (2) Snippets from Postgres — yes

Postgres `ts_headline()` is the direct analog of SQLite's `snippet()`. Local uses `snippet(sessions_fts, 3, char(2), char(3), '…', 12)` — wrapping matches in **STX (0x02) / ETX (0x03)** control chars. We set `ts_headline`'s `StartSel`/`StopSel` to those **same** delimiters:

```
ts_headline('simple', content, <same tsquery>,
            'StartSel=<0x02>, StopSel=<0x03>, MaxWords=…, MinWords=…')
```

→ cloud returns snippets in the identical format the TUI already renders, so local and cloud rows highlight the same way with no client-side special-casing. Return it as a field on each search hit. Two notes: `ts_headline` re-parses each matched document so apply it only to returned rows (cheap at TUI page sizes); and local snippets come from the whole-session flattened `body` while cloud's come from the matched **exchange** — slightly different excerpt granularity, but both are "highlighted text around the match," which is what shows.
