_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 22:54:12Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 22:54:31Z)**_

Yes — this is a legitimate third option, and SQLite **can** largely align to the cloud's `english` semantics. The key is that FTS5 has a built-in **`porter` stemming tokenizer**. Here's the shape and the honest limits.

## What "align local → cloud" looks like

**1. Stemming — fully doable.** Change the FTS table to stem:
```sql
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE sessions_fts USING fts5(
    session_id UNINDEXED, agent UNINDEXED, name, body,
    tokenize = 'porter unicode61'
);
```
FTS5's `porter` tokenizer wraps `unicode61` and applies Porter stemming to tokens **at both index and query time**, automatically and symmetrically — type `running`, it stems to `run` on the way in *and* in the MATCH, so `ftsQuery` doesn't stem anything itself. This is entirely within the existing machinery: bump `reindexVersion`, and the next `reindex` rebuilds `sessions_fts` stemmed (fingerprint invalidation already forces the re-parse).

Caveat: Postgres `english` uses the **Snowball** English stemmer (≈"Porter2"); SQLite's is classic **Porter**. Very close, occasional word-level differences — not byte-identical, but the same character.

**2. Stopwords — only approximable.** FTS5 has **no** stopword feature. To mirror cloud dropping `the`/`you`/`to`, you'd **strip English stopwords from the query** in `ftsQuery` (ship Postgres's ~127-word `english.stop` list in the CLI). Indexed docs still contain them, but queries won't search them → effectively similar. Rough edges in phrases that contain stopwords.

**3. Prefix / type-ahead — this is the casualty.** Cloud (`websearch_to_tsquery`) does no prefix, so aligning to it means **dropping the last-token `*`** in `ftsQuery` — i.e. **giving up live type-ahead** in local search. (Prefix + stemming also interact badly — stemming a half-typed word doesn't reliably match the full stem — so you can't cleanly keep both anyway.)

**4. Operators** — adjust `ftsQuery` to mirror websearch (implicit AND, quoted phrases, `-` NOT). Alignable.

## The tradeoff vs. the other direction

The appeal is real: if local matches `english`+websearch, **you reuse the existing cloud `searchSessions` as-is** — **no Postgres migration, no `simple` column/backfill, no new endpoint.** All the work collapses to the CLI (swap tokenizer + reindex + tweak `ftsQuery`). D18 and the faithful `simple`-column work disappear.

The cost is the mirror image:

| | Align **cloud → local** (D18 faithful) | Align **local → cloud** (this option) |
|---|---|---|
| Server work | new `simple` FTS column + GIN + **backfill on `exchanges`**, aligned query path | **none** — reuse existing `searchSessions` |
| CLI work | call the new path | swap tokenizer, **reindex**, rewrite `ftsQuery` |
| Prefix / type-ahead | **kept** (add `:*` to cloud) | **lost** for all local search |
| Stopwords | kept (literal) | approximated (query-side strip) |
| Who's affected | cloud users | **every** local-search user, incl. offline/non-Pro |

**My lean: don't align local → cloud.** The dealbreaker is #3 — it degrades local live type-ahead for *everyone*, including users who never touch cloud, purely to match a cloud limitation. You'd be making the free/offline feature worse to serve the Pro/cloud one. Aligning cloud→local keeps the better UX on both sides; its only real cost is the `exchanges` backfill.

That said, if you consider live prefix expendable, this option is meaningfully less total work and touches no server infra — so it comes down to how much you value type-ahead in local search.

Want me to add this as the third alternative under Q-UX3 (it reframes the open question as "which direction to align"), and note the lean?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-01 23:00:15Z)**_

That closes the loop — and confirms your insight is right. The exchange-parser upserts content on **every** re-sync via `onConflictDoUpdate` on `(sessionId, orderNumber)` (`exchange_parser_worker.ts:156-169`), and because `fts` is `GENERATED … AS to_tsvector(…, content)`, updating `content` **auto-recomputes** the tsvector. So the parse re-runs and the FTS recomputes on exactly the re-syncs that grant a session its `SessionData`.

**So: no backfill needed — you're right — with one design constraint.** The catch is that the *existing* `fts` is `GENERATED … STORED`, and adding a *second* generated-stored column (`to_tsvector('simple', content)`) would force a one-time full-table **rewrite on `ALTER`** — which *is* the backfill, computed for every legacy row you'll never search. So we must **not** make the `simple` FTS a generated-stored column. Instead:

- Add `fts_simple tsvector` as a **plain nullable column** → instant `ALTER`, no rewrite.
- Populate it **on the write path** — either a `BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE` trigger (`NEW.fts_simple := to_tsvector('simple', NEW.content)`) or in `storeExchanges` — so it fills in whenever `content` is (re)written, i.e. on re-sync.
- GIN-index it → **cheap to build** because it's all-`NULL` initially (GIN doesn't index NULLs); rows enter the index as they populate.

Because re-sync is exactly what grants `SessionData`, `fts_simple` lands for precisely the searchable set. Legacy, un-re-synced sessions stay `NULL` — and are already excluded by the `session_data_size > 0` filter (D5), and wouldn't match `fts_simple @@ query` anyway. **Double-safe, zero backfill.** The only cost moves from a big one-time table rewrite to a trivial per-session recompute that's already happening on re-sync.

Here's the phasing I'd recommend. It follows the dependency graph, and each phase is independently shippable and delivers value on its own.

## Phase 1 — Seed & self-heal (plumbing, no UX)

**Goal:** get `SessionData` flowing into the cloud and start healing the back-catalog. Ships silently — no user-facing change — but every later phase depends on it, and the corpus needs time to accumulate as people re-sync, so this goes first.

- **CLI push:** add `sessionData` + `metadata.machineName` to `APIRequest` (D2, D9). `rawData` untouched (D4).
- **Server storage:** write `session-data.json` blob (D3), add `sessions.session_data_size` column + set it in `Session.upsert` (D5), persist `machineName` in metadata (D9).
- **Self-heal:** `X-Session-Data-Size` on HEAD + the bulk `sessions/sizes` response (D7); extend CLI `requiresSync` to re-send when `serverSessionDataSize == 0` (D6/D7).

**Why first / why coherent:** entirely additive, no gating dependency (push is unconditional), no TUI work. The moment it ships, new sessions carry `SessionData` and old ones heal as they're touched — so Phases 2–3 launch onto a populated corpus instead of an empty one.

## Phase 2 — Cloud resume (browse)

**Goal:** the first cross-machine feature — resume a session from another machine via the blended browser.

- **Server:** stream-`SessionData` read endpoint (D8); list sessions filtered `session_data_size > 0` + return `metadata` + `limit 500` (D5/D9/D21); reuse `GET /api/v1/projects` for blended projects (D16).
- **CLI cloud client:** list sessions, list projects, fetch `SessionData`, `GetEntitlement` (D10 — pulls in the `skills-interface` entitlement dependency).
- **CLI TUI (browse):** async local-first + "searching cloud…" indicator (D11); unified list + dedup, local-preferred (D13); cloud icon (D14); machine filter `m` (D15); blended project list + cloud-only icon (D16); Pro soft-gate + nudges (D10).
- **Resume:** fetch `SessionData` → existing reconstruct path (D12).

**Why here:** depends only on Phase 1's blobs. Establishes all the shared TUI plumbing — async layering, dedup, machine filter, gating — that Phase 3 reuses. Resume-first also matches the entitlement flag name (`Features.Resume`) and needs no new FTS infra.

## Phase 3 — Cloud search

**Goal:** cross-machine full-text search, semantically consistent with local.

- **Server:** `exchanges.fts_simple` column + trigger + GIN (D20); aligned search endpoint — `simple` `to_tsquery` builder mirroring `ftsQuery` (D18); `ts_headline` snippets delimiter-matched to local (D19); recency sort + `limit 500` (D17/D21).
- **CLI:** call cloud search, merge into the search TUI, render snippets uniformly — reusing Phase 2's dedup, machine filter, gating, and async layering.

**Why last:** the FTS work is the most novel/isolated, and it sits cleanly on Phase 2's TUI. `fts_simple` heals via the same re-sync as Phase 1, so by the time this ships the search corpus is populated.

---

**Shape:** 1 → 2 → 3, each spanning CLI + server, each shippable. Phase 1 is the keystone (ship ASAP for corpus build-up + de-risk); Phase 2 builds the reusable TUI; Phase 3 layers search on top.

Want me to write this into the doc as **§4 — Work plan / phasing**? And does the resume-before-search ordering match your instinct, or would you flip them?

20:- **D5 — A `session_data_size INTEGER` (nullable) column on `sessions` tracks blob presence** (byte count, set in `Session.upsert` when the push carries `sessionData`), mirroring the existing `markdown_size` / `raw_data_size` columns. `NULL` = legacy/no blob; `> 0` = cloud-resumable. Both read paths filter on it so browse/search only surface resumable cloud sessions — but the filter is **opt-in, not unconditional**: the list endpoint (`GET …/{projectId}/sessions`) is shared with the web app, and a blanket `WHERE session_data_size > 0` would hide every legacy session from cloud.specstory.com until re-synced (regressing a surface this feature doesn't own, contrary to §3's additive promise). So the CLI passes a new **`?resumable=true`** query param, which adds `WHERE session_data_size > 0`; without the param the endpoint behaves exactly as today. The aligned FTS search (D18) applies the same predicate on the `sessions` row unconditionally — it's a new resume-only surface, so no opt-in is needed there. Nullable represents the back-catalog with no backfill. This is metadata *about* the blob — consistent with D3, not a contents column.
34:- **D20 — The `simple` FTS needs no backfill; it populates lazily on the same re-sync that grants `SessionData`.** `fts_simple` is added as a **plain nullable `tsvector` column** on `exchanges` (instant `ALTER`, no table rewrite) — **not** a `GENERATED … STORED` column, which would rewrite every legacy row on `ALTER`. It's populated on the write path (a `BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE` trigger `to_tsvector('simple', content)`, or in `storeExchanges`), so it fills in whenever `content` is (re)written — which the exchange-parser does on every re-sync via `onConflictDoUpdate` on `(sessionId, orderNumber)` (`exchange_parser_worker.ts:156-169`). Since re-sync is exactly what grants `SessionData` (D6/D7), `fts_simple` lands for precisely the searchable set. Legacy un-re-synced rows stay `NULL` — excluded by the `session_data_size > 0` filter (D5) and inert against `fts_simple @@ query` anyway. The GIN index on `fts_simple` builds cheaply (all-`NULL` initially; GIN skips NULLs). Net: a big one-time table rewrite becomes a trivial per-session recompute already happening on re-sync.
253:- **List (`GET …/{projectId}/sessions`)** — new opt-in **`?resumable=true`** param → filter `WHERE session_data_size > 0` (omitted = today's behavior, so the web app is untouched); return `metadata` (for the machine badge/filter); `limit = 500` (D5/D9/D21).
